source: ས་མཚམས།གསུམ་པ་ནི། ས་དང་པོ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་ན་ཡོད། དེའང་འབྲས་བུ་མཐོང་ན་དེ་དོན་གཉེར་སྐྱེ་བས་མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་མཇུག་ཐོགས་སུ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མ་བརྗོད་པར་དེའི་བྱེད་པ་གསུངས་པ་ནི། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཆིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གིས་བསྟན། དོན་ནི། སྒོམ་པའི་ལམ་གྱི་རང་བཞིན་གྱི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་གང་ལ་འགྲོ་བའི་མགོན་པོ་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་དང་། རྒྱལ་སྲས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་མཉམ་རྗེས་ཀྱི་གནས་སྐབས་ཀུན་ཏུ་སྤྱོད་ཅིང་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པ་ཡི་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་འདི་ནི་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུའམ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་མོ་གང་ཞིག་གིས་དད་ཅིང་གུས་པར་བྱས་ཏེ་གཞུང་བློ་ལ་འཛིན་པ་དང༌། ཐོས་བསམ་བསྒོམ་པའི་རང་བཞིན་གྱི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་དོན་ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་དེ་ལ་ཕྱིའི་དུག་དང་མཚོན་དང་མེ་དང་ཆུས་གནོད་པས་མི་ཚུགས་ཤིང༌། དེ་ཙམ་དུ་མ་ཟད་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པ་དུག་ལྟ་བུ་དང་། མཚོན་ལྟ་བུའོ་ཞེ་སྡང་དང་། མེ་དང་འདྲ་བའི་འདོད་ཆགས་དང་། ཆུ་དང་འདྲ་བའི་གཏི་མུག་སོགས་ཉོན་མོངས་པས་ཀྱང་མི་ཚུགས་སོ། །ལམ་གྱི་བར་ཆད་བྱེད་པའི་དགའ་རབ་དབང་ཕྱུགས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་བདུད་དང༌། བདུད་ཀྱི་སྡེའམ་བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་གྱུར་པའི་ནག་པོའི་རྩ་ལག་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་གླགས་བཙལ་ཀྱང་གླགས་རྙེད་པར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ་ཆོས་ཉིད་སྟོབས་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་སེམས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་བུ་སྡུག་དང་འདྲ་བར་དགོས་ཤིང་རྟག་ཏུ་སྲུང་སྐྱོབས་སྦ་བར་མཛད་པས་སོ། །འདིར་གུས་བྱས་ཞེས་པས་ཀུན་ལ་འདུད་པའི་བྱེད་པ་བསྟན་པ་ཡིན་ལ། བརྒྱད་སྟོང་པ་ལས། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས་ཡོངས་སུ་དུལ་བ་དང་། ཁེངས་པ་མཆིས་པར་བགྱི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཀྱིས་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་བྱེད་པ་བསྟན་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
translation: Boundaries. Third, it exists from the first ground up to the Buddha ground. Moreover, because seeing the result gives rise to seeking it, the function [of the path of meditation] is explained immediately after the path of seeing, without [first] explaining the path of meditation itself: this is taught by the single stanza beginning, "The perfection of wisdom." The meaning is: Whatever son or daughter of good family has faith and respect for this perfection of wisdom—which is the nature of the path of meditation, and in which the protectors of beings, the completely perfect Buddha Bhagavāns, and all the Bodhisattva heirs of the Victors engage and abide during all occasions of meditative equipoise and subsequent attainment—memorizes its text, and comprehends all its meanings through the wisdom that is the nature of hearing, reflecting, and meditating, they cannot be harmed by outer poisons, weapons, fire, and water. Not only that, but they cannot be harmed by afflictions such as the poison-like manifest clinging to true existence, the weapon-like hatred, the fire-like attachment, and the water-like ignorance. Even if māras such as Kāmadeva who cause obstacles to the path, and the hosts of māras or the dark relatives allied with the māras seek an opportunity, they will not find an opportunity, because of the power of dharmatā, and because the Buddhas and bodhisattvas hold them dear like a beloved child and always protect, shelter, and conceal them. Here, by saying "has respect," the function of bowing to all is taught, and it is stated in the Eight Thousand Stanza Perfection of Wisdom: "Bodhisattva great beings are completely tamed and their arrogance is eliminated," and so forth, teaching the function of the path of meditation.

Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. To teach by way of an example that meditating on the path of seeing will attain the prophecy by the Tathāgata: The Victorious One, the Lion of the Śākyas himself, who was victorious over the enemies of the four māras, spoke thus: "At whatever time I, the Teacher Śākyamuni, came to speak in accordance with this supreme perfection of wisdom which is the essence of the path of seeing, at that time the former supreme being Dīpaṃkara prophesied me, saying, 'You, brahmin boy, will become a Buddha in future times.'" [3-91] translation already produced for this document:
Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. Therefore, directly realizing this meaning of not being born by nature is engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which has become the essence of the path of seeing.

[3-92] translation already produced for this document:
To teach by way of an example that meditating on the path of seeing will attain the prophecy by the Tathāgata: The Victorious One, the Lion of the Śākyas himself, who was victorious over the enemies of the four māras, spoke thus: "At whatever time I, the Teacher Śākyamuni, came to speak in accordance with this supreme perfection of wisdom which is the essence of the path of seeing, at that time the former supreme being Dīpaṃkara prophesied me, saying, 'You, brahmin boy, will become a Buddha in future times.'" Therefore, having understood that it is implicitly taught that the trainees of future generations will also abide in this perfection of wisdom, be prophesied by Buddhas, and become completely and perfectly awakened, one should rely on exertion in practicing the Mahayana path like the continuous flow of a river. This completes the commentary on the second chapter, the chapter of Śakra, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, Clarifying the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, the Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate.

Second, if that is divided, there are six: the function of having mastered the mind and completely pacifying pride and so forth; the function of apprehending all sentient beings as spiritual friends and respecting and bowing to them; the function of being victorious over afflictions such as the three poisons; the function of not being subdued by the harm of humans and non-humans; the function of accomplishing perfectly complete awakening; and the function of the place where the support, the bodhisattva on the path of meditation, resides also becoming an object of homage and worship by all beings.

translation: Divisions. Second, if that is divided, there are two: the conceptual contaminated path of meditation and the non-conceptual uncontaminated path of meditation.

Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. Therefore, directly realizing this meaning of not being born by nature is engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which has become the essence of the path of seeing.

To teach by way of an example that meditating on the path of seeing will attain the prophecy by the Tathāgata: The Victorious One, the Lion of the Śākyas himself, who was victorious over the enemies of the four māras, spoke thus: "At whatever time I, the Teacher Śākyamuni, came to speak in accordance with this supreme perfection of wisdom which is the essence of the path of seeing, at that time the former supreme being Dīpaṃkara prophesied me, saying, 'You, brahmin boy, will become a Buddha in future times.'" Therefore, having understood that it is implicitly taught that the trainees of future generations will also abide in this perfection of wisdom, be prophesied by Buddhas, and become completely and perfectly awakened, one should rely on exertion in practicing the Mahayana path like the continuous flow of a river. Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. Therefore, directly realizing this meaning of not being born by nature is engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which has become the essence of the path of seeing.

To teach by way of an example that meditating on the path of seeing will attain the prophecy by the Tathāgata: The Victorious One, the Lion of the Śākyas himself, who was victorious over the enemies of the four māras, spoke thus: "At whatever time I, the Teacher Śākyamuni, came to speak in accordance with this supreme perfection of wisdom which is the essence of the path of seeing, at that time the former supreme being Dīpaṃkara prophesied me, saying, 'You, brahmin boy, will become a Buddha in future times.'" Therefore, having understood that it is implicitly taught that the trainees of future generations will also abide in this perfection of wisdom, be prophesied by Buddhas, and become completely and perfectly awakened, one should rely on exertion in practicing the Mahayana path like the continuous flow of a river. This completes the commentary on the second chapter, the chapter of Śakra, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, Clarifying the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, the Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate.

heading: **དབྱེ་བ།**
translation: Divisions. If divided, there are three: the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of others, and the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of both. Because each of those has three—small, middling, and great—there are nine, and because each of those is also divided into three—the small of the small and so forth—there are twenty-seven.

[3-91] translation already produced for this document:
Therefore, those bodhisattvas on the path of seeing who attain such a view devoid of all discriminative awarenesses that grasp at true existence abide in the word of the Teacher that teaches prophecies by Buddhas saying, "In this life they are irreversible and remember their future births, and having gone to the perfection of the grounds and paths, they will become perfectly awakened as a Buddha named such-and-such," and so forth. If one says, "Because meditating on the path and so forth exist, establishment by nature exists": Even if the Sugata, the Teacher who has become a valid cognition, were to reside for eons equal to the sand grains of the river Ganges and fully proclaim the sound, "Sentient beings exist," how could sentient beings ultimately exist or be born by nature? They would not, because from the very beginning they are unborn by nature and completely pure without defilements entering their nature. Therefore, directly realizing this meaning of not being born by nature is engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which has become the essence of the path of seeing.

To teach by way of an example that meditating on the path of seeing will attain the prophecy by the Tathāgata: The Victorious One, the Lion of the Śākyas himself, who was victorious over the enemies of the four māras, spoke thus: "At whatever time I, the Teacher Śākyamuni, came to speak in accordance with this supreme perfection of wisdom which is the essence of the path of seeing, at that time the former supreme being Dīpaṃkara prophesied me, saying, 'You, brahmin boy, will become a Buddha in future times.'" Therefore, having understood that it is implicitly taught that the trainees of future generations will also abide in this perfection of wisdom, be prophesied by Buddhas, and become completely and perfectly awakened, one should rely on exertion in practicing the Mahayana path like the continuous flow of a river. This completes the commentary on the second chapter, the chapter of Śakra, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, Clarifying the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, the Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate.

heading: **ས་མཚམས།**
translation: Boundaries. The boundaries are from the first to the tenth ground. As for the explanation of three—the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, for the sake of both, and for the sake of others—although there is no difference in acting for the sake of others by way of intention, they are divided into three from the perspective of how they are practiced in application.

heading: **རང་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake. To teach the first of those, the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, it is taught with three verses starting with "If some... the Sugata...". The meaning is that these paths of meditation are taught by way of their benefits, and that too is just as it is stated in the Suvarṇaprabhāsa: "The Buddha never passes into nirvana; / The Dharma too will not decline..." and so forth, and "If there is no bone or blood in the body, / How could there be relics?" and so forth. In the definitive meaning, the Buddha does not pass into nirvana and the true Dharma does not decline; until samsara is emptied, the enlightened activities of body, speech, and mind arise continuously, effortlessly, and spontaneously. And although there are no relics or the like in the body of wisdom, one should understand how, because of skill in means for taming disciples and the inconceivable power of aspiration, he emanates inconceivable arrays of marvelous emanations pervading space, such as demonstrating the manner of passing into nirvana in accordance with the devoted perspective of the disciples and leaving relics in the world. Therefore, if "some" make a reliquary stupa that has the essence of the relics of the completely nirvana-ed "Sugata," the materials of that stupa also being made of the seven precious things—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, emerald, red pearl, and heart of stone—and makes offerings to it; and furthermore, if it is not just one, but one were to make such stupas of the Sugata equal in number to the grains of sand of the "Ganges river," filling countless and boundless buddha fields—thousands of tens of millions and so forth—without exception; taking this as a complete hypothesis—that is, making an example in the manner of taking an extreme hypothesis—if all those sentient beings of however many types reside in those many boundless tens of millions of fields, doing nothing else at all such as commerce or agriculture, were to make offerings without interruption three times "each day and night" with particularly exalted offering substances—"divine flowers and exceedingly fragrant incense and marvelous ointments"—and if they were to make offerings in such a manner for an "eon" or more than an eon, there would certainly be immeasurable merit in that. Yet, compared to that, "if any being," generating devoted interest for the sake of their own excellent benefit, were to write this text of the "perfection of wisdom"—the Mother of the Sugatas which teaches completely both means and wisdom, from which cause the exalted qualities such as the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of the Guides, the Lords of Victors, will "arise"—in a volume and "hold it" in their hands, and make offerings to it with flowers and ointments and pay respect for just a short time, that previous merit of making such reliquary stupas of the Sugata and making offerings to them "would not rival even a fraction" or a number such as a hundred thousand ten million billionths of that latter merit of having written this sutra of the perfection of wisdom in a volume and made offerings to it.

heading: **གཉིས་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of both. To teach the second, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of both, it is taught with four verses starting with "The Victors' wisdom...". The meaning is: This perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Victors, is a "great knowledge mantra" or "an unsurpassable knowledge mantra" because it pacifies the afflictions in the mindstreams of all, oneself and others. Furthermore, in general, a "knowledge mantra" refers to something like that which is able to pacify harms from humans and non-humans and so forth merely by rishis who have accomplished truthful speech reciting, "May it be pacified!", and although there are also ordinary ones, this perfection of wisdom is, as already explained, a great and unsurpassable knowledge mantra, and because in dependence upon it one becomes equal to the unequaled Buddhas, or because one will attain buddhahood, it is stated to be the "mantra equal to the unequaled". This is because it pacifies all that belongs to the phenomena of physical suffering such as sickness and mental sorrow such as separation from the pleasant for an "immeasurable" multitude of realms of "sentient beings", and causes them to attain buddhahood. "Whichever Buddhas have passed in the past and whichever" presently live and remain "as protectors of the worlds in the ten directions," they too having trained in this knowledge mantra equal to the unequaled have "become unsurpassable kings of physicians" who dispel the sins, obscurations, sufferings, sicknesses, and so forth of all sentient beings.

[3-105] translation already produced for this document:
Path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake. To teach the first of those, the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, it is taught with three verses starting with "If some... the Sugata...". The meaning is that these paths of meditation are taught by way of their benefits, and that too is just as it is stated in the Suvarṇaprabhāsa: "The Buddha never passes into nirvana; / The Dharma too will not decline..." and so forth, and "If there is no bone or blood in the body, / How could there be relics?" and so forth. In the definitive meaning, the Buddha does not pass into nirvana and the true Dharma does not decline; until samsara is emptied, the enlightened activities of body, speech, and mind arise continuously, effortlessly, and spontaneously. And although there are no relics or the like in the body of wisdom, one should understand how, because of skill in means for taming disciples and the inconceivable power of aspiration, he emanates inconceivable arrays of marvelous emanations pervading space, such as demonstrating the manner of passing into nirvana in accordance with the devoted perspective of the disciples and leaving relics in the world. Therefore, if "some" make a reliquary stupa that has the essence of the relics of the completely nirvana-ed "Sugata," the materials of that stupa also being made of the seven precious things—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, emerald, red pearl, and heart of stone—and makes offerings to it; and furthermore, if it is not just one, but one were to make such stupas of the Sugata equal in number to the grains of sand of the "Ganges river," filling countless and boundless buddha fields—thousands of tens of millions and so forth—without exception; taking this as a complete hypothesis—that is, making an example in the manner of taking an extreme hypothesis—if all those sentient beings of however many types reside in those many boundless tens of millions of fields, doing nothing else at all such as commerce or agriculture, were to make offerings without interruption three times "each day and night" with particularly exalted offering substances—"divine flowers and exceedingly fragrant incense and marvelous ointments"—and if they were to make offerings in such a manner for an "eon" or more than an eon, there would certainly be immeasurable merit in that. Yet, compared to that, "if any being," generating devoted interest for the sake of their own excellent benefit, were to write this text of the "perfection of wisdom"—the Mother of the Sugatas which teaches completely both means and wisdom, from which cause the exalted qualities such as the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of the Guides, the Lords of Victors, will "arise"—in a volume and "hold it" in their hands, and make offerings to it with flowers and ointments and pay respect for just a short time, that previous merit of making such reliquary stupas of the Sugata and making offerings to them "would not rival even a fraction" or a number such as a hundred thousand ten million billionths of that latter merit of having written this sutra of the perfection of wisdom in a volume and made offerings to it.

heading: **གཉིས་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: If that is how the Tathagatas are generated, how do bodhisattvas accomplish benefit? "Whichever bodhisattvas" actually accomplish benefit and happiness by applying themselves to sentient beings and "practice" the conduct of the victors' children, such as giving, "with a mind of compassion," all of them having trained in this great knowledge mantra, the perfection of wisdom, all those "wise ones" will in future times "touch," that is, awaken to, "supreme, unsurpassable awakening". Whichever contaminated happiness is conditioned and included in samsara, and whichever unconditioned, undefiled happiness there is in the mindstreams of the noble ones who have attained liberation having abandoned afflictions—one should know that "all" those happinesses of samsara and nirvana "arise from this" perfection of wisdom.

[3-105] translation already produced for this document:
Path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake. To teach the first of those, the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, it is taught with three verses starting with "If some... the Sugata...". The meaning is that these paths of meditation are taught by way of their benefits, and that too is just as it is stated in the Suvarṇaprabhāsa: "The Buddha never passes into nirvana; / The Dharma too will not decline..." and so forth, and "If there is no bone or blood in the body, / How could there be relics?" and so forth. In the definitive meaning, the Buddha does not pass into nirvana and the true Dharma does not decline; until samsara is emptied, the enlightened activities of body, speech, and mind arise continuously, effortlessly, and spontaneously. And although there are no relics or the like in the body of wisdom, one should understand how, because of skill in means for taming disciples and the inconceivable power of aspiration, he emanates inconceivable arrays of marvelous emanations pervading space, such as demonstrating the manner of passing into nirvana in accordance with the devoted perspective of the disciples and leaving relics in the world. Therefore, if "some" make a reliquary stupa that has the essence of the relics of the completely nirvana-ed "Sugata," the materials of that stupa also being made of the seven precious things—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, emerald, red pearl, and heart of stone—and makes offerings to it; and furthermore, if it is not just one, but one were to make such stupas of the Sugata equal in number to the grains of sand of the "Ganges river," filling countless and boundless buddha fields—thousands of tens of millions and so forth—without exception; taking this as a complete hypothesis—that is, making an example in the manner of taking an extreme hypothesis—if all those sentient beings of however many types reside in those many boundless tens of millions of fields, doing nothing else at all such as commerce or agriculture, were to make offerings without interruption three times "each day and night" with particularly exalted offering substances—"divine flowers and exceedingly fragrant incense and marvelous ointments"—and if they were to make offerings in such a manner for an "eon" or more than an eon, there would certainly be immeasurable merit in that. Yet, compared to that, "if any being," generating devoted interest for the sake of their own excellent benefit, were to write this text of the "perfection of wisdom"—the Mother of the Sugatas which teaches completely both means and wisdom, from which cause the exalted qualities such as the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of the Guides, the Lords of Victors, will "arise"—in a volume and "hold it" in their hands, and make offerings to it with flowers and ointments and pay respect for just a short time, that previous merit of making such reliquary stupas of the Sugata and making offerings to them "would not rival even a fraction" or a number such as a hundred thousand ten million billionths of that latter merit of having written this sutra of the perfection of wisdom in a volume and made offerings to it.

translation: What is the example for its being the basis of all mundane and supramundane qualities? "Just as when seeds" of barley and so forth are planted, they "abide in the earth" without deteriorating and shoots and so forth will arise, and having found their own respective assembly of causes and conditions such as water, fertilizer, warmth, and moisture, "the forms of many aspects" of fruits "will grow," similarly, "however many" immeasurable qualities there are of the paths of the five perfections such as giving and of the result, unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening, "all" of them "arise from this" perfection of wisdom.

Path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake. To teach the first of those, the path of meditation of devoted interest for one's own sake, it is taught with three verses starting with "If some... the Sugata...". The meaning is that these paths of meditation are taught by way of their benefits, and that too is just as it is stated in the Suvarṇaprabhāsa: "The Buddha never passes into nirvana; / The Dharma too will not decline..." and so forth, and "If there is no bone or blood in the body, / How could there be relics?" and so forth. In the definitive meaning, the Buddha does not pass into nirvana and the true Dharma does not decline; until samsara is emptied, the enlightened activities of body, speech, and mind arise continuously, effortlessly, and spontaneously. And although there are no relics or the like in the body of wisdom, one should understand how, because of skill in means for taming disciples and the inconceivable power of aspiration, he emanates inconceivable arrays of marvelous emanations pervading space, such as demonstrating the manner of passing into nirvana in accordance with the devoted perspective of the disciples and leaving relics in the world. Therefore, if "some" make a reliquary stupa that has the essence of the relics of the completely nirvana-ed "Sugata," the materials of that stupa also being made of the seven precious things—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, emerald, red pearl, and heart of stone—and makes offerings to it; and furthermore, if it is not just one, but one were to make such stupas of the Sugata equal in number to the grains of sand of the "Ganges river," filling countless and boundless buddha fields—thousands of tens of millions and so forth—without exception; taking this as a complete hypothesis—that is, making an example in the manner of taking an extreme hypothesis—if all those sentient beings of however many types reside in those many boundless tens of millions of fields, doing nothing else at all such as commerce or agriculture, were to make offerings without interruption three times "each day and night" with particularly exalted offering substances—"divine flowers and exceedingly fragrant incense and marvelous ointments"—and if they were to make offerings in such a manner for an "eon" or more than an eon, there would certainly be immeasurable merit in that. Yet, compared to that, "if any being," generating devoted interest for the sake of their own excellent benefit, were to write this text of the "perfection of wisdom"—the Mother of the Sugatas which teaches completely both means and wisdom, from which cause the exalted qualities such as the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of the Guides, the Lords of Victors, will "arise"—in a volume and "hold it" in their hands, and make offerings to it with flowers and ointments and pay respect for just a short time, that previous merit of making such reliquary stupas of the Sugata and making offerings to them "would not rival even a fraction" or a number such as a hundred thousand ten million billionths of that latter merit of having written this sutra of the perfection of wisdom in a volume and made offerings to it.

heading: **གཉིས་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: This is because if they are thoroughly embraced by the wisdom that realizes the agent, action, and object as lacking true existence, giving and so forth become perfections and cause the ultimate result, the Truth Body and Form Bodies, to be accomplished. "For example, whichever path" a wheel-turning king "always goes on, on that very" path "other kings also go" and pay homage, and the seven precious elements of sovereignty such as the precious wheel, accomplished by the power of his merit, "and all the four branches of his army go" without separation; "similarly," from whichever continuum of a person and whichever state of the grounds and paths "this perfection of wisdom," the Mother of the Victors, is present or "goes, from that very" place "all" the paths included in the collections of merit and wisdom such as love, compassion, and bodhicitta "and all the phenomena of the qualities of the Buddha," the result, "will also go," that is, will be attained, and thus supreme beings seeking unsurpassable awakening should have faith in and aspire to this perfection of wisdom, the Mother. From the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, Clarifying the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, this is the commentary on the third chapter, "Holding the Immeasurable Benefits of the Perfection of Wisdom and Honoring the Stupa."

To teach the second, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of both, it is taught with four verses starting with "The Victors' wisdom...". "Whichever Buddhas have passed in the past and whichever" presently live and remain "as protectors of the worlds in the ten directions," they too having trained in this knowledge mantra equal to the unequaled have "become unsurpassable kings of physicians" who dispel the sins, obscurations, sufferings, sicknesses, and so forth of all sentient beings.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of others. To teach the third, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of others, it is taught with nine verses starting with "The Victor... to Śakra." The meaning is: "The Victor," the Bhagavan who has conquered the four maras, completely put a "question to Śakra," the lord of gods who possesses the splendor of a hundred ordinary gods, having placed all the realms equal to the sands of the Ganges completely filled with the relics of the Victor without intervening space in one portion, and having placed a volume of the perfection of wisdom in the second portion, asking, "Which do you take?" His answer was: "If they were Buddha realms equal to the number of sands of the river Ganges, and all those realms were completely filled and packed with the relics of the Victor" without intervening space, I, the lord of gods, "would take this very" perfection of wisdom written in a volume.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: "For what reason" do you take the volume of the perfection of wisdom? "It is not that I," Śakra, "am lacking in respect" and faith "for the relics"—indeed I am extremely respectful—however, the reason for taking the perfection of wisdom is that because all the paths are thoroughly embraced and permeated by such a perfection of wisdom, in dependence on it "these relics of the Victor too have become worthy of all beings paying homage and making offerings." "Just as those who depend on a king," such as his ministers and so forth, "also obtain reverence and respect from others," the relics of the Buddha, endowed with immeasurable qualities, are accomplished in dependence on this very perfection of wisdom.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: If one thinks, "Well, even if it arose in that way through the power of the perfection of wisdom, since the Buddha has passed into nirvana and is free from acting in that way, the relics are not worthy of offerings," to establish that they are worthy by means of an example: "A precious wish-fulfilling jewel" endowed with all qualities such as granting needs and desires and possessing immeasurable value, "whichever vessel it is kept" or placed "in, such as a casket"—a storage box, amulet box, or so forth—"that vessel is worthy of homage," and "even if" the jewel "is taken out of that vessel," one generates great joy toward "that casket" which previously acted as the vessel in which it was kept, thinking, "Because it is the vessel in which the precious jewel was kept, it is unlike others." "That" the vessel "obtained such qualities is through the power of that precious jewel."

To teach the second, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of both, it is taught with four verses starting with "The Victors' wisdom...". The meaning is: This perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Victors, is a "great knowledge mantra" or "an unsurpassable knowledge mantra" because it pacifies the afflictions in the mindstreams of all, oneself and others. This is because it pacifies all that belongs to the phenomena of physical suffering such as sickness and mental sorrow such as separation from the pleasant for an "immeasurable" multitude of realms of "sentient beings", and causes them to attain buddhahood. "Whichever Buddhas have passed in the past and whichever" presently live and remain "as protectors of the worlds in the ten directions," they too having trained in this knowledge mantra equal to the unequaled have "become unsurpassable kings of physicians" who dispel the sins, obscurations, sufferings, sicknesses, and so forth of all sentient beings.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: If one asks, "Why, since there are other perfections such as giving, is only the perfection of wisdom made the principal and posited in the three devoted interests?", to teach the reason for that, it is stated: Since one must practice giving by means of being thoroughly embraced by the wisdom that realizes the non-apprehension of the three spheres—the substance to be given, the giver, and the recipient of the gift and so forth—the phenomenon that "precedes the perfection of giving is wisdom," and "ethics, patience, diligence, and concentration too" must "similarly" be preceded by wisdom.

"For example, whichever path" a wheel-turning king "always goes on, on that very" path "other kings also go" and pay homage, and the seven precious elements of sovereignty such as the precious wheel, accomplished by the power of his merit, "and all the four branches of his army go" without separation; "similarly," from whichever continuum of a person and whichever state of the grounds and paths "this perfection of wisdom," the Mother of the Victors, is present or "goes, from that very" place "all" the paths included in the collections of merit and wisdom such as love, compassion, and bodhicitta "and all the phenomena of the qualities of the Buddha," the result, "will also go," that is, will be attained, and thus supreme beings seeking unsurpassable awakening should have faith in and aspire to this perfection of wisdom, the Mother. From the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, Clarifying the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, this is the commentary on the third chapter, "Holding the Immeasurable Benefits of the Perfection of Wisdom and Honoring the Stupa."

Path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of others. To teach the third, the path of meditation of devoted interest for the sake of others, it is taught with nine verses starting with "The Victor... to Śakra." The meaning is: "The Victor," the Bhagavan who has conquered the four maras, completely put a "question to Śakra," the lord of gods who possesses the splendor of a hundred ordinary gods, having placed all the realms equal to the sands of the Ganges completely filled with the relics of the Victor without intervening space in one portion, and having placed a volume of the perfection of wisdom in the second portion, asking, "Which do you take?" His answer was: "If they were Buddha realms equal to the number of sands of the river Ganges, and all those realms were completely filled and packed with the relics of the Victor" without intervening space, I, the lord of gods, "would take this very" perfection of wisdom written in a volume.

"For what reason" do you take the volume of the perfection of wisdom? "It is not that I," Śakra, "am lacking in respect" and faith "for the relics"—indeed I am extremely respectful—however, the reason for taking the perfection of wisdom is that because all the paths are thoroughly embraced and permeated by such a perfection of wisdom, in dependence on it "these relics of the Victor too have become worthy of all beings paying homage and making offerings." "Just as those who depend on a king," such as his ministers and so forth, "also obtain reverence and respect from others," the relics of the Buddha, endowed with immeasurable qualities, are accomplished in dependence on this very perfection of wisdom.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Why is that? If all virtuous phenomena such as giving are bound by apprehending signs and stained by the defilement of inferior mental engagement, they will be wasted by falling into samsara or the extreme of peace; so in order that they are not wasted in that way, dedicating them to unsurpassable complete awakening, they are completely embraced on the path by the perfection of wisdom which completely purifies giving and so forth by means of the wisdom that realizes non-apprehension. Thus, this wisdom "shows exactly one method of the path" in which "all" virtuous phenomena such as giving have one taste as the "cause of a Buddha." "For example, in Jambudvīpa there are many thousands of tens of millions of different trees" such as sandalwood and aloeswood, and though they have various colors, shapes, and scents and so forth and "many forms" with many aspects of color and shape of branches, fruits, leaves, and flowers and so forth, except for "their shadows" merely being expressed as synonyms for shadows of trees, the shadows do not have various differing colors and scents and so forth like the trees, and "shadows do not have distinctions" like the individual trees from their own side. "Similarly to that example, these five perfections" of the Victor, "such as giving," too, if embraced by the wisdom that realizes the non-apprehension of the three spheres, "will attain the very name" of perfections, and that they become supramundane perfections is also by the power of this perfection of wisdom.

"For what reason" do you take the volume of the perfection of wisdom? "It is not that I," Śakra, "am lacking in respect" and faith "for the relics"—indeed I am extremely respectful—however, the reason for taking the perfection of wisdom is that because all the paths are thoroughly embraced and permeated by such a perfection of wisdom, in dependence on it "these relics of the Victor too have become worthy of all beings paying homage and making offerings." "Just as those who depend on a king," such as his ministers and so forth, "also obtain reverence and respect from others," the relics of the Buddha, endowed with immeasurable qualities, are accomplished in dependence on this very perfection of wisdom.

If one thinks, "Well, even if it arose in that way through the power of the perfection of wisdom, since the Buddha has passed into nirvana and is free from acting in that way, the relics are not worthy of offerings," to establish that they are worthy by means of an example: "A precious wish-fulfilling jewel" endowed with all qualities such as granting needs and desires and possessing immeasurable value, "whichever vessel it is kept" or placed "in, such as a casket"—a storage box, amulet box, or so forth—"that vessel is worthy of homage," and "even if" the jewel "is taken out of that vessel," one generates great joy toward "that casket" which previously acted as the vessel in which it was kept, thinking, "Because it is the vessel in which the precious jewel was kept, it is unlike others." "That" the vessel "obtained such qualities is through the power of that precious jewel."

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The wise who have unmistakably realized the meaning of the natural state always unmistakably show and uphold the meaning of the scriptural phenomena of the pronouncements, such as the sutras of the perfection of wisdom, and do not cause the essence of the teaching to decline or be destroyed.

If one thinks, "Well, even if it arose in that way through the power of the perfection of wisdom, since the Buddha has passed into nirvana and is free from acting in that way, the relics are not worthy of offerings," to establish that they are worthy by means of an example: "A precious wish-fulfilling jewel" endowed with all qualities such as granting needs and desires and possessing immeasurable value, "whichever vessel it is kept" or placed "in, such as a casket"—a storage box, amulet box, or so forth—"that vessel is worthy of homage," and "even if" the jewel "is taken out of that vessel," one generates great joy toward "that casket" which previously acted as the vessel in which it was kept, thinking, "Because it is the vessel in which the precious jewel was kept, it is unlike others." "That" the vessel "obtained such qualities is through the power of that precious jewel."

[3-116] translation already produced for this document:
Why is that? If all virtuous phenomena such as giving are bound by apprehending signs and stained by the defilement of inferior mental engagement, they will be wasted by falling into samsara or the extreme of peace; so in order that they are not wasted in that way, dedicating them to unsurpassable complete awakening, they are completely embraced on the path by the perfection of wisdom which completely purifies giving and so forth by means of the wisdom that realizes non-apprehension. Thus, this wisdom "shows exactly one method of the path" in which "all" virtuous phenomena such as giving have one taste as the "cause of a Buddha." "For example, in Jambudvīpa there are many thousands of tens of millions of different trees" such as sandalwood and aloeswood, and though they have various colors, shapes, and scents and so forth and "many forms" with many aspects of color and shape of branches, fruits, leaves, and flowers and so forth, except for "their shadows" merely being expressed as synonyms for shadows of trees, the shadows do not have various differing colors and scents and so forth like the trees, and "shadows do not have distinctions" like the individual trees from their own side. "Similarly to that example, these five perfections" of the Victor, "such as giving," too, if embraced by the wisdom that realizes the non-apprehension of the three spheres, "will attain the very name" of perfections, and that they become supramundane perfections is also by the power of this perfection of wisdom.

heading: **གཞན་དོན་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Having thus taught that the counterfeit perfection of wisdom is to be discarded, explaining how to train in the genuine perfection of wisdom by way of negative consequence: "Whatever phenomenon" does not truly exist as "form," one does not cling to it as nonexistent, "and similarly it is not feeling, and one does not apprehend it" as truly existent "as perception, and does not apprehend it as consciousness, and" does not apprehend it as truly existent as "volition" either, but rather perfectly knows "all phenomena" of samsara and nirvana, illustrated by the entities and features of phenomena such as form being impermanent and so forth, in the manner of being "empty by nature of arising," and shows them to others in that way as well; "this is practicing" the genuine perfection of wisdom, "the supreme perfection of wisdom."

If all virtuous phenomena such as giving are bound by apprehending signs and stained by the defilement of inferior mental engagement, they will be wasted by falling into samsara or the extreme of peace; so in order that they are not wasted in that way, dedicating them to unsurpassable complete awakening, they are completely embraced on the path by the perfection of wisdom which completely purifies giving and so forth by means of the wisdom that realizes non-apprehension. "Similarly to that example, these five perfections" of the Victor, "such as giving," too, if embraced by the wisdom that realizes the non-apprehension of the three spheres, "will attain the very name" of perfections, and that they become supramundane perfections is also by the power of this perfection of wisdom.

translation: The benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest. The seventh, the benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest: The Ornament says, from "On the perfection of wisdom..." up to "...are asserted as reverence and praise." Its defining characteristic is a quality attained by the power of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest, which has become the method for attaining it. If divided, there are twenty-seven. Its boundary is from the second moment of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest up to the ground of a Buddha. To show that, in order to make the bodhisattva of devoted interest thus enter the higher paths and to generate enthusiasm, the Buddhas offer praise, reverence, commendation, and so forth, the meaning taught by the seven verses from "If some..." and so forth is: Compared to some person establishing or guiding however many hosts of sentient beings are dwelling in realms equal in number to however many grains of sand there are in the river Ganges into the state of Hearer or Solitary Realizer arhats, "if some person writes this perfection of wisdom" in letters "and gives" that volume "to a supreme sentient being," a bodhisattva, "this is much more exceedingly superior" in merit than the former.

If one thinks, "Well, even if it arose in that way through the power of the perfection of wisdom, since the Buddha has passed into nirvana and is free from acting in that way, the relics are not worthy of offerings," to establish that they are worthy by means of an example: "A precious wish-fulfilling jewel" endowed with all qualities such as granting needs and desires and possessing immeasurable value, "whichever vessel it is kept" or placed "in, such as a casket"—a storage box, amulet box, or so forth—"that vessel is worthy of homage," and "even if" the jewel "is taken out of that vessel," one generates great joy toward "that casket" which previously acted as the vessel in which it was kept, thinking, "Because it is the vessel in which the precious jewel was kept, it is unlike others." "That" the vessel "obtained such qualities is through the power of that precious jewel."

[3-116] translation already produced for this document:
Why is that? If all virtuous phenomena such as giving are bound by apprehending signs and stained by the defilement of inferior mental engagement, they will be wasted by falling into samsara or the extreme of peace; so in order that they are not wasted in that way, dedicating them to unsurpassable complete awakening, they are completely embraced on the path by the perfection of wisdom which completely purifies giving and so forth by means of the wisdom that realizes non-apprehension. Thus, this wisdom "shows exactly one method of the path" in which "all" virtuous phenomena such as giving have one taste as the "cause of a Buddha." "For example, in Jambudvīpa there are many thousands of tens of millions of different trees" such as sandalwood and aloeswood, and though they have various colors, shapes, and scents and so forth and "many forms" with many aspects of color and shape of branches, fruits, leaves, and flowers and so forth, except for "their shadows" merely being expressed as synonyms for shadows of trees, the shadows do not have various differing colors and scents and so forth like the trees, and "shadows do not have distinctions" like the individual trees from their own side. "Similarly to that example, these five perfections" of the Victor, "such as giving," too, if embraced by the wisdom that realizes the non-apprehension of the three spheres, "will attain the very name" of perfections, and that they become supramundane perfections is also by the power of this perfection of wisdom.

heading: **མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: If one asks, "Why is that?", it is because the former is for the sake of only some sentient beings, whereas the latter becomes for the sake of all sentient beings. For those bodhisattvas, supreme among beings who speak, having trained in this path, "will show all phenomena here" to be "empty by nature," and through having heard, realized, and meditated on that meaning of emptiness, those with dull faculties belonging to the Hearer lineage will quickly "touch" and attain "liberation," completely liberated from samsara; those with medium faculties belonging to the Solitary Realizer lineage, having seen that meaning, "will attain the awakening of a Solitary Realizer;" and "those with sharp faculties" belonging to the Mahayana lineage, having realized all phenomena of samsara and nirvana to be equality, empty of true existence, "will touch the awakening of a Buddha."

Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The seventh, the benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest: The Ornament says, from "On the perfection of wisdom..." up to "...are asserted as reverence and praise." translation: Similarly, if conventional and ultimate awakening mind, which are like the sprout and are the principal meaning taught in the sutras of the Mother, do not exist, the arising of a Victor, who is like the trunk, is entirely nonexistent in the world. If they do not exist, how could Śakra, Brahmā, Hearers, and so forth arise, being equivalent to the branches, leaves, and so forth, which are the results of having practiced virtue and the path after the Buddha's Dharma has been taught? Because there would be no cause.

[3-118] translation already produced for this document:
Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The wise who have unmistakably realized the meaning of the natural state always unmistakably show and uphold the meaning of the scriptural phenomena of the pronouncements, such as the sutras of the perfection of wisdom, and do not cause the essence of the teaching to decline or be destroyed.

Having thus taught that the counterfeit perfection of wisdom is to be discarded, explaining how to train in the genuine perfection of wisdom by way of negative consequence: "Whatever phenomenon" does not truly exist as "form," one does not cling to it as nonexistent, "and similarly it is not feeling, and one does not apprehend it" as truly existent "as perception, and does not apprehend it as consciousness, and" does not apprehend it as truly existent as "volition" either, but rather perfectly knows "all phenomena" of samsara and nirvana, illustrated by the entities and features of phenomena such as form being impermanent and so forth, in the manner of being "empty by nature of arising," and shows them to others in that way as well; "this is practicing" the genuine perfection of wisdom, "the supreme perfection of wisdom."

[3-120] translation already produced for this document:
The benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest. The seventh, the benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest: The Ornament says, from "On the perfection of wisdom..." up to "...are asserted as reverence and praise." Its defining characteristic is a quality attained by the power of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest, which has become the method for attaining it. If divided, there are twenty-seven. Its boundary is from the second moment of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest up to the ground of a Buddha. To show that, in order to make the bodhisattva of devoted interest thus enter the higher paths and to generate enthusiasm, the Buddhas offer praise, reverence, commendation, and so forth, the meaning taught by the seven verses from "If some..." and so forth is: Compared to some person establishing or guiding however many hosts of sentient beings are dwelling in realms equal in number to however many grains of sand there are in the river Ganges into the state of Hearer or Solitary Realizer arhats, "if some person writes this perfection of wisdom" in letters "and gives" that volume "to a supreme sentient being," a bodhisattva, "this is much more exceedingly superior" in merit than the former.

If one asks, "Why is that?", it is because the former is for the sake of only some sentient beings, whereas the latter becomes for the sake of all sentient beings. For those bodhisattvas, supreme among beings who speak, having trained in this path, "will show all phenomena here" to be "empty by nature," and through having heard, realized, and meditated on that meaning of emptiness, those with dull faculties belonging to the Hearer lineage will quickly "touch" and attain "liberation," completely liberated from samsara; those with medium faculties belonging to the Solitary Realizer lineage, having seen that meaning, "will attain the awakening of a Solitary Realizer;" and "those with sharp faculties" belonging to the Mahayana lineage, having realized all phenomena of samsara and nirvana to be equality, empty of true existence, "will touch the awakening of a Buddha."

heading: **མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: Thus, just as "when" the "sun's disk, having risen," emits limitless nets of "light rays" in the ten directions, "at that time sentient beings" in the world realms "strive at doing" many types of "work", "similarly", if "the wise", in order to attain the resultant perfection of wisdom, the exalted wisdom of omniscient knowledge, generate conventional and ultimate awakening mind in their own mindstreams, then based on that, the unsurpassable exalted wisdom of a Buddha will arise, and based on that exalted wisdom itself acting as the empowering condition, by emitting light rays of the profound and vast Dharma to disciples, sentient beings will come to be endowed with temporary higher status and the ultimate phenomena of the qualities of a Sugata.

[3-118] translation already produced for this document:
Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The wise who have unmistakably realized the meaning of the natural state always unmistakably show and uphold the meaning of the scriptural phenomena of the pronouncements, such as the sutras of the perfection of wisdom, and do not cause the essence of the teaching to decline or be destroyed.

དེ་ལྟར་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ལྟར་སྣང་དོར་བྱར་བསྟན་ནས། ལྡོག་འགྲོའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་རྣལ་མ་ལ་སློབ་ཚུལ་འཆད་པར། ཆོས་གང་ལ་གཟུགས་སུ་བདེན་པར་མེད་ན་མེད་པར་ཞེན་པ་མིན་པ་དང་། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཆོར་བ་མིན་ལ་འདུ་ཤེས་སུ་བདེན་པར་མི་དམིགས་ཤིང་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་ལ་དམིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཞིང་། སེམས་པ་ལ་ཡང་བདེན་པར་མི་དམིགས་ལ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་ཆོས་མི་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ཀྱིས་མཚོན་པའི་འཁོར་འདས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀུན་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པར་སྟོང་པའི་ཚུལ་དུ་རབ་ཏུ་ཤེས་ཤིང་གཞན་ལའང་དེ་ལྟར་སྟོན་པ་འདི་ནི། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་རྣལ་མ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཞེས་པའོ། །

Having thus taught that the counterfeit perfection of wisdom is to be discarded, explaining how to train in the genuine perfection of wisdom by way of negative consequence: "Whatever phenomenon" does not truly exist as "form," one does not cling to it as nonexistent, "and similarly it is not feeling, and one does not apprehend it" as truly existent "as perception, and does not apprehend it as consciousness, and" does not apprehend it as truly existent as "volition" either, but rather perfectly knows "all phenomena" of samsara and nirvana, illustrated by the entities and features of phenomena such as form being impermanent and so forth, in the manner of being "empty by nature of arising," and shows them to others in that way as well; "this is practicing" the genuine perfection of wisdom, "the supreme perfection of wisdom."

མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན། བདུན་པ་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན་ནི། རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ། །ནས། བཀུར་བ་དང་ནི་བསྔགས་པར་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་ཐོབ་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཐབས་སུ་གྱུར་པའི་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསྒོམས་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་ཐོབ་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དེ། མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན་ཉེར་བདུན་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྒོམས་པའི་སྐད་ཅིག་གཉིས་པ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། དེ་ལྟར་མོས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལམ་གོང་མར་འཇུག་ཅིང་སྤྲོ་བ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་བསྟོད་པ་དང་བཀུར་སྟི་དང་བསྔགས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་མཛད་དོ་ཞེས་སྟོན་པར། ལ་ལས་གཱང་གའི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་བདུན་གྱིས་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་ནི། གང་ཟག་གང་ལ་ལས་གངྒཱའི་ཀླུང་གི་བྱེ་མ་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ་དེ་སྙེད་ཀྱི་གྲངས་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང་རྣམས་ན་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ཇི་སྙེད་ཅིག་འཁོད་པ་དེ་དག་ཀུན་ཉན་རང་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཉིད་ལ་བཀོད་པའམ་བརྟུལ་བ་པས། གང་ཟག་གང་གིས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ཡི་གེར་བྲིས་ཏེ་སེམས་ཅན་མཆོག་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ལ་གླེགས་བམ་དེ་བྱིན་ན་སྔ་མ་བས་འདི་ནི་བསོད་ནམས་ཆེས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་སོ། །

The benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest. The seventh, the benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest: The Ornament says, from "On the perfection of wisdom..." up to "...are asserted as reverence and praise." Its defining characteristic is a quality attained by the power of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest, which has become the method for attaining it. If divided, there are twenty-seven. Its boundary is from the second moment of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest up to the ground of a Buddha. To show that, in order to make the bodhisattva of devoted interest thus enter the higher paths and to generate enthusiasm, the Buddhas offer praise, reverence, commendation, and so forth, the meaning taught by the seven verses from "If some..." and so forth is: Compared to some person establishing or guiding however many hosts of sentient beings are dwelling in realms equal in number to however many grains of sand there are in the river Ganges into the state of Hearer or Solitary Realizer arhats, "if some person writes this perfection of wisdom" in letters "and gives" that volume "to a supreme sentient being," a bodhisattva, "this is much more exceedingly superior" in merit than the former.

དེ་ཅི་ཡི་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན། སྔ་མ་ནི་སེམས་ཅན་ཕྱོགས་རེ་བའི་དོན་ཡིན་ལ། ཕྱི་མ་ནི་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་དོན་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཏེ། སྨྲ་བའི་སྐྱེས་མཆོག་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག་ལམ་འདིར་བསླབ་ནས་ཆོས་རྣམས་མཐའ་དག་རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དུ་འདིར་སྟོན་པར་བྱེད་ལ། སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་དོན་དེ་ཐོས་ནས་རྟོགས་ཤིང་སྒོམ་པར་བྱས་པས་དབང་རྟུལ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་རིགས་ཅན་རྣམས་མྱུར་དུ་འཁོར་བ་ལས་རྣམ་བར་གྲོལ་བའི་ཐར་བ་ལ་རེག་སྟེ་ཐོབ་པ་དང༌། དབང་འབྲིང་རང་རྒྱལ་གྱི་རིགས་ཅན་རྣམས་དོན་དེ་མཐོང་ནས་རང་རྒྱལ་གྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཐོབ་པ་དང་ནི། དབང་པོ་རྣོན་པོ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་རིགས་ཅན་རྣམས་འཁོར་འདས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀུན་བདེན་སྟོང་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དུ་རྟོགས་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །

If one asks, "Why is that?", it is because the former is for the sake of only some sentient beings, whereas the latter becomes for the sake of all sentient beings. For those bodhisattvas, supreme among beings who speak, having trained in this path, "will show all phenomena here" to be "empty by nature," and through having heard, realized, and meditated on that meaning of emptiness, those with dull faculties belonging to the Hearer lineage will quickly "touch" and attain "liberation," completely liberated from samsara; those with medium faculties belonging to the Solitary Realizer lineage, having seen that meaning, "will attain the awakening of a Solitary Realizer;" and "those with sharp faculties" belonging to the Mahayana lineage, having realized all phenomena of samsara and nirvana to be equality, empty of true existence, "will touch the awakening of a Buddha."

heading: **མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: Showing by way of negative consequence that without awakening mind those results do not exist: "For example, if the" great "nāga lord did not exist in Lake Anavatapta, how could the rivers", such as the Ganges, which arise "by his power, flow in this Jambudvīpa"? If there were no rivers, because there is no moisture, "flowers" such as lotuses and utpalas "and fruits would not arise either". "Also, in the great ocean", "many different forms" of "various jewels" arising from the connection of touching the water "would not exist".

Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The wise who have unmistakably realized the meaning of the natural state always unmistakably show and uphold the meaning of the scriptural phenomena of the pronouncements, such as the sutras of the perfection of wisdom, and do not cause the essence of the teaching to decline or be destroyed.

Having thus taught that the counterfeit perfection of wisdom is to be discarded, explaining how to train in the genuine perfection of wisdom by way of negative consequence: "Whatever phenomenon" does not truly exist as "form," one does not cling to it as nonexistent, "and similarly it is not feeling, and one does not apprehend it" as truly existent "as perception, and does not apprehend it as consciousness, and" does not apprehend it as truly existent as "volition" either, but rather perfectly knows "all phenomena" of samsara and nirvana, illustrated by the entities and features of phenomena such as form being impermanent and so forth, in the manner of being "empty by nature of arising," and shows them to others in that way as well; "this is practicing" the genuine perfection of wisdom, "the supreme perfection of wisdom."

The benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest. The seventh, the benefits of the path of meditation of devoted interest: The Ornament says, from "On the perfection of wisdom..." up to "...are asserted as reverence and praise." Its defining characteristic is a quality attained by the power of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest, which has become the method for attaining it. If divided, there are twenty-seven. Its boundary is from the second moment of meditating on the path of meditation of devoted interest up to the ground of a Buddha. To show that, in order to make the bodhisattva of devoted interest thus enter the higher paths and to generate enthusiasm, the Buddhas offer praise, reverence, commendation, and so forth, the meaning taught by the seven verses from "If some..." and so forth is: Compared to some person establishing or guiding however many hosts of sentient beings are dwelling in realms equal in number to however many grains of sand there are in the river Ganges into the state of Hearer or Solitary Realizer arhats, "if some person writes this perfection of wisdom" in letters "and gives" that volume "to a supreme sentient being," a bodhisattva, "this is much more exceedingly superior" in merit than the former.

heading: **མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: "Similarly" to that example, if "in this world" realm "too" there were no scriptural pronouncements and awakening mind with the essence of emptiness and compassion, which are like the nāga lord, "how could" the arising of benefit and "bliss" and the "stream of exalted wisdom" that clears away evil deeds and obscurations, which arise from the power of "the Sugatas, arise in all these worlds"? They would not arise. If there were no such water stream of exalted wisdom, there would be no "increasing" of the qualities of the grounds and paths, such as the perfection of generosity, and if those did not exist, the results, the "three awakenings", would not exist either, and the immeasurable "phenomena of a Buddha", such as the ten powers, which are like an ocean of qualities of abandonment and realization, would not exist either. Therefore, one should know that generating the two types of precious awakening mind, which are the sole root and source of all the qualities of the Mahayana path and result, in one's own mindstream and striving at the methods to ensure they do not decline but rather increase and expand higher and higher is the root of all excellent collections.

Knowing that abandoning the faults of the fabricated through these three devoted interests is familiarization, in order to abandon the fabricated, showing the defining characteristics of the fabricated perfection of wisdom by way of positive consequence: If whichever bodhisattva, without themselves perfectly knowing the profound meaning of the Mother, emptiness, exactly as it is, thoroughly shows these five aggregates—form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness—as impermanent, suffering, lacking a personal self, and so forth, by way of clinging to them as truly existent, and speaks of and meditates on this saying, "This is the perfection of wisdom," that is practicing the counterfeit perfection of wisdom or the fabricated perfection of wisdom, because it merely shows a path that takes conventional proliferations as the object of its mode of apprehension. The wise who have unmistakably realized the meaning of the natural state always unmistakably show and uphold the meaning of the scriptural phenomena of the pronouncements, such as the sutras of the perfection of wisdom, and do not cause the essence of the teaching to decline or be destroyed.

heading: **མོས་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་ཕན་ཡོན།**
translation: For example, in this world realm, if "however many" "beings" there are, such as light-emitting stars, lamps, and fireflies, that dispel darkness and illuminate forms, simultaneously "emitted" "lights" in order to illuminate the directions, the arising of the light rays of the "sun's disk" alone would be much more extraordinarily exalted and supreme. All other lights of the multitudes of illuminators, such as stars, "would not amount" even "to a fraction", merely belonging to a portion, of the sun's light. "Similarly", "Hearers" and so forth "would not amount to a fraction" of the "qualities of a bodhisattva". Therefore, one should know that the Buddhas praising bodhisattvas is also factual. This concludes the commentary on the fifth chapter, the Categories of Merit, from the Jewel Lamp Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, Clarifying the Profound Reality of Dependent Arising, a Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection.

Therefore, one should know that generating the two types of precious awakening mind, which are the sole root and source of all the qualities of the Mahayana path and result, in one's own mindstream and striving at the methods to ensure they do not decline but rather increase and expand higher and higher is the root of all excellent collections.

source: རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་སྒོམ་ལམ། སྟོང་ཕྲག་བརྒྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྟར། རྒྱན་དུའང་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་། བརྒྱད་པར་གསུངས་ཀྱང་དོན་ལ་འགལ་བ་མེད་པས་འདིར་དེ་ལས་གོ་རིམ་བཟློག་སྟེ་བརྒྱད་པ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསྟན་པས། དེ་ཉིད་སྟོན་པར་རྒྱན་ལས། ཐབས་དང་མི་དམིགས་པ་དག་གིས། །ནས། འདིར་བརྗོད་དོ། །ཞེས་པའི་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང༌། རང་གཞན་གང་རུང་གི་དགེ་རྩ་ལ་དགའ་བ་བསྒོམ་པའི་སྒྲ་དོན་འདྲེས་རུང་དུ་འཛིན་པའི་རྟོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རངས་སྒོམས་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། རང་དང་གཞན་གྱི་དགེ་རྩ་ལ་དགའ་བ་བསྒོམ་པའི་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་སྒོམ་ལམ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ས་དང་པོ་ནས་རྒྱུན་མཐའི་བར་ཡོད། བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བྱའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེ་གོང་འཕེལ་དུ་བྱེད་པ་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་ལ་རག་ལས་པས་ཐོག་མར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རངས་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྟོན་པར། ཉན་ཐོས་ཚོགས་རྣམས་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གིས་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་ནི། ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རང་དོན་དུ་ཇི་སྙེད་པའི་སྦྱིན་པ་གཏོང་བ་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་དགེ་བ་དང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ལས་བྱུང་བ་དང་བསྒོམ་པ་ལས་བྱུང་བའི་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་དང་རབ་ཏུ་ལྡན་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་བརྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་བསྐྱེད་པའང་སྐྱེ་འཕགས་ཀུན་གྱི་དགེ་རྩ་ཐམས་ཅད་མི་དམིགས་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བའི་ཐབས་མཁས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གི་སེམས་སྐད་ཅིག་གཅིག་བསྐྱེད་པ་ལ། ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོས་དེའི་ཆ་ཤས་སུ་གཏོགས་པ་ཙམ་གྱི་ཆར་ཡང་མི་ཕོད་དེ་ཉན་ཐོས་རྣམས་ནི་ཐབས་ཤེས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་མི་དང་ལྡན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཞེས་པའོ །
translation: The path of meditation of rejoicing. Although in the Hundred Thousand and so forth, as well as in the Ornament, the path of meditation of dedication is taught as the eighth, since there is no contradiction in meaning, here the order is reversed from that, and the path of meditation of rejoicing is taught as the eighth. To show that very point, there is one verse from the Ornament: from "By means of skillful methods and non-apprehension..." up to "...is stated here." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of meditating on joy in the roots of virtue of either oneself or others as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of rejoicing. If divided, there are two: the paths of meditation of rejoicing that meditate on joy in the roots of virtue of oneself and of others. Its boundaries are from the first ground up to the end of the continuum. Since causing the roots of virtue to be dedicated to unsurpassable awakening to increase further depends on rejoicing, to show first the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the one verse beginning with "The multitudes of Hearers..." is as follows: Even if "the multitudes of Hearers" were to generate, for their own sake, a great multitude of merit thoroughly endowed with "however many" virtues arising from giving "generosity", arising from "ethical discipline", and roots of virtue arising from "meditation", the "multitude of merit" of the multitudes of Hearers "would not amount to a fraction", even one belonging to a mere portion of that, of a bodhisattva generating a single instant of a mind of "rejoicing" that is embraced by the wisdom realizing all roots of virtue of all ordinary and noble beings as non-apprehendable and by the special skillful means of dedicating to unsurpassable awakening. This is because Hearers do not possess such special means and wisdom.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
source: བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དགུ་པ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པརཅན། །ནས། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་འབྱུང་བདག་ཉིད་དོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས། རང་གཞན་གང་རུང་གི་དགེ་རྩ་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་ཏུ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲ་དོན་འདྲེས་རུང་དུ་འཛིན་པའི་རྟོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་། མི་དམིག་པའི་རྣམ་པ་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དབེན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་དྲན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། མཚན་མ་མེད་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་རྗེས་སུ་གནང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཁམས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་གཏོགས་པའིབསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་འབྱུང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་ཆུང་ངུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང༌། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་འབྲིང་གི་བསྔ་ོབ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བསྔ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་རོ། །སྔར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གིས་མི་ཟད་པར་སྤེལ་བའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེའང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པ་བསྔོ་བ་ལ་རག་ལས་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཡི་རང་སྒོས་ལམ་གྱི་འོག་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་སྟོན་པར། །ཞིང་ཁམས་མང་པོ་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་དག་ན་གང་བཞུགས་པའི་འདས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་རྣམས་དང་།
