translation: The path of meditation of dedication. To show the ninth, the path of meditation of dedication, it is stated in the Ornament: from "Special thorough dedication..." up to "...is the nature of great merit arising." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of transforming the roots of virtue of either oneself or others into factors of perfect awakening as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of dedication. If divided, there are twelve: the path of meditation of special thorough dedication, the path of meditation of dedication with the aspect of non-apprehension, the path of meditation of dedication having the defining characteristic of being unmistaken, the path of meditation of isolated dedication, the path of meditation of dedication remembering the nature of the Buddha's multitude of merit, the path of meditation of dedication skillful in means, the path of meditation of signless dedication, the path of meditation of dedication permitted by the Buddhas, the path of meditation of dedication not included in the three realms, the path of meditation of small dedication where great merit arises, the path of meditation of medium dedication of great merit, and the path of meditation of great dedication of great merit. Its boundaries are from the first up to the tenth ground. Since causing those roots of virtue—which were previously increased inexhaustibly by rejoicing—to be directed toward unsurpassable awakening depends on dedication, to show the path of meditation of dedication after the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the eight verses beginning with "Of previous past times..." is as follows: Whichever "many" hundreds of thousands of millions of "previous Buddhas" appeared in the time of "past" eons, and the limitless past Buddhas who dwelled in "many limitless worlds" of thousands of millions, and whichever "protectors of the world" have passed beyond the extremes of existence and peace into non-abiding nirvana, and are now living and remaining, continuing to teach the "precious Dharma" in order to exhaust the suffering of migrating beings—all of them, from first stably generating the mind of supreme awakening in their mindstreams up to finally becoming perfectly awakened and leading immeasurable trainees completely out of cyclic existence, down to the very "waning" or exhaustion of the sublime Dharma of those Victorious Ones—whichever "merit" of their first generating of the mind up to that time, and whichever possessing magnificent roots of virtue of "activities" such as the six perfections and the four means of gathering, and whichever "results" such as the ten powers and the eighteen unshared phenomena of a Buddha were attained, and whichever other contaminated and uncontaminated "virtues" of "the Buddhas' sons", the bodhisattvas, "along with" "the Hearers" and Solitary Realizers, in short, of all individuals who are learners and non-learners—all those, by gathering them into one with one's mind, that bodhisattva "rejoices" with supreme joy from the depths of their heart, without jealousy and so forth. Embracing the intention—the generation of the mind—with the wisdom realizing the three spheres as non-apprehendable, "in order to attain" "great" unsurpassable "awakening" as the cause for accomplishing the welfare of migrating beings equaling the limits of space, one should "dedicate" all those roots of virtue of oneself and others.

The path of meditation of rejoicing. Although in the Hundred Thousand and so forth, as well as in the Ornament, the path of meditation of dedication is taught as the eighth, since there is no contradiction in meaning, here the order is reversed from that, and the path of meditation of rejoicing is taught as the eighth. To show that very point, there is one verse from the Ornament: from "By means of skillful methods and non-apprehension..." up to "...is stated here." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of meditating on joy in the roots of virtue of either oneself or others as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of rejoicing. If divided, there are two: the paths of meditation of rejoicing that meditate on joy in the roots of virtue of oneself and of others. Its boundaries are from the first ground up to the end of the continuum. Since causing the roots of virtue to be dedicated to unsurpassable awakening to increase further depends on rejoicing, to show first the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the one verse beginning with "The multitudes of Hearers..." is as follows: Even if "the multitudes of Hearers" were to generate, for their own sake, a great multitude of merit thoroughly endowed with "however many" virtues arising from giving "generosity", arising from "ethical discipline", and roots of virtue arising from "meditation", the "multitude of merit" of the multitudes of Hearers "would not amount to a fraction", even one belonging to a mere portion of that, of a bodhisattva generating a single instant of a mind of "rejoicing" that is embraced by the wisdom realizing all roots of virtue of all ordinary and noble beings as non-apprehendable and by the special skillful means of dedicating to unsurpassable awakening. This is because Hearers do not possess such special means and wisdom.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Having thus taught the Mahayana dedication in general, to show that one must make a special dedication by way of the non-apprehension of the three spheres: Regarding "that" "thorough dedication" "likewise", "if" one has "the perception" clinging to it as true or apprehending it as true, thinking "this is" the dedicating "mind", and one has the perception of "awakening"—"where" it is dedicated—as true, and the perception arises of "sentient beings"—for whose sake the thorough dedication is made—as true, then, since one is bound by the perception or apprehension of signs that manifest adherence to the three—the action, agent, and object—as true, one "abides in a view" with the focal aim of true apprehension; and since "that mind" "has an apprehension" of "attachment" to the three spheres through true adherence, it is "not included in" "thorough dedication" having an unmistaken nature.

ཁམས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་གཏོགས་པའིབསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་འབྱུང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་ཆུང་ངུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང༌། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་འབྲིང་གི་བསྔ་ོབ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བསྔ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་རོ། །སྔར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གིས་མི་ཟད་པར་སྤེལ་བའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེའང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པ་བསྔོ་བ་ལ་རག་ལས་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཡི་རང་སྒོས་ལམ་གྱི་འོག་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་སྟོན་པར། འདས་དུས་སྔོན་གྱི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་བརྒྱད་ཀྱིས་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་ནི། བསྐལ་པ་འདས་པའི་དུས་ན་བྱུང་བའི་སྔོན་གྱི་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་གང་ཞིག །ཞིང་ཁམས་མང་པོ་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་དག་ན་གང་བཞུགས་པའི་འདས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་རྣམས་དང་། གང་ཡང་སྲིད་ཞིའི་མཐའ་ལས་འདས་པའིའི་མི་གནས་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་མགོན་པོ་རྣམས་ད་ལྟར་འཚོ་ཞིང་བཞེས་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྔུག་བསྔལ་ཟད་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་རིན་ཆེན་ཆོས་ཀྱང་སྟོན་བཞིན་དུ་བཞུགས་པ་དེ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་མཆོག་ཏུ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ་རང་རྒྱུད་ལ་བརྟན་པོར་བསྐྱེད་པ་ནས་བཟུང་སྟེ་མཐུར་ཐུག་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་ནས་གདུལ་བྱ་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་འཁོར་བ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་འདྲེན་པ་མཛད་པ་དེ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དམ་པའི་ཆོས་ནུབ་པའམ་ཟད་པར་གྱུར་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་དུས་དེའི་བར་གྱི་རྒྱལ་བ་དེ་དག་གི་དང་པོ་ཐུགས་བསྐྱེད་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང་། སྤྱོད་པ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་དང་བསྡུ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་བཞི་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རླབས་པོ་ཆེའི་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དང་། འབྲས་བུ་སྟོབས་བཅུ་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་མ་འདྲེས་པ་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་ལ་སོགས་པ་གང་ཞིག་ཐོབ་པ་དང་། གང་དག་གཞན་ཡང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྲས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་དང་ནི་ཉན་ཐོས་དང་རང་རྒྱལ་དང་བཅས་པ་མདོར་ན་སློབ་པ་དང་མི་སློབ་པའི་གང་ཟག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དགེ་བ་ཟག་བཅས་དང་ཟག་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་གི་བློས་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསྡུས་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཡིས་ཕྲག་དོག་སོགས་མེད་པར་བསམ་པ་ཐག་པ་ནས་ཡིད་རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བས་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱ་ཞིང་། བསམ་པ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་འཁོར་གསུམ་མི་དམིགས་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པར་བྱས་ནས་ནམ་མཁའི་མཐའ་དང་མཉམ་པའི་འགྲོ་བའི་དོན་སྒྲུབ་པའི་རྒྱུ་རུ་བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཆེན་པོ་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་ནི་རང་གཞན་གྱི་དགེ་རྩ་དེ་ཐམས་ཅད་བསྔོ་བར་བྱའོ། The path of meditation of dedication. To show the ninth, the path of meditation of dedication, it is stated in the Ornament: from "Special thorough dedication..." up to "...is the nature of great merit arising." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of transforming the roots of virtue of either oneself or others into factors of perfect awakening as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of dedication. If divided, there are twelve: the path of meditation of special thorough dedication, the path of meditation of dedication with the aspect of non-apprehension, the path of meditation of dedication having the defining characteristic of being unmistaken, the path of meditation of isolated dedication, the path of meditation of dedication remembering the nature of the Buddha's multitude of merit, the path of meditation of dedication skillful in means, the path of meditation of signless dedication, the path of meditation of dedication permitted by the Buddhas, the path of meditation of dedication not included in the three realms, the path of meditation of small dedication where great merit arises, the path of meditation of medium dedication of great merit, and the path of meditation of great dedication of great merit. Its boundaries are from the first up to the tenth ground. Since causing those roots of virtue—which were previously increased inexhaustibly by rejoicing—to be directed toward unsurpassable awakening depends on dedication, to show the path of meditation of dedication after the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the eight verses beginning with "Of previous past times..." is as follows: Whichever "many" hundreds of thousands of millions of "previous Buddhas" appeared in the time of "past" eons, and the limitless past Buddhas who dwelled in "many limitless worlds" of thousands of millions, and whichever "protectors of the world" have passed beyond the extremes of existence and peace into non-abiding nirvana, and are now living and remaining, continuing to teach the "precious Dharma" in order to exhaust the suffering of migrating beings—all of them, from first stably generating the mind of supreme awakening in their mindstreams up to finally becoming perfectly awakened and leading immeasurable trainees completely out of cyclic existence, down to the very "waning" or exhaustion of the sublime Dharma of those Victorious Ones—whichever "merit" of their first generating of the mind up to that time, and whichever possessing magnificent roots of virtue of "activities" such as the six perfections and the four means of gathering, and whichever "results" such as the ten powers and the eighteen unshared phenomena of a Buddha were attained, and whichever other contaminated and uncontaminated "virtues" of "the Buddhas' sons", the bodhisattvas, "along with" "the Hearers" and Solitary Realizers, in short, of all individuals who are learners and non-learners—all those, by gathering them into one with one's mind, that bodhisattva "rejoices" with supreme joy from the depths of their heart, without jealousy and so forth. Embracing the intention—the generation of the mind—with the wisdom realizing the three spheres as non-apprehendable, "in order to attain" "great" unsurpassable "awakening" as the cause for accomplishing the welfare of migrating beings equaling the limits of space, one should "dedicate" all those roots of virtue of oneself and others.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: If one asks, "Then how should one dedicate?" "If" a bodhisattva comes to "know" how "these phenomena"—the virtue to be dedicated, the dedicating mind, and so forth—are inherently ceased and "exhausted" or non-existent in terms of true establishment, and how that unsurpassed awakening "where" it is "thoroughly dedicated" is also not truly established or "exhausted", and how all the phenomena of the dedicated, the dedicator, and the object of dedication are unproduced and "exhausted" by their own essence—meaning they do not have even the slightest establishment from their own side—and therefore, ultimately, how the dedicating phenomena or mind "never dedicates" or does not have any virtue to dedicate to "whichever phenomena" are the objects of dedication; then being embraced by "thoroughly knowing" "thus" that the three spheres of dedication are not truly existent is called "excellent thorough dedication".

རང་གཞན་གང་རུང་གི་དགེ་རྩ་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་ཏུ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲ་དོན་འདྲེས་རུང་དུ་འཛིན་པའི་རྟོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་། མི་དམིག་པའི་རྣམ་པ་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དབེན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་དྲན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། མཚན་མ་མེད་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་རྗེས་སུ་གནང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཁམས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་གཏོགས་པའིབསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་འབྱུང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་ཆུང་ངུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང༌། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་འབྲིང་གི་བསྔ་ོབ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བསྔ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་རོ། །སྔར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གིས་མི་ཟད་པར་སྤེལ་བའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེའང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པ་བསྔོ་བ་ལ་རག་ལས་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཡི་རང་སྒོས་ལམ་གྱི་འོག་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་སྟོན་པར། འདས་དུས་སྔོན་གྱི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་བརྒྱད་ཀྱིས་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་ནི། བསྐལ་པ་འདས་པའི་དུས་ན་བྱུང་བའི་སྔོན་གྱི་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་གང་ཞིག །ཞིང་ཁམས་མང་པོ་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་དག་ན་གང་བཞུགས་པའི་འདས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་རྣམས་དང་། སྤྱོད་པ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་དང་བསྡུ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་བཞི་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རླབས་པོ་ཆེའི་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དང་། འབྲས་བུ་སྟོབས་བཅུ་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་མ་འདྲེས་པ་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་ལ་སོགས་པ་གང་ཞིག་ཐོབ་པ་དང་། གང་དག་གཞན་ཡང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྲས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་དང་ནི་ཉན་ཐོས་དང་རང་རྒྱལ་དང་བཅས་པ་མདོར་ན་སློབ་པ་དང་མི་སློབ་པའི་གང་ཟག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དགེ་བ་ཟག་བཅས་དང་ཟག་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་གི་བློས་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསྡུས་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཡིས་ཕྲག་དོག་སོགས་མེད་པར་བསམ་པ་ཐག་པ་ནས་ཡིད་རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བས་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱ་ཞིང་། The path of meditation of dedication. To show the ninth, the path of meditation of dedication, it is stated in the Ornament: from "Special thorough dedication..." up to "...is the nature of great merit arising." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of transforming the roots of virtue of either oneself or others into factors of perfect awakening as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of dedication. If divided, there are twelve: the path of meditation of special thorough dedication, the path of meditation of dedication with the aspect of non-apprehension, the path of meditation of dedication having the defining characteristic of being unmistaken, the path of meditation of isolated dedication, the path of meditation of dedication remembering the nature of the Buddha's multitude of merit, the path of meditation of dedication skillful in means, the path of meditation of signless dedication, the path of meditation of dedication permitted by the Buddhas, the path of meditation of dedication not included in the three realms, the path of meditation of small dedication where great merit arises, the path of meditation of medium dedication of great merit, and the path of meditation of great dedication of great merit. Its boundaries are from the first up to the tenth ground. Since causing those roots of virtue—which were previously increased inexhaustibly by rejoicing—to be directed toward unsurpassable awakening depends on dedication, to show the path of meditation of dedication after the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the eight verses beginning with "Of previous past times..." is as follows: Whichever "many" hundreds of thousands of millions of "previous Buddhas" appeared in the time of "past" eons, and the limitless past Buddhas who dwelled in "many limitless worlds" of thousands of millions, and whichever "protectors of the world" have passed beyond the extremes of existence and peace into non-abiding nirvana, and are now living and remaining, continuing to teach the "precious Dharma" in order to exhaust the suffering of migrating beings—all of them, from first stably generating the mind of supreme awakening in their mindstreams up to finally becoming perfectly awakened and leading immeasurable trainees completely out of cyclic existence, down to the very "waning" or exhaustion of the sublime Dharma of those Victorious Ones—whichever "merit" of their first generating of the mind up to that time, and whichever possessing magnificent roots of virtue of "activities" such as the six perfections and the four means of gathering, and whichever "results" such as the ten powers and the eighteen unshared phenomena of a Buddha were attained, and whichever other contaminated and uncontaminated "virtues" of "the Buddhas' sons", the bodhisattvas, "along with" "the Hearers" and Solitary Realizers, in short, of all individuals who are learners and non-learners—all those, by gathering them into one with one's mind, that bodhisattva "rejoices" with supreme joy from the depths of their heart, without jealousy and so forth. Embracing the intention—the generation of the mind—with the wisdom realizing the three spheres as non-apprehendable, "in order to attain" "great" unsurpassable "awakening" as the cause for accomplishing the welfare of migrating beings equaling the limits of space, one should "dedicate" all those roots of virtue of oneself and others.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Regarding this, others say: If pure and impure dedication are posited by the absence or presence of the perception of signs, why do some sutras teach apprehension as primary? That was taught in order to lead some beginners, but to teach that virtues bound by manifest adherence are not entirely pure, it is stated: "If" one has "the perception of signs" regarding the three—the action, agent, and object—of dedication and makes dedication while being "presumptuous", "that is not perfectly dedicating."

བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དགུ་པ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པརཅན། །ནས། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་འབྱུང་བདག་ཉིད་དོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས། རང་གཞན་གང་རུང་གི་དགེ་རྩ་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་ཏུ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲ་དོན་འདྲེས་རུང་དུ་འཛིན་པའི་རྟོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་། མི་དམིག་པའི་རྣམ་པ་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དབེན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་དྲན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། མཚན་མ་མེད་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་རྗེས་སུ་གནང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཁམས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་གཏོགས་པའིབསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་འབྱུང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་ཆུང་ངུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང༌། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་འབྲིང་གི་བསྔ་ོབ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བསྔ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་རོ། །སྔར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གིས་མི་ཟད་པར་སྤེལ་བའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེའང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པ་བསྔོ་བ་ལ་རག་ལས་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཡི་རང་སྒོས་ལམ་གྱི་འོག་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་སྟོན་པར། འདས་དུས་སྔོན་གྱི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་བརྒྱད་ཀྱིས་བསྟན་པའི་དོན་ནི། བསྐལ་པ་འདས་པའི་དུས་ན་བྱུང་བའི་སྔོན་གྱི་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་གང་ཞིག །ཞིང་ཁམས་མང་པོ་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་དག་ན་གང་བཞུགས་པའི་འདས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་རྣམས་དང་། གང་ཡང་སྲིད་ཞིའི་མཐའ་ལས་འདས་པའིའི་མི་གནས་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་མགོན་པོ་རྣམས་ད་ལྟར་འཚོ་ཞིང་བཞེས་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྔུག་བསྔལ་ཟད་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་དུ་རིན་ཆེན་ཆོས་ཀྱང་སྟོན་བཞིན་དུ་བཞུགས་པ་དེ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་མཆོག་ཏུ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ་རང་རྒྱུད་ལ་བརྟན་པོར་བསྐྱེད་པ་ནས་བཟུང་སྟེ་མཐུར་ཐུག་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་ནས་གདུལ་བྱ་དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་འཁོར་བ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་འདྲེན་པ་མཛད་པ་དེ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དམ་པའི་ཆོས་ནུབ་པའམ་ཟད་པར་གྱུར་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་དུས་དེའི་བར་གྱི་རྒྱལ་བ་དེ་དག་གི་དང་པོ་ཐུགས་བསྐྱེད་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང་། སྤྱོད་པ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་དང་བསྡུ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་བཞི་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རླབས་པོ་ཆེའི་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དང་། འབྲས་བུ་སྟོབས་བཅུ་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་མ་འདྲེས་པ་བཅོ་བརྒྱད་ལ་སོགས་པ་གང་ཞིག་ཐོབ་པ་དང་། གང་དག་གཞན་ཡང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྲས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་དང་ནི་ཉན་ཐོས་དང་རང་རྒྱལ་དང་བཅས་པ་མདོར་ན་སློབ་པ་དང་མི་སློབ་པའི་གང་ཟག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དགེ་བ་ཟག་བཅས་དང་ཟག་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་གི་བློས་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསྡུས་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཡིས་ཕྲག་དོག་སོགས་མེད་པར་བསམ་པ་ཐག་པ་ནས་ཡིད་རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བས་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱ་ཞིང་། བསམ་པ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་འཁོར་གསུམ་མི་དམིགས་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པར་བྱས་ནས་ནམ་མཁའི་མཐའ་དང་མཉམ་པའི་འགྲོ་བའི་དོན་སྒྲུབ་པའི་རྒྱུ་རུ་བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཆེན་པོ་ཐོབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་ནི་རང་གཞན་གྱི་དགེ་རྩ་དེ་ཐམས་ཅད་བསྔོ་བར་བྱའོ། The path of meditation of dedication. To show the ninth, the path of meditation of dedication, it is stated in the Ornament: from "Special thorough dedication..." up to "...is the nature of great merit arising." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of transforming the roots of virtue of either oneself or others into factors of perfect awakening as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of dedication. If divided, there are twelve: the path of meditation of special thorough dedication, the path of meditation of dedication with the aspect of non-apprehension, the path of meditation of dedication having the defining characteristic of being unmistaken, the path of meditation of isolated dedication, the path of meditation of dedication remembering the nature of the Buddha's multitude of merit, the path of meditation of dedication skillful in means, the path of meditation of signless dedication, the path of meditation of dedication permitted by the Buddhas, the path of meditation of dedication not included in the three realms, the path of meditation of small dedication where great merit arises, the path of meditation of medium dedication of great merit, and the path of meditation of great dedication of great merit. Its boundaries are from the first up to the tenth ground. Since causing those roots of virtue—which were previously increased inexhaustibly by rejoicing—to be directed toward unsurpassable awakening depends on dedication, to show the path of meditation of dedication after the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the eight verses beginning with "Of previous past times..." is as follows: Whichever "many" hundreds of thousands of millions of "previous Buddhas" appeared in the time of "past" eons, and the limitless past Buddhas who dwelled in "many limitless worlds" of thousands of millions, and whichever "protectors of the world" have passed beyond the extremes of existence and peace into non-abiding nirvana, and are now living and remaining, continuing to teach the "precious Dharma" in order to exhaust the suffering of migrating beings—all of them, from first stably generating the mind of supreme awakening in their mindstreams up to finally becoming perfectly awakened and leading immeasurable trainees completely out of cyclic existence, down to the very "waning" or exhaustion of the sublime Dharma of those Victorious Ones—whichever "merit" of their first generating of the mind up to that time, and whichever possessing magnificent roots of virtue of "activities" such as the six perfections and the four means of gathering, and whichever "results" such as the ten powers and the eighteen unshared phenomena of a Buddha were attained, and whichever other contaminated and uncontaminated "virtues" of "the Buddhas' sons", the bodhisattvas, "along with" "the Hearers" and Solitary Realizers, in short, of all individuals who are learners and non-learners—all those, by gathering them into one with one's mind, that bodhisattva "rejoices" with supreme joy from the depths of their heart, without jealousy and so forth. Embracing the intention—the generation of the mind—with the wisdom realizing the three spheres as non-apprehendable, "in order to attain" "great" unsurpassable "awakening" as the cause for accomplishing the welfare of migrating beings equaling the limits of space, one should "dedicate" all those roots of virtue of oneself and others.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: "If," on the other hand, one has the perception that those three phenomena lack the signs of true establishment and dedicates by way of "thoroughly knowing" them to be not truly existent and illusion-like, "that is perfectly thoroughly dedicating" to "awakening". For example, "just as" eating "good food mixed with poison" appears pleasant temporarily but ultimately ruins one, "similarly", even though "white phenomena" are virtuous, "apprehending" them with the perception of true adherence is "said by the Victor" to be like eating good food mixed with poison.

བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དགུ་པ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པརཅན། །ནས། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེ་འབྱུང་བདག་ཉིད་དོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས། རང་གཞན་གང་རུང་གི་དགེ་རྩ་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡན་ལག་ཏུ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པའི་སྒྲ་དོན་འདྲེས་རུང་དུ་འཛིན་པའི་རྟོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། ཡོངས་སུ་བསྔོ་བ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་། མི་དམིག་པའི་རྣམ་པ་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཕྱིན་ཅི་མ་ལོག་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཅན་གྱི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། དབེན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་དྲན་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། མཚན་མ་མེད་པའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས་རྗེས་སུ་གནང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། ཁམས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་གཏོགས་པའིབསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོ་འབྱུང་བའི་བསྔོ་བ་ཆུང་ངུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང༌། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་འབྲིང་གི་བསྔ་ོབ་སྒོམ་ལམ། བསོད་ནམས་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བསྔ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་རོ། །སྔར་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་གིས་མི་ཟད་པར་སྤེལ་བའི་དགེ་རྩ་དེའང་བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བར་བྱེད་པ་བསྔོ་བ་ལ་རག་ལས་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཡི་རང་སྒོས་ལམ་གྱི་འོག་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་སྟོན་པར། གང་དག་གཞན་ཡང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྲས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་དང་ནི་ཉན་ཐོས་དང་རང་རྒྱལ་དང་བཅས་པ་མདོར་ན་སློབ་པ་དང་མི་སློབ་པའི་གང་ཟག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་དགེ་བ་ཟག་བཅས་དང་ཟག་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་གི་བློས་གཅིག་ཏུ་བསྡུས་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཡིས་ཕྲག་དོག་སོགས་མེད་པར་བསམ་པ་ཐག་པ་ནས་ཡིད་རབ་ཏུ་དགའ་བས་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱ་ཞིང་། The path of meditation of dedication. To show the ninth, the path of meditation of dedication, it is stated in the Ornament: from "Special thorough dedication..." up to "...is the nature of great merit arising." That Mahayana subsequent clear realization that is endowed with the realization that apprehends the sound and meaning of transforming the roots of virtue of either oneself or others into factors of perfect awakening as suitable to be mixed, is the definition of the path of meditation of dedication. If divided, there are twelve: the path of meditation of special thorough dedication, the path of meditation of dedication with the aspect of non-apprehension, the path of meditation of dedication having the defining characteristic of being unmistaken, the path of meditation of isolated dedication, the path of meditation of dedication remembering the nature of the Buddha's multitude of merit, the path of meditation of dedication skillful in means, the path of meditation of signless dedication, the path of meditation of dedication permitted by the Buddhas, the path of meditation of dedication not included in the three realms, the path of meditation of small dedication where great merit arises, the path of meditation of medium dedication of great merit, and the path of meditation of great dedication of great merit. Its boundaries are from the first up to the tenth ground. Since causing those roots of virtue—which were previously increased inexhaustibly by rejoicing—to be directed toward unsurpassable awakening depends on dedication, to show the path of meditation of dedication after the path of meditation of rejoicing, the meaning taught by the eight verses beginning with "Of previous past times..." is as follows: Whichever "many" hundreds of thousands of millions of "previous Buddhas" appeared in the time of "past" eons, and the limitless past Buddhas who dwelled in "many limitless worlds" of thousands of millions, and whichever "protectors of the world" have passed beyond the extremes of existence and peace into non-abiding nirvana, and are now living and remaining, continuing to teach the "precious Dharma" in order to exhaust the suffering of migrating beings—all of them, from first stably generating the mind of supreme awakening in their mindstreams up to finally becoming perfectly awakened and leading immeasurable trainees completely out of cyclic existence, down to the very "waning" or exhaustion of the sublime Dharma of those Victorious Ones—whichever "merit" of their first generating of the mind up to that time, and whichever possessing magnificent roots of virtue of "activities" such as the six perfections and the four means of gathering, and whichever "results" such as the ten powers and the eighteen unshared phenomena of a Buddha were attained, and whichever other contaminated and uncontaminated "virtues" of "the Buddhas' sons", the bodhisattvas, "along with" "the Hearers" and Solitary Realizers, in short, of all individuals who are learners and non-learners—all those, by gathering them into one with one's mind, that bodhisattva "rejoices" with supreme joy from the depths of their heart, without jealousy and so forth. Embracing the intention—the generation of the mind—with the wisdom realizing the three spheres as non-apprehendable, "in order to attain" "great" unsurpassable "awakening" as the cause for accomplishing the welfare of migrating beings equaling the limits of space, one should "dedicate" all those roots of virtue of oneself and others.

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Having thus taught the manner of dedication extensively, to summarize it is stated: Since the ways of pure and impure dedication are as previously explained, one should "thus" understand the faults and qualities and train in unmistaken "thorough dedication". How? With the gnosis that unmistakenly realizes and knows the rejoicing of "those" Victors, the perfectly complete "Buddhas", the virtues to be dedicated, and the manner of dedication, etc., they know whatever is the essence or aspect of dedication conventionally, whatever infallible result arises from it and what it is like, and what their nature of ultimate non-apprehension is like. Having realized their status just as it is, regarding how they rejoice and dedicate, one thinks: "I too shall rejoice in accordance with that and make such a thorough dedication." By thinking this and dedicating, even if one is unskilled in how to dedicate oneself, because one dedicates in accordance with how the Victors dedicate, it is entirely pure dedication. As it is said in the Aspiration of Good Conduct, "Just as the hero Mañjuśrī knows..." and so forth. To teach the result of dedicating "thus": If one "thoroughly dedicates" all the merit of oneself and others to great "awakening" by way of being embraced by the wisdom that realizes them as non-apprehendable "just as it was explained", it is a perfectly pure dedication, akin to "good food without poison", and its result is not abandoning or attaining Buddhahood, and one is unmistakenly speaking the Mahayana Dharma "spoken by the Victor".

heading: **བསྔོ་བ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: "That bodhisattva", "the hero" who "thoroughly dedicates" "thus" in the manner of not apprehending things as true, "outshines" "all those" "bodhisattvas in the world" who have an apprehension that grasps at signs. Thus it is said. This concludes the commentary on the sixth chapter, on thorough dedication, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called the Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate, Illuminating the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

translation: Path of meditation of accomplishment. Tenth, to teach the path of meditation of accomplishment, it is said in the Ornament: From "Its essence, supremacy..." up to "...directing it, is of great purpose." The definition of the path of meditation of accomplishment is: any undefiled Mahayana subsequent clear realization that establishes the lasting result of the ultimate realization which is to be attained by oneself. When divided, there are five: the essence of that path of meditation of accomplishment, the supremacy of the path of meditation of accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom, that path of meditation not constructing all phenomena as truly established, that path of meditation directing all phenomena toward lacking the apprehension of true establishment, and the great purpose of attaining Buddhahood as the result of that path of meditation. Its boundaries are from the first to the tenth ground. To teach such a path of meditation of accomplishment, the four verses beginning with "Blind without a guide..." teach what is called supremacy among the five paths of meditation of accomplishment. Furthermore, "for example", even if "a hundred million" "blind" people lacking eyes, without a "guide" or leader to lead them on the path, assemble together, if they "do not see" and do not know the "way" to go to the "city", then "how could they" enter that path and "enter the city"? "There is no way" that could happen.

heading: **སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: "Similarly", "if" one lacks "this" eye-like perfection of "wisdom" that realizes the abiding nature, "these five perfections, giving and so forth", which are like those "without eyes", are not embraced by wisdom—which becomes the essence of accomplishment that is like a guide leading to higher grounds such as the Extremely Joyful—or lack that companion, and so they "are not able to touch" the city of perfect "awakening". "When" the paths of "giving and so forth" "are perfectly embraced by" the "wisdom" that realizes the three spheres as not truly existent, "at that time" "they", giving and so forth, "attain eyes", "attain the name of these perfections", and easily cause one to go to or attain the city of omniscience.

Having thus taught the manner of dedication extensively, to summarize it is stated: Since the ways of pure and impure dedication are as previously explained, one should "thus" understand the faults and qualities and train in unmistaken "thorough dedication". With the gnosis that unmistakenly realizes and knows the rejoicing of "those" Victors, the perfectly complete "Buddhas", the virtues to be dedicated, and the manner of dedication, etc., they know whatever is the essence or aspect of dedication conventionally, whatever infallible result arises from it and what it is like, and what their nature of ultimate non-apprehension is like. Path of meditation of accomplishment. Tenth, to teach the path of meditation of accomplishment, it is said in the Ornament: From "Its essence, supremacy..." up to "...directing it, is of great purpose." The definition of the path of meditation of accomplishment is: any undefiled Mahayana subsequent clear realization that establishes the lasting result of the ultimate realization which is to be attained by oneself. When divided, there are five: the essence of that path of meditation of accomplishment, the supremacy of the path of meditation of accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom, that path of meditation not constructing all phenomena as truly established, that path of meditation directing all phenomena toward lacking the apprehension of true establishment, and the great purpose of attaining Buddhahood as the result of that path of meditation. Its boundaries are from the first to the tenth ground. To teach such a path of meditation of accomplishment, the four verses beginning with "Blind without a guide..." teach what is called supremacy among the five paths of meditation of accomplishment. Furthermore, "for example", even if "a hundred million" "blind" people lacking eyes, without a "guide" or leader to lead them on the path, assemble together, if they "do not see" and do not know the "way" to go to the "city", then "how could they" enter that path and "enter the city"? "There is no way" that could happen.

heading: **སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: For example regarding those, even if the work of painting figures such as a king has been completely painted in all other respects, if only the eyes are absent or missing, then as long as the eyes are not painted, the painting is incomplete, so one does not receive wages or a reward. Therefore, having gained certainty in how this very wisdom that realizes emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects is the supreme essence of the Mahayana path, those of the supreme vehicle's disposition should actualize that very excellent path within their own mindstreams through hearing, contemplating, and meditating. "When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". For example, "space" is merely the negation of obstruction and contact, but because it has no form that acts as its own essence, it "does not abide in anything" at all; it is "like that".

[3-134] translation already produced for this document:
Having thus taught the manner of dedication extensively, to summarize it is stated: Since the ways of pure and impure dedication are as previously explained, one should "thus" understand the faults and qualities and train in unmistaken "thorough dedication". How? With the gnosis that unmistakenly realizes and knows the rejoicing of "those" Victors, the perfectly complete "Buddhas", the virtues to be dedicated, and the manner of dedication, etc., they know whatever is the essence or aspect of dedication conventionally, whatever infallible result arises from it and what it is like, and what their nature of ultimate non-apprehension is like. Having realized their status just as it is, regarding how they rejoice and dedicate, one thinks: "I too shall rejoice in accordance with that and make such a thorough dedication." By thinking this and dedicating, even if one is unskilled in how to dedicate oneself, because one dedicates in accordance with how the Victors dedicate, it is entirely pure dedication. As it is said in the Aspiration of Good Conduct, "Just as the hero Mañjuśrī knows..." and so forth. To teach the result of dedicating "thus": If one "thoroughly dedicates" all the merit of oneself and others to great "awakening" by way of being embraced by the wisdom that realizes them as non-apprehendable "just as it was explained", it is a perfectly pure dedication, akin to "good food without poison", and its result is not abandoning or attaining Buddhahood, and one is unmistakenly speaking the Mahayana Dharma "spoken by the Victor".

heading: **སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: At that time, in order to teach that manifest adherence to the dharmadhātu as true is also a mistake, it is said: "If", even though embraced by special skillful means, being bound by sign-grasping, one "wanders" through adhering as true to the object, emptiness, thinking "I will engage in this perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Jinas," and has a mind of manifest adherence as true, thinking "I will liberate a hundred million sentient beings who touch suffering or are tormented by suffering from their suffering," then since they perceive self and other sentient beings as true, "that bodhisattva" with complete conceptualization "is called one with apprehension"; "such as this" is "not engaging in the supreme" or genuine "perfection of wisdom." In the Eight Thousand, it is said: "The perfection of wisdom is that which illuminates," and so forth. After this, although the perfectly pure path of meditation should be taught, as it is said in the Ornament: "Relying on Buddhas, giving and so forth," one needs to know the two causes of the arising and non-arising of the perfectly pure path of meditation, so first, to teach the cause of its arising, the meaning of the one verse taught beginning with "Whatever bodhisattva..." is: "Whatever bodhisattva" has "pleased the Tathāgatas" in "previous" lifetimes and, when "engaging in the conduct of a conqueror's son," engages in conduct by means of respectfully listening to, holding, and contemplating this profound sutra of the perfection of wisdom, they, "born now in this world," by the power of past latencies and excellent causes, become skilled in the meaning of the perfection of wisdom and "free from doubt" or hesitation "regarding the profound meaning," and "as soon as they hear this" sutra, that person generates the perception of the Teacher, thinking "I have seen the Teacher," and by that cause, they will "swiftly realize" the perfectly pure path of meditation, the "great peace" of awakening. Thus it is said.

"When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". For example, "space" is merely the negation of obstruction and contact, but because it has no form that acts as its own essence, it "does not abide in anything" at all; it is "like that".

heading: **སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: To teach the cause of non-arising, the two verses beginning with "When practicing previously..." are taught. The meaning is: "Whatever bodhisattva", "when" engaging in the conduct of a conqueror's son "previously", has "honored" "many hundreds of millions of Buddhas" and "accumulated merit" by offering vast requisites and so forth, but has not engaged in hearing, contemplating, and so forth regarding the perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Jinas, and lacking faith, has "not made aspirations" to realize its meaning, then even if they have attained a human body "now", upon hearing this profound sutra of the perfection of wisdom, "at that moment", "that one of small intellect" who is "unable to realize the profound meaning" "abandons" this sutra of the perfection of wisdom and does not hold it; and because by abandoning it they have also abandoned the jewel of the Buddha, and become devoid of the refuge of the holy Dharma and the companionship of the noble Sangha, "they go to the Avīci hell" and will "experience suffering for an eon" and so forth; thus limitless disadvantages are taught. Thus it is said.

Path of meditation of accomplishment. Tenth, to teach the path of meditation of accomplishment, it is said in the Ornament: From "Its essence, supremacy..." up to "...directing it, is of great purpose." The definition of the path of meditation of accomplishment is: any undefiled Mahayana subsequent clear realization that establishes the lasting result of the ultimate realization which is to be attained by oneself. When divided, there are five: the essence of that path of meditation of accomplishment, the supremacy of the path of meditation of accomplishment of the perfection of wisdom, that path of meditation not constructing all phenomena as truly established, that path of meditation directing all phenomena toward lacking the apprehension of true establishment, and the great purpose of attaining Buddhahood as the result of that path of meditation. Its boundaries are from the first to the tenth ground. To teach such a path of meditation of accomplishment, the four verses beginning with "Blind without a guide..." teach what is called supremacy among the five paths of meditation of accomplishment. Furthermore, "for example", even if "a hundred million" "blind" people lacking eyes, without a "guide" or leader to lead them on the path, assemble together, if they "do not see" and do not know the "way" to go to the "city", then "how could they" enter that path and "enter the city"? "There is no way" that could happen.

For example regarding those, even if the work of painting figures such as a king has been completely painted in all other respects, if only the eyes are absent or missing, then as long as the eyes are not painted, the painting is incomplete, so one does not receive wages or a reward. Therefore, having gained certainty in how this very wisdom that realizes emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects is the supreme essence of the Mahayana path, those of the supreme vehicle's disposition should actualize that very excellent path within their own mindstreams through hearing, contemplating, and meditating. "When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". For example, "space" is merely the negation of obstruction and contact, but because it has no form that acts as its own essence, it "does not abide in anything" at all; it is "like that".

heading: **སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
translation: Having summarized the meaning of arising and non-arising, the instruction with an example that it is proper to train in the sutra of the perfection of wisdom with faith and respect is: Because the benefits and disadvantages of having or not having faith in the perfection of wisdom are like that, "if" one desires to "touch" or attain the supreme "exalted wisdom of a Buddha," one "should generate faith in this mother of the Jinas" and engage in it through hearing, contemplating, and meditating; thus the disciples of future generations are instructed out of compassion. The reason why this is necessary is that, "now", having met the Buddha's teachings which are like an "island of jewels", and in this time of having the protection of spiritual friends, one must make it meaningful: "for example, if merchants go to an island of jewels", it is improper if they deplete their previous merchandise and, without finding any jewels at all, "return empty-handed again", because there is no greater loss or worse situation than that. Therefore, fortunate ones should rely on joyous effort to accomplish the two goals upon a support of leisure, like the continuous flow of a river. This is the commentary on the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Hell, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled The Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate and Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

དེ་དག་དཔེ་ཇི་ལྟར་ན་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་རི་མོའི་ལས་ནི་གཞན་རྣམས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པར་བྲིས་ཟིན་ནའང་དེ་ལ་མིག་གཅིག་ཁོ་ན་མེད་པ་སྟེ་མ་ཚང་ན། ཇི་སྲིད་མིག་མ་བྲིས་པར་རི་མོ་ཡོངས་སུ་མ་རྫོགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་གླའམ་རྔན་པ་མི་ཐོབ་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །དེས་ན་རྣམ་ཀུན་མཆོག་ལྡན་གྱི་སྟོང་ཉིད་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཉིད་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ལམ་གྱི་སྙིང་པོ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་ཡིན་པའི་ཚུལ་ལ་ངེས་པ་རྙེད་ནས་ཐེག་པ་མཆོག་གི་རིགས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཐོས་བསམ་སྒོམ་པས་རང་རྒྱུད་ལ་ལམ་བཟང་དེ་ཉིད་མངོན་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཞིག་བྱའོ། །གང་གི་ཚེ་འདུས་བྱས་ཁམས་གསུམ་དང་འདུས་མ་བྱས་ཏེ་སྟོངཉིད་དང༌། དཀར་པོ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་དགེ་བ་དང་ནག་པོ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་དགེ་བ་མན་ཆད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་གནས་ལུགས་ལ་དཔྱོད་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་བརྟགས་ཤིང་དཔྱད་དེ་མཚན་འཛིན་གྱི་དམིགས་བཏད་རྣམ་པར་གཤིག་ནས་དེ་དག་ལ་རང་ངོས་ནས་གྲུབ་པ་རྡུལ་ཕྲ་རབ་ཙམ་ཡང་མི་དམིགས་ཤིང་མེད་པར་རྟོགས་པ་དེའི་ཚེ། འཇིག་རྟེན་དག་ན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གྲངས་འགྲོ་སྟེ། དཔེར་ན་ནམ་མཁའ་ནི་ཐོག་རེག་བཀག་ཙམ་ཡིན་གྱི་རང་གི་ངོ་བོར་གྱུར་པའི་གཟུགས་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་གང་ལའང་ཅུང་ཟད་རྟེན་དེ་མི་གནས་པ་དེ་དང་འདྲའོ། །

For example regarding those, even if the work of painting figures such as a king has been completely painted in all other respects, if only the eyes are absent or missing, then as long as the eyes are not painted, the painting is incomplete, so one does not receive wages or a reward. Therefore, having gained certainty in how this very wisdom that realizes emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects is the supreme essence of the Mahayana path, those of the supreme vehicle's disposition should actualize that very excellent path within their own mindstreams through hearing, contemplating, and meditating. "When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". For example, "space" is merely the negation of obstruction and contact, but because it has no form that acts as its own essence, it "does not abide in anything" at all; it is "like that".

དེའི་ཚེ་ཆོས་དབྱིངས་ལ་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པའང་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་བསྟན་པའི་ཕྱིར་གསུངས་པ། གལ་ཏེ་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱིས་ཟིན་ཀྱང་མཚན་འཛིན་གྱིས་བཅིང་ནས་བདག་ནི་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ལ་སྤྱད་པར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་ཡུལ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པས་འཕྱན་ཞིང་། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་རེག་བའམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱིས་མནར་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས་དགྲོལ་ལོ་ཞེས་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པའི་སེམས་ཡོད་ན་བདག་དང་གཞན་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བདེན་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ནི་དམིགས་པ་ཅན་ཞེས་བྱ་སྟེ། འདི་ལྟ་བུ་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་གམ་རྣལ་མ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །བརྒྱད་སྟོང་པ་ལས། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ནི་སྣང་བར་བགྱི་བ་ལགས་སོ་ཞེས་སོགས་གསུངས་སོ། །འདིའི་འོག་ཏུ་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསྟན་དགོས་ཀྱང་། རྒྱན་ལས། སངས་རྒྱས་བསྟེན་དང་སྦྱིན་སོགས་དང་ཞེས་སོགས་གསུངས་པ་ལྟར་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྐྱེ་བ་དང་མི་སྐྱེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་གཉིས་ཤེས་དགོས་པས་དང་པོར་སྐྱེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་སྟོན་པར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གསུངས་པའི་དོན་ནི། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་ཀྱི་སྐྱེ་བ་རྣམས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་མཉེས་པར་བྱས་ཤིང་རྒྱལ་སྲས་ཀྱི་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཚེ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཟབ་མོའི་མདོ་འདིར་གུས་པས་ཉན་ཅིང་འཛིན་ལ་སེམས་པ་སོགས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་དག་འཇིག་རྟེན་འདིར་ད་ལྟར་སྐྱེས་ནས་སྔོན་གྱིས་བག་ཆགས་དང་རྒྱུ་བཟང་བའི་དབང་གིས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ལ་མཁས་པ་དང་ཟབ་མོའི་དོན་ལ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མམ་སོམ་ཉི་མེད་པར་གྱུར་ནས་མདོ་འདི་ཐོས་མ་ཐག་ཏུ་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེས་ནི་བདག་གིས་སྟོན་པ་མཐོང་ངོ་སྙམ་དུ་སྟོན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། རྒྱུ་དེས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཞི་བ་ཆེན་པོ་མྱུར་དུ་རྟོགས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཞེས་སོ། །

At that time, in order to teach that manifest adherence to the dharmadhātu as true is also a mistake, it is said: "If", even though embraced by special skillful means, being bound by sign-grasping, one "wanders" through adhering as true to the object, emptiness, thinking "I will engage in this perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Jinas," and has a mind of manifest adherence as true, thinking "I will liberate a hundred million sentient beings who touch suffering or are tormented by suffering from their suffering," then since they perceive self and other sentient beings as true, "that bodhisattva" with complete conceptualization "is called one with apprehension"; "such as this" is "not engaging in the supreme" or genuine "perfection of wisdom." In the Eight Thousand, it is said: "The perfection of wisdom is that which illuminates," and so forth. After this, although the perfectly pure path of meditation should be taught, as it is said in the Ornament: "Relying on Buddhas, giving and so forth," one needs to know the two causes of the arising and non-arising of the perfectly pure path of meditation, so first, to teach the cause of its arising, the meaning of the one verse taught beginning with "Whatever bodhisattva..." is: "Whatever bodhisattva" has "pleased the Tathāgatas" in "previous" lifetimes and, when "engaging in the conduct of a conqueror's son," engages in conduct by means of respectfully listening to, holding, and contemplating this profound sutra of the perfection of wisdom, they, "born now in this world," by the power of past latencies and excellent causes, become skilled in the meaning of the perfection of wisdom and "free from doubt" or hesitation "regarding the profound meaning," and "as soon as they hear this" sutra, that person generates the perception of the Teacher, thinking "I have seen the Teacher," and by that cause, they will "swiftly realize" the perfectly pure path of meditation, the "great peace" of awakening. Thus it is said.

To teach the cause of non-arising, the two verses beginning with "When practicing previously..." are taught. The meaning is: "Whatever bodhisattva", "when" engaging in the conduct of a conqueror's son "previously", has "honored" "many hundreds of millions of Buddhas" and "accumulated merit" by offering vast requisites and so forth, but has not engaged in hearing, contemplating, and so forth regarding the perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Jinas, and lacking faith, has "not made aspirations" to realize its meaning, then even if they have attained a human body "now", upon hearing this profound sutra of the perfection of wisdom, "at that moment", "that one of small intellect" who is "unable to realize the profound meaning" "abandons" this sutra of the perfection of wisdom and does not hold it; and because by abandoning it they have also abandoned the jewel of the Buddha, and become devoid of the refuge of the holy Dharma and the companionship of the noble Sangha, "they go to the Avīci hell" and will "experience suffering for an eon" and so forth; thus limitless disadvantages are taught. Thus it is said.

heading: **རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ།**
source: རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ།བཅུ་གཅིག་པ་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་ནི། རྒྱན་ལས། འབྲས་བུ་དག་པ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས། །ནས། སོགས་པའི་ལམ་ནི་དག་པ་ཡིན། །ཞེས་གསུངས། ཟག་པ་མེད་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་གང་ཞིག །རང་གི་ཐོབ་བྱར་གྱུར་པའི་སྤངས་པ་མཐར་ཐུག་གི་ལག་རྗེས་འཇོག་བྱེད་དེ༑ རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་ན། སྒོམ་སྤངས་སྐོར་དགུའི་གཉེན་པོ་རྣམ་དག་སྒྲོམ་ལམ་ཆུང་ངུའི་ནས་དེ་ཆེན་པོའི་ཆེན་པོའི་བར་དགུ་ཡོད། སྒྲུབ་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་དང་འདི་གཉིས་ལྡོག་པ་ཐ་དད་ཙམ་ལས་དོན་གཅིག་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ས་མཚམས་ས་དང་པོ་ནས་ས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། དེ་འདྲའི་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་ལ་གཉིས་ལས་
translation: The perfectly pure path of meditation. Eleventh, the perfectly pure path of meditation: In the Ornament, it is said: "The purity of the result is form and so forth..." up to "...and so forth is the pure path." The defining characteristic of the perfectly pure path of meditation is: whatever uncontaminated Mahayana subsequent clear realization establishes the imprint of the ultimate abandonment that is to be attained by oneself. When divided, there are nine perfectly pure paths of meditation, which are the antidotes to the nine cycles of objects abandoned by meditation, ranging from the small of the small to the great of the great. The meditative path of achievement and this perfectly pure path of meditation are the same in meaning, merely being conceptually distinct. For example regarding those, even if the work of painting figures such as a king has been completely painted in all other respects, if only the eyes are absent or missing, then as long as the eyes are not painted, the painting is incomplete, so one does not receive wages or a reward. Therefore, having gained certainty in how this very wisdom that realizes emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects is the supreme essence of the Mahayana path, those of the supreme vehicle's disposition should actualize that very excellent path within their own mindstreams through hearing, contemplating, and meditating. "When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". heading: **སྤྱིར་བསྟན་པ།**
translation: General teaching. First, the general teaching: It is the one verse line beginning with "The purity of form" and so forth. The meaning is: Furthermore, because stains do not enter into the abiding nature, all phenomena subsumed by the aggregates, elements, and sense sources, such as form and so forth, are primordially perfectly pure and naturally luminous; however, because they are apprehended mistakenly by the ignorance of true-grasping, afflictions such as attachment arise, so they are called adventitious stains. As long as one does not clearly see the abiding nature because it is obscured by true-grasping, form and so forth are said to be perfectly impure. When the obscuring stains are purified and one clearly sees the abiding nature, because of the vital point that the fact that the abiding nature of form and so forth is primordially perfectly pure without being corrupted by stains matches one's own mode of seeing, the object—the purity of the aggregate of form and so forth from stains—and the subject—the purity of the result, ranging from the path of release of the path of seeing, which is the perfection of wisdom or the result of asceticism, up to Buddhahood—have become one in meaning. Therefore, since the purity of the result cannot be posited separately from the "purity of form" and so forth, one should know that those two cannot be conceptually divided and are one in essence; and in dependence on that mode of the purity of the result, at that time it is said that the object, form, is pure. For example, when falling hairs appear upon a form, at that time it is said that the form is not clear, but when the cause of delusion, visual aberration and so forth, is eliminated, it is said that the form is clear; it is like that.

དེ་དག་དཔེ་ཇི་ལྟར་ན་རྒྱལ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་རི་མོའི་ལས་ནི་གཞན་རྣམས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པར་བྲིས་ཟིན་ནའང་དེ་ལ་མིག་གཅིག་ཁོ་ན་མེད་པ་སྟེ་མ་ཚང་ན། ཇི་སྲིད་མིག་མ་བྲིས་པར་རི་མོ་ཡོངས་སུ་མ་རྫོགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་གླའམ་རྔན་པ་མི་ཐོབ་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །དེས་ན་རྣམ་ཀུན་མཆོག་ལྡན་གྱི་སྟོང་ཉིད་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཉིད་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ལམ་གྱི་སྙིང་པོ་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་ཡིན་པའི་ཚུལ་ལ་ངེས་པ་རྙེད་ནས་ཐེག་པ་མཆོག་གི་རིགས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཐོས་བསམ་སྒོམ་པས་རང་རྒྱུད་ལ་ལམ་བཟང་དེ་ཉིད་མངོན་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཞིག་བྱའོ། །གང་གི་ཚེ་འདུས་བྱས་ཁམས་གསུམ་དང་འདུས་མ་བྱས་ཏེ་སྟོངཉིད་དང༌། དཀར་པོ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་དགེ་བ་དང་ནག་པོ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་དགེ་བ་མན་ཆད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་གནས་ལུགས་ལ་དཔྱོད་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་བརྟགས་ཤིང་དཔྱད་དེ་མཚན་འཛིན་གྱི་དམིགས་བཏད་རྣམ་པར་གཤིག་ནས་དེ་དག་ལ་རང་ངོས་ནས་གྲུབ་པ་རྡུལ་ཕྲ་རབ་ཙམ་ཡང་མི་དམིགས་ཤིང་མེད་པར་རྟོགས་པ་དེའི་ཚེ། འཇིག་རྟེན་དག་ན་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གྲངས་འགྲོ་སྟེ། དཔེར་ན་ནམ་མཁའ་ནི་ཐོག་རེག་བཀག་ཙམ་ཡིན་གྱི་རང་གི་ངོ་བོར་གྱུར་པའི་གཟུགས་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་གང་ལའང་ཅུང་ཟད་རྟེན་དེ་མི་གནས་པ་དེ་དང་འདྲའོ། །

For example regarding those, even if the work of painting figures such as a king has been completely painted in all other respects, if only the eyes are absent or missing, then as long as the eyes are not painted, the painting is incomplete, so one does not receive wages or a reward. Therefore, having gained certainty in how this very wisdom that realizes emptiness endowed with all supreme aspects is the supreme essence of the Mahayana path, those of the supreme vehicle's disposition should actualize that very excellent path within their own mindstreams through hearing, contemplating, and meditating. "When", regarding "conditioned" phenomena—the three realms—and "unconditioned" phenomena—emptiness—and "white" phenomena—virtue embraced by bodhicitta—and "black" phenomena—phenomena from virtue in the mindstreams of śrāvakas and below—having examined and investigated them with the "wisdom" that discerns the abiding nature, and having "completely destroyed" the focal target of sign-grasping, one realizes that not even a mere subtle "particle" of them is established from its own side and they are "unapprehendable" and non-existent, at "that time", it "is counted as the perfection of wisdom in the worlds". For example, "space" is merely the negation of obstruction and contact, but because it has no form that acts as its own essence, it "does not abide in anything" at all; it is "like that".

དེའི་ཚེ་ཆོས་དབྱིངས་ལ་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པའང་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་བསྟན་པའི་ཕྱིར་གསུངས་པ། གལ་ཏེ་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱིས་ཟིན་ཀྱང་མཚན་འཛིན་གྱིས་བཅིང་ནས་བདག་ནི་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ལ་སྤྱད་པར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་ཡུལ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པས་འཕྱན་ཞིང་། སེམས་ཅན་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་རེག་བའམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱིས་མནར་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་པོ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལས་དགྲོལ་ལོ་ཞེས་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པའི་སེམས་ཡོད་ན་བདག་དང་གཞན་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བདེན་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ནི་དམིགས་པ་ཅན་ཞེས་བྱ་སྟེ། འདི་ལྟ་བུ་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་གམ་རྣལ་མ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །བརྒྱད་སྟོང་པ་ལས། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ནི་སྣང་བར་བགྱི་བ་ལགས་སོ་ཞེས་སོགས་གསུངས་སོ། །འདིའི་འོག་ཏུ་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསྟན་དགོས་ཀྱང་། རྒྱན་ལས། སངས་རྒྱས་བསྟེན་དང་སྦྱིན་སོགས་དང་ཞེས་སོགས་གསུངས་པ་ལྟར་རྣམ་དག་སྒོམ་ལམ་སྐྱེ་བ་དང་མི་སྐྱེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་གཉིས་ཤེས་དགོས་པས་དང་པོར་སྐྱེ་བའི་རྒྱུ་སྟོན་པར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གསུངས་པའི་དོན་ནི། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་ཀྱི་སྐྱེ་བ་རྣམས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་མཉེས་པར་བྱས་ཤིང་རྒྱལ་སྲས་ཀྱི་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཚེ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཟབ་མོའི་མདོ་འདིར་གུས་པས་ཉན་ཅིང་འཛིན་ལ་སེམས་པ་སོགས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་སྤྱད་པ་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་དག་འཇིག་རྟེན་འདིར་ད་ལྟར་སྐྱེས་ནས་སྔོན་གྱིས་བག་ཆགས་དང་རྒྱུ་བཟང་བའི་དབང་གིས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ལ་མཁས་པ་དང་ཟབ་མོའི་དོན་ལ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མམ་སོམ་ཉི་མེད་པར་གྱུར་ནས་མདོ་འདི་ཐོས་མ་ཐག་ཏུ་སྐྱེས་བུ་དེས་ནི་བདག་གིས་སྟོན་པ་མཐོང་ངོ་སྙམ་དུ་སྟོན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱེད་ཅིང་། རྒྱུ་དེས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཞི་བ་ཆེན་པོ་མྱུར་དུ་རྟོགས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །ཞེས་སོ། །

At that time, in order to teach that manifest adherence to the dharmadhātu as true is also a mistake, it is said: "If", even though embraced by special skillful means, being bound by sign-grasping, one "wanders" through adhering as true to the object, emptiness, thinking "I will engage in this perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Jinas," and has a mind of manifest adherence as true, thinking "I will liberate a hundred million sentient beings who touch suffering or are tormented by suffering from their suffering," then since they perceive self and other sentient beings as true, "that bodhisattva" with complete conceptualization "is called one with apprehension"; "such as this" is "not engaging in the supreme" or genuine "perfection of wisdom." In the Eight Thousand, it is said: "The perfection of wisdom is that which illuminates," and so forth. After this, although the perfectly pure path of meditation should be taught, as it is said in the Ornament: "Relying on Buddhas, giving and so forth," one needs to know the two causes of the arising and non-arising of the perfectly pure path of meditation, so first, to teach the cause of its arising, the meaning of the one verse taught beginning with "Whatever bodhisattva..." is: "Whatever bodhisattva" has "pleased the Tathāgatas" in "previous" lifetimes and, when "engaging in the conduct of a conqueror's son," engages in conduct by means of respectfully listening to, holding, and contemplating this profound sutra of the perfection of wisdom, they, "born now in this world," by the power of past latencies and excellent causes, become skilled in the meaning of the perfection of wisdom and "free from doubt" or hesitation "regarding the profound meaning," and "as soon as they hear this" sutra, that person generates the perception of the Teacher, thinking "I have seen the Teacher," and by that cause, they will "swiftly realize" the perfectly pure path of meditation, the "great peace" of awakening. Thus it is said.

heading: **རྣམ་དག་བྱེ་བྲག་འཆད་པ།**
translation: Explaining the specific perfect purities. Second, regarding explaining the specific perfect purities, three verse lines beginning with "the purity of the result, form" and so forth are spoken. Furthermore, as is said in the Ornament: "Because of being weakened by the three paths concerning afflictions and objects of knowledge, it is the purity of disciples, rhinoceros-like ones, and sons of the Jinas; for a Buddha, it is thoroughly [pure] in all aspects." Accordingly, because Śrāvaka Arhats have abandoned merely the afflictive obscurations, and rhinoceros-like Pratyekabuddha Arhats have abandoned the afflictive obscurations and one part of the cognitive obscurations—merely the conceptuality of the apprehended—their perfect purity is partial; it is not thoroughly pure. Because the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a noble Buddha have abandoned the two obscurations without remainder, it is thoroughly perfect purity or ultimate perfect purity. Just as it was explained previously that "the purity of form" and "the purity of the result" are one in essence, similarly, when the stains of the objects to be abandoned allocated to the uninterrupted path that acts as the attainer of the path of release, which is the result, are purified, its object, form and so forth, must also be posited as being purified by those very stains in one's mind-stream. The subject isolated from the single object of purification—which is the perfection of wisdom or the perfectly pure result—and the perfectly pure object, form and so forth, are indivisible in essence and cannot be conceptually divided as different. Likewise, when the nine cycles of the Mahayana path of meditation from the second ground up to the tenth ground act as the direct antidotes to their respective allocated objects to be abandoned—the conceptuality of the apprehended and the apprehender abandoned by meditation, from the great up to the small of the small—and abandon the two obscurations without remainder, it becomes the thoroughly perfectly pure result subsumed by the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a Buddha, the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, these three purities—the ultimate purity which is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, the purity of attaining the cessations and paths which are the respective results of the path of training, and the purity of the phenomena of the bases (the aggregates, elements, and sense sources such as form and so forth)—merely appear as different conventionally; ultimately, just as the element of space has no divisions into different essences, the naturally perfectly pure dharmadhatu is indivisible into different essences, and cannot even be conceptually separated as different, because all dharmadhatus are of a single nature. Thus, having finished teaching the eleven phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the path, the summary of the chapter is: This is the commentary on the second chapter from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled The Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate and Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

Having summarized the meaning of arising and non-arising, the instruction with an example that it is proper to train in the sutra of the perfection of wisdom with faith and respect is: Because the benefits and disadvantages of having or not having faith in the perfection of wisdom are like that, "if" one desires to "touch" or attain the supreme "exalted wisdom of a Buddha," one "should generate faith in this mother of the Jinas" and engage in it through hearing, contemplating, and meditating; thus the disciples of future generations are instructed out of compassion. The reason why this is necessary is that, "now", having met the Buddha's teachings which are like an "island of jewels", and in this time of having the protection of spiritual friends, one must make it meaningful: "for example, if merchants go to an island of jewels", it is improper if they deplete their previous merchandise and, without finding any jewels at all, "return empty-handed again", because there is no greater loss or worse situation than that. Therefore, fortunate ones should rely on joyous effort to accomplish the two goals upon a support of leisure, like the continuous flow of a river. This is the commentary on the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Hell, from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled The Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate and Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

General teaching. First, the general teaching: It is the one verse line beginning with "The purity of form" and so forth. The meaning is: Furthermore, because stains do not enter into the abiding nature, all phenomena subsumed by the aggregates, elements, and sense sources, such as form and so forth, are primordially perfectly pure and naturally luminous; however, because they are apprehended mistakenly by the ignorance of true-grasping, afflictions such as attachment arise, so they are called adventitious stains. As long as one does not clearly see the abiding nature because it is obscured by true-grasping, form and so forth are said to be perfectly impure. When the obscuring stains are purified and one clearly sees the abiding nature, because of the vital point that the fact that the abiding nature of form and so forth is primordially perfectly pure without being corrupted by stains matches one's own mode of seeing, the object—the purity of the aggregate of form and so forth from stains—and the subject—the purity of the result, ranging from the path of release of the path of seeing, which is the perfection of wisdom or the result of asceticism, up to Buddhahood—have become one in meaning. Therefore, since the purity of the result cannot be posited separately from the "purity of form" and so forth, one should know that those two cannot be conceptually divided and are one in essence; and in dependence on that mode of the purity of the result, at that time it is said that the object, form, is pure. For example, when falling hairs appear upon a form, at that time it is said that the form is not clear, but when the cause of delusion, visual aberration and so forth, is eliminated, it is said that the form is clear; it is like that.

heading: གཞི་ཤེས།
source: གཞི་ཤེས།དེ་ལྟར་རྒྱུ་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས་ལམ་ཤེས་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པ་ལ། མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་པའི་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་། །ནས། དེ་འདྲ་ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་རྒྱུད་ལྡན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པ་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཞི་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ། དགུ་ཡོད་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། སྦྱོར་བའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་དགུ་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། དང་པོ་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར་ཚུལ་རོལ་ཕ་རོལ་མཐའ་ལ་མིན། །ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང་། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་སྲིད་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་དང་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་ཞི་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་འཕགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེན། དེར་གྱུར་བའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་སྒོམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྔ་མ་དང་འདྲ།
translation: Knowledge of the bases. Thus, having finished explaining the cause, the knowledge of the path, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases which is that which perfectly purifies the knowledge of the path: it is said in the Ornament of Clear Realization: "Through knowledge one does not abide in existence..." up to "...is asserted as the knowledge of all those [bases]." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases is: an exalted wisdom in the mind-stream of a person who possesses it, which is embraced by the wisdom that directly realizes selflessness, and which abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana. Regarding the phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases, there are nine: the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge; the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion; the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class; the preparation of the knowledge of the bases; the equality of the mode of apprehension of the preparation; and the path of seeing, since there are nine. To teach the first two, there is one verse beginning with "Not on the near shore, the far shore, or the limits..." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge is: a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of existence in relation to the conventional bases. That and the knowledge of the path that knows the path of the Śrāvakas are one in meaning. If divided, there are three: the Mahayana path of seeing, path of meditation, and path of no more learning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion is: a knowledge in a noble being's mind-stream that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of peace in relation to the conventional bases. That and a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization of exceptional methods are one in meaning. If divided, there are three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning of the Mahayana that become it. Its boundaries are like the previous one.

སྤྱིར་བསྟན་པ།དང་པོ་སྤྱིར་བསྟན་པ་ནི། གཟུགས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་རྐང་གཅིག་སྟེ། དོན་ནི། དེའང་དྲི་མ་གནས་ལུགས་ལ་མ་ཞུགས་པས་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕུང་ཁམས་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་ཀྱིས་བསྡུས་པའི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་གདོད་མ་ནས་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་དང་། རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་འོད་གསལ་བ་ཡིན་ཀྱང་བདེན་འཛིན་གྱི་མ་རིག་པས་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་བཟུང་ནས་ཆགས་སོགས་ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམས་སྐྱེས་པ་ཡིན་པས་དྲི་མ་བློ་བུར་བ་ཟེར་ཞིང་། བདེན་འཛིན་གྱིས་སྒྲིབ་ནས་གནས་ལུགས་གསལ་བར་མ་མཐོང་བའི་བར་དུ་གཟུགས་སོགས་རྣམ་པར་མ་དག་པ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་ལ། སྒྲིབ་བྱེད་ཀྱི་དྲི་མ་དག་ནས་གནས་ལུགས་གསལ་བར་མཐོང་བའི་ཚེ་གཟུགས་སོགས་ཀྱི་གནས་ལུགས་ལ་དྲི་མས་སླད་མ་ཞུགས་པར་གདོན་ནས་རྣམ་བར་དག་ཡོད་པ་དེ་དང་། རང་གི་མཐོང་ཚུལ་གཉིས་མཐུན་སོང་པའི་གནད་ཀྱིས་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སོགས་དྲི་མས་དག་པ་དང་། ཡུལ་ཅན་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ནམ་དགེ་སྦྱོང་ཚུལ་གྱི་འབྲས་བུ་མཐོང་ལམ་རྣམ་གྲོལ་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བར་གྱི་འབྲས་བུ་དག་པ་གཉིས་དོན་གཅིག་ཏུ་སོང་བ་ཡིན་ལ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་གཟུགས་སོགས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་དེ་ལས་ལོགས་ཤིག་ཏུ་འབྲས་བུ་དག་པ་འཇོག་ཏུ་མེད་པས་དེ་གཉིས་བློས་སོ་སོར་བཅད་དུ་མེད་པ་ངོ་བོ་གཅིག་པར་རིག་པར་བྱ་ཞིང་།འབྲས་བུ་དག་ཚུལ་དེ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་དེའི་ཚེ་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་དག་པ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་སྟེང་ན་སྐྲ་བཤད་འབབ་པར་སྣང་བ་དེའི་ཚེ་གཟུགས་མི་གསལ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་ལ། འཁྲུལ་རྒྱུ་རབ་རིབ་སོགས་ལག་པའི་ཚེ་གཟུགས་གསལ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པ་བཞིན་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །

General teaching. First, the general teaching: It is the one verse line beginning with "The purity of form" and so forth. The meaning is: Furthermore, because stains do not enter into the abiding nature, all phenomena subsumed by the aggregates, elements, and sense sources, such as form and so forth, are primordially perfectly pure and naturally luminous; however, because they are apprehended mistakenly by the ignorance of true-grasping, afflictions such as attachment arise, so they are called adventitious stains. As long as one does not clearly see the abiding nature because it is obscured by true-grasping, form and so forth are said to be perfectly impure. When the obscuring stains are purified and one clearly sees the abiding nature, because of the vital point that the fact that the abiding nature of form and so forth is primordially perfectly pure without being corrupted by stains matches one's own mode of seeing, the object—the purity of the aggregate of form and so forth from stains—and the subject—the purity of the result, ranging from the path of release of the path of seeing, which is the perfection of wisdom or the result of asceticism, up to Buddhahood—have become one in meaning. Therefore, since the purity of the result cannot be posited separately from the "purity of form" and so forth, one should know that those two cannot be conceptually divided and are one in essence; and in dependence on that mode of the purity of the result, at that time it is said that the object, form, is pure. For example, when falling hairs appear upon a form, at that time it is said that the form is not clear, but when the cause of delusion, visual aberration and so forth, is eliminated, it is said that the form is clear; it is like that.

རྣམ་དག་བྱེ་བྲག་འཆད་པ། གཉིས་པ་རྣམ་དག་བྱེ་བྲག་འཆད་པ་ལ། འབྲས་བུ་གཟུགས་དག་ཅེས་སོགས་རྐང་བ་གསུམ་གསུངས། དེའང་རྒྱན་ལས། ཉོན་མོངས་ཤེས་བྱ་ལམ་གསུམ་གྱིས། །ཉམས་ཕྱིར་སློབ་མ་བསེ་རུ་དང་། །རྒྱལ་སྲས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་སྟེ། །སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམ་ཀུན་ཤན་ཏུ་བ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་པ་ལྟར་ཉན་ཐོས་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པས་ཉོན་སྒྲིབ་ཙམ་སྤངས་པ་དང་། བསེ་རུ་ལྟ་བུའི་རང་རྒྱལ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་གྱིས་ཉོན་སྒྲིབ་དང་ཤེས་བྱའི་སྒྲིབ་པའི་ཕྱོགས་གཅིག་གཟུང་རྟོག་ཙམ་སྤངས་པས་དེ་དག་གི་རྣམ་དག་ནི་ཕྱོགས་རེ་བ་ཡིན་གྱི་ཤིན་ཏུ་དག་པ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། སངས་རྒྱས་འཕགས་པའི་ཐུགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་འགོག་ལམ་གྱིས་སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་མ་ལུས་པ་སྤངས་པས་རྣམ་དག་ཤིན་ཏུ་པའམ་རྣམ་དག་མཐར་ཐུག་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །སྔརབཤད་པ་ལྟར་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་འབྲས་བུ་དག་པ་གཉིས་ངོ་བོ་གཅིག་ཡིན་པ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འབྲས་བུ་རྣམ་གྲོལ་ལམ་རང་ཐོབ་བྱེད་ཀྱི་བར་ཆད་མེད་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་སྐལ་གྱི་སྤངས་བྱའི་དྲི་མ་དག་པ་ན་དེའི་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པའང་རང་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་དྲི་མ་དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་དག་པར་འཇོག་དགོས་ཏེ། དག་བྱ་གཅིག་གིས་དབེན་པའི་ཡུལ་ཅན་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ནམ་འབྲས་བུ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་དང་། ཡུལ་གཟུགས་སོགས་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་གཉིས་ངོ་བོ་དབྱེར་མེད་ཅིང་ཐ་དད་དུ་བློས་བཅད་དུ་མེད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ས་གཉིས་པ་ནས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་གྱི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསྐོར་དགུས་རང་རང་གི་ངོ་སྐལ་གྱི་སྤངས་བྱ་སྒོམ་སྤངས་བཟུང་འཛིན་གྱི་རྟོག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ནས་ཆུང་ངུའི་ཆུང་ངུའི་བར་གྱི་དངོས་གཉེན་བྱས་ཏེ་སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་མ་ལུས་པ་སྤངས་པ་ན་རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཐུགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་འགོག་ལམ་གྱིས་བསྡུས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཤིན་ཏུ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟར་དག་པ་མཐར་ཐུག་རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་དག་པ་དང་། སློབ་ལམ་གྱིས་སོ་སོའི་འབྲས་པ་འགོག་ལམ་ཐོབ་པའི་དག་པ་དང་། གཞི་གཟུགས་སོགས་ཕུང་ཁམས་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དག་པ་གསུམ་པོ་འདི་དག་ཀྱང་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ཏུ་ཐ་དད་དུ་སྣང་བ་ཙམ་ལས། ཡང་དག་པར་ན་ནམ་མཁའི་ཁམས་ལ་ངོ་བོ་མི་འདྲ་བའི་དབྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དང་མཚུངས་ཏེ་རང་བཞིིན་རྣམ་དག་ཆོས་དབྱིངས་ལ་ངོ་བོ་མི་འདྲ་བ་དབྱེར་མེད་ཅིང་བློས་ཀྱང་ཐ་དད་དུ་བཅད་དུ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཏེ། ཆོསདབྱིངས་ཐམས་ཅད་རིགས་གཅིག་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟར་ལམ་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཆོས་བཅུ་གཅིག་བསྟན་ཟིན་ནས་སྐབས་བསྡུ་བ་ནི། ཡོན་ཏན་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་སྡུད་པ་ཚིགས་བཅད་པའི་འགྲེལ་བ་ཟབ་མོ་རྟེན་འབྱུང་གི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་ནོར་བུའི་སྒྲོན་མེ་སྐལ་བཟང་རེ་སྐོང་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལས་སྐབས་གཉིས་པའི་འགྲེལ་པའོ༎ །།
