Explaining the specific perfect purities. Second, regarding explaining the specific perfect purities, three verse lines beginning with "the purity of the result, form" and so forth are spoken. Furthermore, as is said in the Ornament: "Because of being weakened by the three paths concerning afflictions and objects of knowledge, it is the purity of disciples, rhinoceros-like ones, and sons of the Jinas; for a Buddha, it is thoroughly [pure] in all aspects." Accordingly, because Śrāvaka Arhats have abandoned merely the afflictive obscurations, and rhinoceros-like Pratyekabuddha Arhats have abandoned the afflictive obscurations and one part of the cognitive obscurations—merely the conceptuality of the apprehended—their perfect purity is partial; it is not thoroughly pure. Because the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a noble Buddha have abandoned the two obscurations without remainder, it is thoroughly perfect purity or ultimate perfect purity. Just as it was explained previously that "the purity of form" and "the purity of the result" are one in essence, similarly, when the stains of the objects to be abandoned allocated to the uninterrupted path that acts as the attainer of the path of release, which is the result, are purified, its object, form and so forth, must also be posited as being purified by those very stains in one's mind-stream. The subject isolated from the single object of purification—which is the perfection of wisdom or the perfectly pure result—and the perfectly pure object, form and so forth, are indivisible in essence and cannot be conceptually divided as different. Likewise, when the nine cycles of the Mahayana path of meditation from the second ground up to the tenth ground act as the direct antidotes to their respective allocated objects to be abandoned—the conceptuality of the apprehended and the apprehender abandoned by meditation, from the great up to the small of the small—and abandon the two obscurations without remainder, it becomes the thoroughly perfectly pure result subsumed by the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a Buddha, the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, these three purities—the ultimate purity which is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, the purity of attaining the cessations and paths which are the respective results of the path of training, and the purity of the phenomena of the bases (the aggregates, elements, and sense sources such as form and so forth)—merely appear as different conventionally; ultimately, just as the element of space has no divisions into different essences, the naturally perfectly pure dharmadhatu is indivisible into different essences, and cannot even be conceptually separated as different, because all dharmadhatus are of a single nature. Thus, having finished teaching the eleven phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the path, the summary of the chapter is: This is the commentary on the second chapter from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled The Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate and Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

heading: **ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དང་སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞིལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས།**
translation: The knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge and the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion. To explain those two: not abiding in existence through such knowledge and the knowledge of the path of abiding in peace through compassion, the meaning of the one verse spoken beginning with "The heroes, wherever they act" and so forth is: The heroes, the bodhisattvas, who cannot be swayed by true-grasping and self-cherishing, wherever they act in the domains of samsara, see the faults of samsara; and by abiding in the perfection of wisdom embraced by exceptional means and knowledge, they perfectly pass beyond birth in samsara caused by karma and afflictions without being attached to any domain of samsara in the three realms; and even though they have passed beyond, they do not abide in the one-sided peace of nirvana that is merely liberation from existence like the Śrāvakas, so they do not abide in either of the extremes of existence or peace. Even though they have cleared away the karma and afflictions of powerless birth in existence, by the power of compassion and aspiration they thoroughly demonstrate taking birth in samsara. As it is said in the Sublime Continuum: "Because they are noble, they have eradicated the suffering of sickness, aging, and death." Like that, although they do not have aging, sickness, and death, for the sake of others they demonstrate dying, transmigrating, and so forth, because they are experts who possess exceptional means, such as great compassion and bodhicitta, and exceptional wisdom that realizes existence and peace as empty of true existence. This directly teaches the two knowledges of the path of not abiding in the two extremes of existence and peace, and implicitly teaches the two: the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother due to not being expert in the means of stopping the two extremes of existence and peace, and the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother due to being expert in those means. Also from the Eight Thousand Stanza: "Bhagavan, the perfection of wisdom does not abide on the near shore, it does not abide on the far shore, nor does it abide afar in between the two," and so forth is spoken.

General teaching. First, the general teaching: It is the one verse line beginning with "The purity of form" and so forth. The meaning is: Furthermore, because stains do not enter into the abiding nature, all phenomena subsumed by the aggregates, elements, and sense sources, such as form and so forth, are primordially perfectly pure and naturally luminous; however, because they are apprehended mistakenly by the ignorance of true-grasping, afflictions such as attachment arise, so they are called adventitious stains. As long as one does not clearly see the abiding nature because it is obscured by true-grasping, form and so forth are said to be perfectly impure. When the obscuring stains are purified and one clearly sees the abiding nature, because of the vital point that the fact that the abiding nature of form and so forth is primordially perfectly pure without being corrupted by stains matches one's own mode of seeing, the object—the purity of the aggregate of form and so forth from stains—and the subject—the purity of the result, ranging from the path of release of the path of seeing, which is the perfection of wisdom or the result of asceticism, up to Buddhahood—have become one in meaning. Therefore, since the purity of the result cannot be posited separately from the "purity of form" and so forth, one should know that those two cannot be conceptually divided and are one in essence; and in dependence on that mode of the purity of the result, at that time it is said that the object, form, is pure. For example, when falling hairs appear upon a form, at that time it is said that the form is not clear, but when the cause of delusion, visual aberration and so forth, is eliminated, it is said that the form is clear; it is like that.

Explaining the specific perfect purities. Second, regarding explaining the specific perfect purities, three verse lines beginning with "the purity of the result, form" and so forth are spoken. Furthermore, as is said in the Ornament: "Because of being weakened by the three paths concerning afflictions and objects of knowledge, it is the purity of disciples, rhinoceros-like ones, and sons of the Jinas; for a Buddha, it is thoroughly [pure] in all aspects." Accordingly, because Śrāvaka Arhats have abandoned merely the afflictive obscurations, and rhinoceros-like Pratyekabuddha Arhats have abandoned the afflictive obscurations and one part of the cognitive obscurations—merely the conceptuality of the apprehended—their perfect purity is partial; it is not thoroughly pure. Because the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a noble Buddha have abandoned the two obscurations without remainder, it is thoroughly perfect purity or ultimate perfect purity. Just as it was explained previously that "the purity of form" and "the purity of the result" are one in essence, similarly, when the stains of the objects to be abandoned allocated to the uninterrupted path that acts as the attainer of the path of release, which is the result, are purified, its object, form and so forth, must also be posited as being purified by those very stains in one's mind-stream. The subject isolated from the single object of purification—which is the perfection of wisdom or the perfectly pure result—and the perfectly pure object, form and so forth, are indivisible in essence and cannot be conceptually divided as different. Likewise, when the nine cycles of the Mahayana path of meditation from the second ground up to the tenth ground act as the direct antidotes to their respective allocated objects to be abandoned—the conceptuality of the apprehended and the apprehender abandoned by meditation, from the great up to the small of the small—and abandon the two obscurations without remainder, it becomes the thoroughly perfectly pure result subsumed by the cessations and paths in the mind-stream of a Buddha, the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, these three purities—the ultimate purity which is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, the purity of attaining the cessations and paths which are the respective results of the path of training, and the purity of the phenomena of the bases (the aggregates, elements, and sense sources such as form and so forth)—merely appear as different conventionally; ultimately, just as the element of space has no divisions into different essences, the naturally perfectly pure dharmadhatu is indivisible into different essences, and cannot even be conceptually separated as different, because all dharmadhatus are of a single nature. Thus, having finished teaching the eleven phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the path, the summary of the chapter is: This is the commentary on the second chapter from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection titled The Jewel Lamp that Fulfills the Hopes of the Fortunate and Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

source: འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས།གསུམ་པ་འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས་དེ་ནི་མཚན་མར་དམིགས་སྒ་ོནས། ཐབས་མ་ཡིན་པས་རིང་པ་སྟེ། ཞེས་གསུངས། བཞི་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་བྲལ་ཞིང་བདེན་འཛིན་གྱིས་བཅིང་པ་དེ། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་སློབ་ལམ་གྱི་བར་ན་ཡོད།
translation: The knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother. Third, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother, it is said in the Ornament: "Through the door of apprehending marks, it is distant because of lacking skill in means." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother is: a knowledge of the bases that is separated from great compassion and bound by true-grasping. That and the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Hinayana path of seeing up to the Hinayana path of learning.

གཞི་ཤེས།དེ་ལྟར་རྒྱུ་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས་ལམ་ཤེས་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པ་ལ། མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་པའི་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་། །ནས། དེ་འདྲ་ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་རྒྱུད་ལྡན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པ་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཞི་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ། དགུ་ཡོད་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། སྦྱོར་བའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་དགུ་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། དང་པོ་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར་ཚུལ་རོལ་ཕ་རོལ་མཐའ་ལ་མིན། །ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང་། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་སྲིད་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་དང་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་ཞི་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་འཕགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེན། དེར་གྱུར་བའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་སྒོམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྔ་མ་དང་འདྲ།

Knowledge of the bases. Thus, having finished explaining the cause, the knowledge of the path, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases which is that which perfectly purifies the knowledge of the path: it is said in the Ornament of Clear Realization: "Through knowledge one does not abide in existence..." up to "...is asserted as the knowledge of all those [bases]." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases is: an exalted wisdom in the mind-stream of a person who possesses it, which is embraced by the wisdom that directly realizes selflessness, and which abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana. Regarding the phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases, there are nine: the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge; the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion; the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class; the preparation of the knowledge of the bases; the equality of the mode of apprehension of the preparation; and the path of seeing, since there are nine. To teach the first two, there is one verse beginning with "Not on the near shore, the far shore, or the limits..." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge is: a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of existence in relation to the conventional bases. That and the knowledge of the path that knows the path of the Śrāvakas are one in meaning. If divided, there are three: the Mahayana path of seeing, path of meditation, and path of no more learning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion is: a knowledge in a noble being's mind-stream that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of peace in relation to the conventional bases. That and a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization of exceptional methods are one in meaning. If divided, there are three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning of the Mahayana that become it. Its boundaries are like the previous one.

The knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge and the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion. To explain those two: not abiding in existence through such knowledge and the knowledge of the path of abiding in peace through compassion, the meaning of the one verse spoken beginning with "The heroes, wherever they act" and so forth is: The heroes, the bodhisattvas, who cannot be swayed by true-grasping and self-cherishing, wherever they act in the domains of samsara, see the faults of samsara; and by abiding in the perfection of wisdom embraced by exceptional means and knowledge, they perfectly pass beyond birth in samsara caused by karma and afflictions without being attached to any domain of samsara in the three realms; and even though they have passed beyond, they do not abide in the one-sided peace of nirvana that is merely liberation from existence like the Śrāvakas, so they do not abide in either of the extremes of existence or peace. Even though they have cleared away the karma and afflictions of powerless birth in existence, by the power of compassion and aspiration they thoroughly demonstrate taking birth in samsara. As it is said in the Sublime Continuum: "Because they are noble, they have eradicated the suffering of sickness, aging, and death." Like that, although they do not have aging, sickness, and death, for the sake of others they demonstrate dying, transmigrating, and so forth, because they are experts who possess exceptional means, such as great compassion and bodhicitta, and exceptional wisdom that realizes existence and peace as empty of true existence. This directly teaches the two knowledges of the path of not abiding in the two extremes of existence and peace, and implicitly teaches the two: the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother due to not being expert in the means of stopping the two extremes of existence and peace, and the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother due to being expert in those means. Also from the Eight Thousand Stanza: "Bhagavan, the perfection of wisdom does not abide on the near shore, it does not abide on the far shore, nor does it abide afar in between the two," and so forth is spoken.

heading: **འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས།**
source: འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས།བཞི་པ་འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས་ནི། རྒྱན་ལས། དེ་ནི་ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པ་ཡིས། །ཡང་དག་ཉེ་བ་ཉིད་དུ་བཤད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། ཐེག་མེན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་གང་ཞིག །སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་སྟོང་ཉིད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་དེ། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་གཉེན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་ན་ཡོད། འདི་གཉིས་མདོ་འདིས་བསྟན་ཚུལ་ནི། བཤད་མ་ཐག་པ་ལྟར་རོ། །
translation: The knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother. Fourth, regarding the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother, it is said in the Ornament: "Because of being expert in means, it is explained as being perfectly close." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother is: a knowledge in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being that abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana, which is embraced by great compassion and the wisdom that directly realizes emptiness. That and the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The manner in which these two are taught by this sutra is just as explained above.

གཞི་ཤེས།དེ་ལྟར་རྒྱུ་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས་ལམ་ཤེས་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པ་ལ། མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་པའི་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་། །ནས། དེ་འདྲ་ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་རྒྱུད་ལྡན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པ་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཞི་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ། དགུ་ཡོད་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། སྦྱོར་བའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་དགུ་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། དང་པོ་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར་ཚུལ་རོལ་ཕ་རོལ་མཐའ་ལ་མིན། །ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང་། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་སྲིད་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་དང་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་ཞི་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་འཕགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེན། དེར་གྱུར་བའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་སྒོམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྔ་མ་དང་འདྲ།

Knowledge of the bases. Thus, having finished explaining the cause, the knowledge of the path, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases which is that which perfectly purifies the knowledge of the path: it is said in the Ornament of Clear Realization: "Through knowledge one does not abide in existence..." up to "...is asserted as the knowledge of all those [bases]." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases is: an exalted wisdom in the mind-stream of a person who possesses it, which is embraced by the wisdom that directly realizes selflessness, and which abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana. Regarding the phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases, there are nine: the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge; the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion; the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class; the preparation of the knowledge of the bases; the equality of the mode of apprehension of the preparation; and the path of seeing, since there are nine. To teach the first two, there is one verse beginning with "Not on the near shore, the far shore, or the limits..." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge is: a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of existence in relation to the conventional bases. That and the knowledge of the path that knows the path of the Śrāvakas are one in meaning. If divided, there are three: the Mahayana path of seeing, path of meditation, and path of no more learning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion is: a knowledge in a noble being's mind-stream that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of peace in relation to the conventional bases. That and a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization of exceptional methods are one in meaning. If divided, there are three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning of the Mahayana that become it. Its boundaries are like the previous one.

The knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge and the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion. To explain those two: not abiding in existence through such knowledge and the knowledge of the path of abiding in peace through compassion, the meaning of the one verse spoken beginning with "The heroes, wherever they act" and so forth is: The heroes, the bodhisattvas, who cannot be swayed by true-grasping and self-cherishing, wherever they act in the domains of samsara, see the faults of samsara; and by abiding in the perfection of wisdom embraced by exceptional means and knowledge, they perfectly pass beyond birth in samsara caused by karma and afflictions without being attached to any domain of samsara in the three realms; and even though they have passed beyond, they do not abide in the one-sided peace of nirvana that is merely liberation from existence like the Śrāvakas, so they do not abide in either of the extremes of existence or peace. Even though they have cleared away the karma and afflictions of powerless birth in existence, by the power of compassion and aspiration they thoroughly demonstrate taking birth in samsara. As it is said in the Sublime Continuum: "Because they are noble, they have eradicated the suffering of sickness, aging, and death." Like that, although they do not have aging, sickness, and death, for the sake of others they demonstrate dying, transmigrating, and so forth, because they are experts who possess exceptional means, such as great compassion and bodhicitta, and exceptional wisdom that realizes existence and peace as empty of true existence. This directly teaches the two knowledges of the path of not abiding in the two extremes of existence and peace, and implicitly teaches the two: the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother due to not being expert in the means of stopping the two extremes of existence and peace, and the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother due to being expert in those means. Also from the Eight Thousand Stanza: "Bhagavan, the perfection of wisdom does not abide on the near shore, it does not abide on the far shore, nor does it abide afar in between the two," and so forth is spoken.

heading: **མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས།**
source: མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས།ལྔ་བ་མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་ནི། རྒྱན་ལས། གཟུགས་སོགས་ཕུང་པོ་སྟེང་ཉིད་དང་།  ནས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས།  ཞེས་གསུངས། གཞི་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐབས་ཤེས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གཉིས་དང་བྲལ་བ་དེ། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐེག་དམན་འཕགས་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདེན་འཛིན་གྱིས་བཅིངས་པའི་གཞི་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གྱི་བར་ན་ཡོད། དེ་ཉིད་མདོ་འདིས་སྟོན་པར། འགྲོ་བ་འདི་དག་ཞེས་སོགས་རྐང་པ་གསུམ་གསུངས་པའི་དོན། མ་རིགས་པས་རྨོངས་པའི་འགྲོ་བ་འདི་དག་བརྒལ་བར་དཀའ་བའི་མིང་དང་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ལྔའི་འདམ་ལ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པར་ཆགས་ནས་རྒྱུ་སྐར་འཕུལ་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གོ་ལའི་རླུང་གི་འཁོར་ལོ་ཡང་དུ་འཁོར་བ་ལྟ་བུའི་སྲིད་རྩེ་ནས་མནར་མེད་ཀྱི་བར་དུ་འཁོར་བའི་འཁོར་ལོར་འཁྱམས་ཏེ་མ་རིགས་པ་ནས་རྐྱེ་རྒའི་བར་རྟེན་འབྲེལ་ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་འགལ་མེའི་འཁོར་ལོ་ལྟར་ལུ་གུ་རྒྱུད་དུ་འབྱུང་པས་སོ། །འགྲ་ོབ་འཁྲུལ་པར་གྱུར་པ་འདི་དག་འཁོར་བའི་གནས་འདིར་ཚུད་པ་རི་དྭགས་རྣམས་འབྲོས་སུ་མེད་པའི་རྒྱར་ཆུད་པ་དང་འདྲ་བར་སྡུག་བསྔལ་དུ་མས་མནར་ཞིང་ཐར་དཀའ་བར་ཤེས་ནས་བྱང་སེམས་ཤེས་རབ་དང་ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པ་རྣམས་འཁོར་བའི་གནས་ལ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་པར་གཞན་དོན་བྱའོ། །
translation: The knowledge of the bases of the discordant class. Fifth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class, it is said in the Ornament: "The emptiness of the aggregates of form and so forth..." up to "...the discordant class." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class is: a knowledge of the bases that is separated from the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases bound by true-grasping in the mind-stream of a noble Hinayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Hinayana path of seeing up to the Hinayana path of no more learning. To teach that very thing, the meaning of the three lines spoken in this sutra beginning with "These beings..." is: These beings who are obscured by ignorance, having become attached through grasping as true to the mud of the five aggregates of name and form which are difficult to cross, wander in the wheel of samsara from the peak of existence down to the Unrelenting Hell, like the continuously turning wheel of the spherical wind that propels the constellations; because the twelve links of dependent origination from ignorance to aging occur in a continuous sequence like a firebrand wheel. Knowing that these deluded beings caught in this state of samsara are tormented by many sufferings and are difficult to liberate, similar to deer caught in an inescapable trap, the bodhisattvas who are expert in wisdom and means should act for the sake of others without being attached to the state of samsara.

གཞི་ཤེས།དེ་ལྟར་རྒྱུ་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས་ལམ་ཤེས་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པ་ལ། མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་པའི་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་། །ནས། དེ་འདྲ་ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་རྒྱུད་ལྡན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པ་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཞི་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ། དགུ་ཡོད་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། སྦྱོར་བའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་དགུ་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། དང་པོ་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར་ཚུལ་རོལ་ཕ་རོལ་མཐའ་ལ་མིན། །ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང་། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་སྲིད་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་དང་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་ཞི་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་འཕགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེན། དེར་གྱུར་བའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་སྒོམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྔ་མ་དང་འདྲ།

Knowledge of the bases. Thus, having finished explaining the cause, the knowledge of the path, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases which is that which perfectly purifies the knowledge of the path: it is said in the Ornament of Clear Realization: "Through knowledge one does not abide in existence..." up to "...is asserted as the knowledge of all those [bases]." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases is: an exalted wisdom in the mind-stream of a person who possesses it, which is embraced by the wisdom that directly realizes selflessness, and which abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana. Regarding the phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases, there are nine: the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge; the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion; the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class; the preparation of the knowledge of the bases; the equality of the mode of apprehension of the preparation; and the path of seeing, since there are nine. To teach the first two, there is one verse beginning with "Not on the near shore, the far shore, or the limits..." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge is: a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of existence in relation to the conventional bases. That and the knowledge of the path that knows the path of the Śrāvakas are one in meaning. If divided, there are three: the Mahayana path of seeing, path of meditation, and path of no more learning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion is: a knowledge in a noble being's mind-stream that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of peace in relation to the conventional bases. That and a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization of exceptional methods are one in meaning. If divided, there are three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning of the Mahayana that become it. Its boundaries are like the previous one.

The knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge and the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion. To explain those two: not abiding in existence through such knowledge and the knowledge of the path of abiding in peace through compassion, the meaning of the one verse spoken beginning with "The heroes, wherever they act" and so forth is: The heroes, the bodhisattvas, who cannot be swayed by true-grasping and self-cherishing, wherever they act in the domains of samsara, see the faults of samsara; and by abiding in the perfection of wisdom embraced by exceptional means and knowledge, they perfectly pass beyond birth in samsara caused by karma and afflictions without being attached to any domain of samsara in the three realms; and even though they have passed beyond, they do not abide in the one-sided peace of nirvana that is merely liberation from existence like the Śrāvakas, so they do not abide in either of the extremes of existence or peace. Even though they have cleared away the karma and afflictions of powerless birth in existence, by the power of compassion and aspiration they thoroughly demonstrate taking birth in samsara. As it is said in the Sublime Continuum: "Because they are noble, they have eradicated the suffering of sickness, aging, and death." Like that, although they do not have aging, sickness, and death, for the sake of others they demonstrate dying, transmigrating, and so forth, because they are experts who possess exceptional means, such as great compassion and bodhicitta, and exceptional wisdom that realizes existence and peace as empty of true existence. This directly teaches the two knowledges of the path of not abiding in the two extremes of existence and peace, and implicitly teaches the two: the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother due to not being expert in the means of stopping the two extremes of existence and peace, and the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother due to being expert in those means. Also from the Eight Thousand Stanza: "Bhagavan, the perfection of wisdom does not abide on the near shore, it does not abide on the far shore, nor does it abide afar in between the two," and so forth is spoken.

heading: **གཉེན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས།**
source: གཉེན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། དྲུག་པ་མཚན་འཛིན་གྱི་གཉེན་པོས་ཟིན་པ་གཉེན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་ནི། རྒྱན་ལས། སྦྱིན་ལ་སོགས་ལ་ངར་འཛིན་མེད། ནས། དེ་ནིབསམ་མི་ཁྱབ་པར་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་གང་ཞིག །ཐབས་ཤེས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གཉིས་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་དེ། གཉན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། དེ་ཉིད་སྟོན་པར། ཤེས་རབ་ལྡན་པ་མཁའ་ལ་བྱ་བཞིན་རྣམ་པར་རྒྱུ། །ཞེས་གསུངས། དོན་ནི། རྨོངས་པའི་བགྲོ་བ་རི་དྭགས་ཀྱི་རྒྱར་ཆུད་པ་དང་འདྲ་བར་འཁོར་བའི་གནས་འདིར་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞིང་ཐར་དཀའ་བའི་ཚུལ་ཤེས་པར་བྱས་ནས་དམིགས་པ་མེད་པའི་བརྩེ་བ་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་གནས་ལུགས་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཕུད་སོགས་བདེན་པར་འཛིན་པའི་འཁྲུལ་བས་མ་བཅིངས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་ནི་བྱ་ནམ་མཁའ་རྒྱུ་ཡང་ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་བྱ་མི་གནས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་འཁོར་བའི་གནས་འདིར་ཆགས་ཞེན་གྱིས་མི་གནས་པར་གཞན་དོན་རྣམ་པར་རྒྱུའོ། །ཞེས་པའོ། །
translation: The knowledge of the bases of the antidote class. Sixth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class that is embraced by the antidote to apprehending marks, it is said in the Ornament: "There is no grasping at an 'I' in generosity and so forth..." up to "...that is asserted to be inconceivable." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class is: a knowledge in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being that abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana, which is embraced by the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. To teach that very thing, it is said: "Those endowed with wisdom roam like a bird in the sky." The meaning is: having known the way that obscured beings are suffering and difficult to liberate in this state of samsara, like deer caught in a trap, the bodhisattvas who are endowed with the non-apprehending affection of great compassion and the wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, and who are not bound by the delusion of grasping the aggregates and so forth as true, roam for the sake of others without abiding with clinging attachment in this state of samsara, just as a bird roams in the sky yet the bird does not abide in the sky.

གཞི་ཤེས།དེ་ལྟར་རྒྱུ་ལམ་ཤེས་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས་ལམ་ཤེས་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས་སྟོན་པ་ལ། མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན་ལས། ཤེས་པའི་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་། །ནས། དེ་འདྲ་ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། རང་རྒྱུད་ལྡན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བདག་མེད་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་གང་ཞིག །ཐེག་དམན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པ་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཞི་ཤེས་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ། དགུ་ཡོད་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་རིང་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། འབྲས་ཡུམ་ལ་ཉེ་བའི་གཞི་ཤེས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་ཤེས། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། སྦྱོར་བའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དང་། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་དགུ་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། དང་པོ་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར་ཚུལ་རོལ་ཕ་རོལ་མཐའ་ལ་མིན། །ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་བྱུང་། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་སྲིད་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། ཤེས་པས་སྲིད་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་ལམ་ཤེས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་སྒོམ་ལམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་དང་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་ལ་ལྟོས་ཏེ་ཞི་མཐའ་འགོག་བྱེད་ཀྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་འཕགས་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དེ། སྙིང་རྗེའི་ཞི་ལ་མི་གནས་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་ཐབས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་གྱི་རྟོགས་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་འཕགས་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེན། དེར་གྱུར་བའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་སྒོམ་མི་སློབ་ལམ་གསུམ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྔ་མ་དང་འདྲ།

Knowledge of the bases. Thus, having finished explaining the cause, the knowledge of the path, regarding teaching the knowledge of the bases which is that which perfectly purifies the knowledge of the path: it is said in the Ornament of Clear Realization: "Through knowledge one does not abide in existence..." up to "...is asserted as the knowledge of all those [bases]." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases is: an exalted wisdom in the mind-stream of a person who possesses it, which is embraced by the wisdom that directly realizes selflessness, and which abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana. Regarding the phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases, there are nine: the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge; the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion; the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother; the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class; the preparation of the knowledge of the bases; the equality of the mode of apprehension of the preparation; and the path of seeing, since there are nine. To teach the first two, there is one verse beginning with "Not on the near shore, the far shore, or the limits..." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge is: a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of existence in relation to the conventional bases. That and the knowledge of the path that knows the path of the Śrāvakas are one in meaning. If divided, there are three: the Mahayana path of seeing, path of meditation, and path of no more learning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion is: a knowledge in a noble being's mind-stream that abides in the class of realization that stops the extreme of peace in relation to the conventional bases. That and a noble Mahayana being's knowledge that abides in the class of realization of exceptional methods are one in meaning. If divided, there are three paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning of the Mahayana that become it. Its boundaries are like the previous one.

The knowledge of the path of not abiding in existence through knowledge and the knowledge of the path of not abiding in peace through compassion. To explain those two: not abiding in existence through such knowledge and the knowledge of the path of abiding in peace through compassion, the meaning of the one verse spoken beginning with "The heroes, wherever they act" and so forth is: The heroes, the bodhisattvas, who cannot be swayed by true-grasping and self-cherishing, wherever they act in the domains of samsara, see the faults of samsara; and by abiding in the perfection of wisdom embraced by exceptional means and knowledge, they perfectly pass beyond birth in samsara caused by karma and afflictions without being attached to any domain of samsara in the three realms; and even though they have passed beyond, they do not abide in the one-sided peace of nirvana that is merely liberation from existence like the Śrāvakas, so they do not abide in either of the extremes of existence or peace. Even though they have cleared away the karma and afflictions of powerless birth in existence, by the power of compassion and aspiration they thoroughly demonstrate taking birth in samsara. As it is said in the Sublime Continuum: "Because they are noble, they have eradicated the suffering of sickness, aging, and death." Like that, although they do not have aging, sickness, and death, for the sake of others they demonstrate dying, transmigrating, and so forth, because they are experts who possess exceptional means, such as great compassion and bodhicitta, and exceptional wisdom that realizes existence and peace as empty of true existence. This directly teaches the two knowledges of the path of not abiding in the two extremes of existence and peace, and implicitly teaches the two: the knowledge of the bases that is distant from the Resultant Mother due to not being expert in the means of stopping the two extremes of existence and peace, and the knowledge of the bases that is close to the Resultant Mother due to being expert in those means. Also from the Eight Thousand Stanza: "Bhagavan, the perfection of wisdom does not abide on the near shore, it does not abide on the far shore, nor does it abide afar in between the two," and so forth is spoken.

heading: **གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ།**
source: གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། བདུན་པ་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས་གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་མི་རྟག་སོགས་དང་། །ནས། སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ཤེས་བྱེད་དོ། །ཅེས་གསུངས། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་དང་དོན་དམ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་གང་རུང་གི་གཉེན་པར་སྒོམ་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྐབས་ནས་བསྟན་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོང་བའི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཁྱད་གཞི་གཟུགས་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཁྱད་ཆོས་མི་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་རྟེན་དུ་མ་རྫོགས་པ་དང་རྫོགས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་ཆགས་མེད་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟེ་ཡུལ་གྱི་ནས་བཞི་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་འཕེལ་འགྲིབ་མི་འགྱུར་བའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱེད་པ་པོ་བདེན་པར་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱ་དཀའ་རྣམ་གསུམ་གྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་མེད་ཀྱང་ཐ་སྙད་དུ་འབྲས་བུ་ཡོད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་གཞན་ལ་རག་མ་ལས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཤེས་བྱེད་དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་བཅུ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ནས་རྒྱུན་མཐའ་བར་ན་ཡོད།
translation: The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

The knowledge of the bases of the discordant class. Fifth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class, it is said in the Ornament: "The emptiness of the aggregates of form and so forth..." up to "...the discordant class." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class is: a knowledge of the bases that is separated from the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases bound by true-grasping in the mind-stream of a noble Hinayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Hinayana path of seeing up to the Hinayana path of no more learning. To teach that very thing, the meaning of the three lines spoken in this sutra beginning with "These beings..." is: These beings who are obscured by ignorance, having become attached through grasping as true to the mud of the five aggregates of name and form which are difficult to cross, wander in the wheel of samsara from the peak of existence down to the Unrelenting Hell, like the continuously turning wheel of the spherical wind that propels the constellations; because the twelve links of dependent origination from ignorance to aging occur in a continuous sequence like a firebrand wheel. Knowing that these deluded beings caught in this state of samsara are tormented by many sufferings and are difficult to liberate, similar to deer caught in an inescapable trap, the bodhisattvas who are expert in wisdom and means should act for the sake of others without being attached to the state of samsara.

The knowledge of the bases of the antidote class. Sixth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class that is embraced by the antidote to apprehending marks, it is said in the Ornament: "There is no grasping at an 'I' in generosity and so forth..." up to "...that is asserted to be inconceivable." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class is: a knowledge in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being that abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana, which is embraced by the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. To teach that very thing, it is said: "Those endowed with wisdom roam like a bird in the sky." The meaning is: having known the way that obscured beings are suffering and difficult to liberate in this state of samsara, like deer caught in a trap, the bodhisattvas who are endowed with the non-apprehending affection of great compassion and the wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, and who are not bound by the delusion of grasping the aggregates and so forth as true, roam for the sake of others without abiding with clinging attachment in this state of samsara, just as a bird roams in the sky yet the bird does not abide in the sky.

heading: **སྦྱོར་བ་དེའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་ཉིད།**
translation: The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

The knowledge of the bases of the discordant class. Fifth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class, it is said in the Ornament: "The emptiness of the aggregates of form and so forth..." up to "...the discordant class." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the discordant class is: a knowledge of the bases that is separated from the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases bound by true-grasping in the mind-stream of a noble Hinayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Hinayana path of seeing up to the Hinayana path of no more learning. To teach that very thing, the meaning of the three lines spoken in this sutra beginning with "These beings..." is: These beings who are obscured by ignorance, having become attached through grasping as true to the mud of the five aggregates of name and form which are difficult to cross, wander in the wheel of samsara from the peak of existence down to the Unrelenting Hell, like the continuously turning wheel of the spherical wind that propels the constellations; because the twelve links of dependent origination from ignorance to aging occur in a continuous sequence like a firebrand wheel. Knowing that these deluded beings caught in this state of samsara are tormented by many sufferings and are difficult to liberate, similar to deer caught in an inescapable trap, the bodhisattvas who are expert in wisdom and means should act for the sake of others without being attached to the state of samsara.

The knowledge of the bases of the antidote class. Sixth, regarding the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class that is embraced by the antidote to apprehending marks, it is said in the Ornament: "There is no grasping at an 'I' in generosity and so forth..." up to "...that is asserted to be inconceivable." The defining characteristic of the knowledge of the bases of the antidote class is: a knowledge in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being that abides in the class of realization of the Hinayana, which is embraced by the two exceptional means and wisdom. That and the knowledge of the bases in the mind-stream of a noble Mahayana being are one in meaning. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of seeing up to the ground of Buddhahood. To teach that very thing, it is said: "Those endowed with wisdom roam like a bird in the sky." The meaning is: having known the way that obscured beings are suffering and difficult to liberate in this state of samsara, like deer caught in a trap, the bodhisattvas who are endowed with the non-apprehending affection of great compassion and the wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, and who are not bound by the delusion of grasping the aggregates and so forth as true, roam for the sake of others without abiding with clinging attachment in this state of samsara, just as a bird roams in the sky yet the bird does not abide in the sky.

source: མཐོང་ལམ། དགུ་པ་མཐོང་ལམ་སྟོན་པར། སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་སོགས་བདེན་པ་དང་། །ནས། ཀུན་ཤེས་ཉིད་ཀྱི་སྐད་ཅིག་མ། །ཞེས་པའི་བར་བྱུང་། སྐབས་འདིར་དངོས་སུ་བསྟན་པའི་སྤྲོས་བྲལ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་བདེན་པ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། སྐབས་འདིར་དངོས་སུ་བསྟན་པའི་མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། སྐབས་འདིར་དངོས་སུ་བསྟན་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཤེས་བཟོང་སྐད་ཅིག་མ་བཅུ་དྲུག་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ཁོ་ནར་ཡོད། མཐོང་ལམ་འདི་ཉིད་འཆད་པར། དེ་ལྟར་སྤྱོད་པའི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གསུངས་པའི་དོན་ནི། སྔར་བཤད་པ་དེ་ལྟར་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེན་སྟོང་སྤྲོས་བྲལ་དུ་རྟོགས་ཤིང་གོམས་པར་བྱས་ཏེ་ལམ་ལ་རིམ་གྱིས་སློབ་ཅིང་སྤྱོད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གནས་ལུགས་ཀྱི་དོན་ལ་མཁས་ཤིང་བློ་གྲོས་གསལ་བ་དེས་ནི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་མཐོང་ལམ་ཐོབ་ནས་བདེན་འཛིན་གྱི་ཆགས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་བཅད་ནས་མཐོང་སྤངས་མ་ལུས་པ་ལས་གྲོལ་བར་འགྱུར་ལ། མངོན་ཞེན་གྱི་ཆགས་པ་མེད་པར་སྒོམ་ལམ་སོགས་གོང་ནས་གང་དུ་འགྲོ་སྟེ།
translation: The path of seeing. Ninth, regarding teaching the path of seeing, it occurs from: "The truth of suffering and so forth..." up to "...the moments of complete knowledge." The defining characteristic of the path of seeing explicitly taught in this context is: a clear realization of the Mahayana truth that directly realizes freedom from conceptual proliferation explicitly taught in this context. When divided, there are sixteen moments of Mahayana knowledge and forbearance explicitly taught in this context. Its boundaries are exclusively the Mahayana path of seeing. To explain this very path of seeing, one verse is spoken beginning with "Conducting themselves thus..." The meaning is: Just as explained before, whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena as the freedom from conceptual proliferation of the emptiness of true existence and familiarizes with it, thus gradually training and engaging on the path, being skilled in the meaning of the natural state and having clear intelligence, attains the Mahayana path of seeing, severs all attachment of true-grasping, and becomes liberated from all objects to be abandoned by seeing without exception; and they proceed higher and higher to the path of meditation and so forth without the attachment of evident grasping.

གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། བདུན་པ་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས་གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་མི་རྟག་སོགས་དང་། །ནས། སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ཤེས་བྱེད་དོ། །ཅེས་གསུངས། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་དང་དོན་དམ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་གང་རུང་གི་གཉེན་པར་སྒོམ་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྐབས་ནས་བསྟན་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོང་བའི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཁྱད་གཞི་གཟུགས་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཁྱད་ཆོས་མི་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་རྟེན་དུ་མ་རྫོགས་པ་དང་རྫོགས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་ཆགས་མེད་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟེ་ཡུལ་གྱི་ནས་བཞི་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་འཕེལ་འགྲིབ་མི་འགྱུར་བའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱེད་པ་པོ་བདེན་པར་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱ་དཀའ་རྣམ་གསུམ་གྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་མེད་ཀྱང་ཐ་སྙད་དུ་འབྲས་བུ་ཡོད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་གཞན་ལ་རག་མ་ལས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཤེས་བྱེད་དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་བཅུ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ནས་རྒྱུན་མཐའ་བར་ན་ཡོད།

The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

translation: For example, just as the sun remains brightly shining when free from the planetary eclipse called Rāhu, and just as a fire burns all grass, trees, and forests when kindled, the non-conceptual exalted wisdom of method and wisdom united in tandem, like the light of the sun and fire, clears away and subdues all the darkness and forests of the two obscurations—so it is said. According to the master, one must make a chapter break here, for he applied this single verse beginning with "All phenomena..." to the brief teaching of the training in complete aspects. According to the commentary on the Verse Summary by Jñānapāda, the section downwards from "To the Victorious Ones, the victory of the gods..." is applied to the training in complete aspects, and a chapter break is made at the beginning of that, and it appears that most manuscripts of the Verse Summary do likewise. Nevertheless, our own system follows the master's commentary; as Gungtang Jamyang also makes the chapter conclusion in his annotated commentary and so forth, the chapter conclusion after having finished explaining the nine phenomena that characterize the knowledge of the bases is: This is the commentary on the third chapter from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."

heading: **དབང་དུ་བྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་རྣམ་རྫོགས་སྦྱོར་བ།**
source: དབང་དུ་བྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་རྣམ་རྫོགས་སྦྱོར་བ།དང་པོ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས། རྣམ་པ་སྦྱོར་བ་བཅས་རྣམས་དང་། །ནས། འདི་ནི་ཐབས་མཁས་བཅས་པ་ཡིན། །ཞེས་གསུངས། མཁྱེན་གསུམ་གྱི་རྣམ་པ་བསྡུས་ནས་བསྒོམ་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དེ། རྣམ་རྫོགས་སྦྱོར་བའི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་བྱང་སེམས་ཀྱི་མཁྱེན་པ་དོན་གཅིག །དབྱེ་ན་རྣམ་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བརྒྱ་དོན་གསུམ་དང་། སྦྱོར་བའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཉི་ཤུ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ནས་རྒྱུན་མཐའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། རྣམ་རྫོགས་སྦྱོར་བ་མཚོན་བྱེད་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་ལ་བཅུ་གཅིག་ཡོད་དེ། རྣམ་པ་དང་། སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཡོན་ཏན་དང་། སྦྱོར་བའི་སྐྱོན་དང༌། མཚན་ཉིད་དང་། ཐར་པ་ཆ་མཐུན་དང་། སློབ་པ་ཕྱིར་མི་ལྡོག་པའི་དགེ་འདུན་དང་། སྲིད་ཞིའི་མཉམ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཞིང་དག་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཐབས་མཁས་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟེ་བཅུ་གཅིག་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར།
translation: The training in complete aspects which is the cause of mastery. Regarding teaching the first, it is said in the Ornament: "The aspects together with the trainings..." up to "...this is together with skillful means." The defining characteristic of the training in complete aspects is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that meditates having summarized the aspects of the three knowledges. That and the knowledge of a bodhisattva are synonymous. When divided, there are one hundred and seventy-three by way of aspects, and twenty by way of trainings. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum. There are eleven phenomena that characterize the training in complete aspects, because there are eleven: the aspects, the trainings, the good qualities, the faults of training, the defining characteristics, the aids to liberation, the sangha of irreversible learners, the training in the equality of existence and peace, the training in pure realms, and the training in skillful means.

གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ། བདུན་པ་གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟོན་པར། རྒྱན་ལས་གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་མི་རྟག་སོགས་དང་། །ནས། སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ཤེས་བྱེད་དོ། །ཅེས་གསུངས། གཞི་ཀུན་རྫོབ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་དང་དོན་དམ་པའི་སྡོད་ལུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་པར་ལ་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་ཞེན་པ་གང་རུང་གི་གཉེན་པར་སྒོམ་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྐབས་ནས་བསྟན་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོང་བའི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། ཁྱད་གཞི་གཟུགས་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཁྱད་ཆོས་མི་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་རྟེན་དུ་མ་རྫོགས་པ་དང་རྫོགས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། གཟུགས་སོགས་དེ་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་ཆགས་མེད་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་སྟེ་ཡུལ་གྱི་ནས་བཞི་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་འཕེལ་འགྲིབ་མི་འགྱུར་བའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱེད་པ་པོ་བདེན་པར་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། བྱ་དཀའ་རྣམ་གསུམ་གྱི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། དོན་དམ་པར་མེད་ཀྱང་ཐ་སྙད་དུ་འབྲས་བུ་ཡོད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་གཞན་ལ་རག་མ་ལས་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་། ཤེས་བྱེད་དཔེའི་སྒོ་ནས་སྣང་བ་རྣམ་བདུན་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་བཀག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་བཅུ་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ནས་རྒྱུན་མཐའ་བར་ན་ཡོད།

The training of the knowledge of the bases. Seventh, regarding teaching the training of the knowledge of the bases, it is said in the Ornament: "Form and so forth, its impermanence and so forth..." up to "...are made known by the sevenfold appearances." The defining characteristic of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva meditated as an antidote to either the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the conventional mode of abiding of the basis, or the mistaken adherence to the essence and attributes of the ultimate mode of abiding. When divided, there are ten: the training that refutes true-grasping to the basis of attributes, form and so forth; the training that refutes true-grasping to the attributes, impermanence and so forth; the training of form and so forth being unperfected and perfected as a basis of good qualities; and the training of non-attachment through true-grasping to form and so forth—these four by way of the object; the training in the perfection of wisdom not increasing or decreasing ultimately; the training of the agent lacking true existence; the training of the three difficult deeds; the training of fruits existing conventionally even though they do not exist ultimately; the training of awakening not depending on others; and the training that refutes true-grasping to the sevenfold appearances by way of illustrating examples. Its boundaries are from the Mahayana path of accumulation up to the end of the continuum.

སྦྱོར་བ་དེའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་ཉིད།བརྒྱད་པ་སྦྱོར་བ་དེའི་འཛིན་སྟངས་མཉམ་ཉིད་སྟོན་པར། གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་ལ་རློམ་མེད་པ། །རྣམ་བཞིའི་དེ་ཡི་མཉམ་བ་ཉིད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། གཞིའི་དབྱེ་བ་དང་མཚན་མཚོན་དང་ཡུལ་ཡུལ་ཅན་ལ་བདེན་ཞེན་འགོག་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་དེ། གཞི་ཤེས་སྐབས་ནས་བསྟན་པའི་བྱང་སེམས་ཀྱི་སྦྱོར་བའི་མཉམ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། གཟུགས་སོགས་ངོ་བོ་ལ་བདེན་པར་རློམ་པའི་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོརཔའི་མཉམ་ཉིད། དེའི་མཚན་མཆོན་ལ་བདེན་པར་རློམ་པ་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བའི་མཉམ་ཉིད། དེའི་དབྱེ་ལ་བདེན་པར་རློམ་པ་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བའི་མཉམ་ཉིད། དེའི་ཡུལ་ཡུལ་ཅན་ལ་བདེན་པར་རློམ་པ་མེད་པའི་སྦྱོར་བའི་མཉམ་ཉིད་དང་བཞི་ཡོད། ས་མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ་དང་འདྲ། འདི་གཉིས་སྡོམ་ཏེ་འཆད་པར། སྤྱོད་པ་ཡོངས་དག་ཅེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གཅིག་གསུངས། དོན་ནི། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཕུང་སོགས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེན་སྟོང་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་དུ་རྟོགས་ཤིང་སྤྱོད་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་དག་པ་གང་ཞིག་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་དང་ཁྱད་ཆོས་མི་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ལ་བདེན་པར་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པས་མི་སྤྱོད་ཅིང་། དེ་བཞིན་དུ་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པ་དང་འདུ་ཤེས་དང་ཚོར་བ་བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམ་གསུམ་དང་སེམས་བྱུང་སེམས་པར་ཡང་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་མྱི་སྤྱོད་ན། དེ་ལྟར་ཡུལ་གང་ལ་ཡང་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་མི་སྤྱོད་པར་རྒྱལ་སྲས་ཀྱི་སྤྱོད་པ་དེ་ནི་བདེན་ཞེན་གྱིས་ཆགས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཡོངས་སུ་སྤོངས་པར་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན་ཞིང་། བདེན་འཛིན་གྱི་ཆགས་པ་མཐའ་དག་ལས་རྣམ་པར་གྲོལ་པ་བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །ཡོན་ཏན་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་སྡུད་པ་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པའི་འགྲེལ་པ་ཟབ་མོ་རྟེན་འབྱུང་གི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་ནོར་བུའི་སྒྲོན་མེད་སྐལ་བཟང་རེ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལས་རྣམ་པར་དག་པའི་ལེའུ་སྟེ་བརྒྱད་པའི་འགྲེལ་བའོ།།  །།

The equality of the mode of apprehension of that training. Eighth, regarding teaching the equality of the mode of apprehension of that training, it is said: "The absence of conceit toward form and so forth... its equality is fourfold." The defining characteristic of the equality of the bodhisattva training taught in the context of the knowledge of the bases is: a yoga of a bodhisattva embraced by the wisdom that refutes true-grasping to the divisions of the bases, definition and definiendum, and object and object-possessor. When divided, there are four: the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding the essence of form and so forth; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its definition and definiendum; the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its divisions; and the equality of the training in the absence of conceit of true existence regarding its object and object-possessor. Its boundaries are similar to the training. To explain these two in summary, one verse is spoken beginning with "Thoroughly pure conduct..." The meaning is: Whichever bodhisattva realizes all phenomena of the aggregates and so forth as the equality of emptiness of true existence and whose conduct is thoroughly pure, does not engage through evident true-grasping to the essence of form and its attributes of impermanence and so forth. Likewise, if they do not engage through true-grasping to consciousness, discrimination, the three feelings of pleasure, pain, and neutrality, and the mental factor of intention, then this conduct of a child of the Victorious One, which does not engage with true-grasping to any object whatsoever in that way, thoroughly abandons all attachment of true-grasping; and they engage in the perfection of wisdom of the Sugatas, which is entirely liberated from all attachment of true-grasping—so it is said. This is the commentary on the eighth chapter, "Total Purity," from the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, called "The Jewelled Lamp that Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Origination, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate."
