heading: **ལྡོག་པ་གཟུང་རྟོག**
translation: Explanation in order to teach another example. When a carpenter who is skilled in the action of constructing mechanical devices constructs mechanical devices from wood in forms resembling men and women, the men and women constructed in that way also perform all activities such as going and staying, but they do not conceptualize thinking, "I have done this," because they have no minds. Similar to that example, that bodhisattva who is skilled and has attained stability in practicing the wisdom that realizes that although all phenomena are not ultimately existent, conventionally appearances are like illusions, performs all activities that accomplish the purpose of beings while abiding in non-conceptual pristine wisdom free from manifest conceptions that strongly adhere to apprehended and apprehender, like a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree. Thus it is said. This concludes the commentary on the twenty-sixth chapter, [the chapter on] being like illusions, from the Lamp of Jewels Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate: A Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection Illuminating the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising.

Conception of an apprehended object concerning engaging. First, to teach the conception of an apprehended object concerning engaging, the meaning of the one verse stated starting with "A bodhisattva..." is: A bodhisattva who, abiding in the pristine wisdom that does not conceptualize truly, completely knows that all thoroughly afflicted and purified phenomena are empty of nature, ultimately without marks, and without the elaborations or wishes of true establishment, does not seek awakening by way of true establishment or grasping at the two extremes through the wisdom realizing the pairs of thorough affliction and purification, apprehended and apprehender, and object to be abandoned and antidote and so forth to be without true existence. Conception of an apprehended object concerning turning back. Second, to teach the conception of an apprehended object concerning turning back, the meaning of the one verse stated starting with "That realm of space..." is: For example, because space is merely the absence of obstruction and contact, there is no entity of that realm of space itself, nor is there anything incompatible that cannot co-exist with that space, nor is there anything obstructing the occurrence of other physical forms. Because the realm of space and what is called space are equally non-entities, their entity is not attained by any physical thing at all. Similar to that example, a bodhisattva who is skilled in practicing the profound wisdom that realizes the nature of the path of seeing—the pairs of things to be adopted and discarded, and objects to be abandoned and antidotes, and so forth—as equality in being empty of true existence, also abides in non-conceptual pristine wisdom like space, possessing the greatness of practicing the complete pacification of all conceptions apprehending true existence, which are what turn one back to the inferior path. Conception of an apprehended object concerning engaging. First, to teach the conception of an apprehended object concerning engaging, the meaning of the one verse stated starting with "A bodhisattva..." is: A bodhisattva who, abiding in the pristine wisdom that does not conceptualize truly, completely knows that all thoroughly afflicted and purified phenomena are empty of nature, ultimately without marks, and without the elaborations or wishes of true establishment, does not seek awakening by way of true establishment or grasping at the two extremes through the wisdom realizing the pairs of thorough affliction and purification, apprehended and apprehender, and object to be abandoned and antidote and so forth to be without true existence. Conception of an apprehended object concerning turning back. Second, to teach the conception of an apprehended object concerning turning back, the meaning of the one verse stated starting with "That realm of space..." is: For example, because space is merely the absence of obstruction and contact, there is no entity of that realm of space itself, nor is there anything incompatible that cannot co-exist with that space, nor is there anything obstructing the occurrence of other physical forms. Because the realm of space and what is called space are equally non-entities, their entity is not attained by any physical thing at all. Similar to that example, a bodhisattva who is skilled in practicing the profound wisdom that realizes the nature of the path of seeing—the pairs of things to be adopted and discarded, and objects to be abandoned and antidotes, and so forth—as equality in being empty of true existence, also abides in non-conceptual pristine wisdom like space, possessing the greatness of practicing the complete pacification of all conceptions apprehending true existence, which are what turn one back to the inferior path. heading: **འཕྲོས་དོན།**
translation: Having thus taught passing beyond the mara of the devaputra, to teach passing beyond the four maras without exception, it is stated: Due to four kinds of causes, that bodhisattva who is skilled in means and possesses the strength of having directly realized emptiness is difficult to be defeated by the four maras, such as the mara of the devaputra, and cannot be moved from the path of the Great Vehicle. What are those four causes? Abiding in the wisdom that realizes phenomena to be empty by nature; great compassion that does not completely abandon accomplishing the purpose of sentient beings; the firm commitment that irreversibly accomplishes unsurpassable awakening for the sake of sentient beings, just as stated in the words of the promise and commitment that were made; and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas, having pleased the Victorious Ones by accumulating great collections of merit and pristine wisdom through making offerings to the Buddhas and so forth. Thus, if they possess those four kinds of causes, they cannot be harmed by the four maras and are able to defeat all maras. Thus it is said.

heading: **འཕྲོས་དོན།**
translation: To explain the remedies for those four conceptions, the three causes of the peak training of the path of seeing—teaching the path of awakening to others, imparting the words and meaning of the perfection of wisdom, and the cause for having no obstacles, which is exerting oneself in practice—and so forth, the meaning of the six verses stated starting with "The Mother of the Tathagatas..." is: When a bodhisattva perfectly teaches the path of seeing and so forth to others in order for them to attain great awakening, and when they explain, write in letters, and so forth this perfection of wisdom, the Mother that generates the Tathagatas, whatever bodhisattva feels heartfelt devotion with supreme joy and also gives it to others, and exerts themselves with sincere resolve in practicing or accomplishing this path themselves, that certain bodhisattva, whose continuum is gentle with love and compassion, should be known as having entered the very path of omniscience. As for the way of abiding without abiding because—although the great awakening subsumed by the peak training of the path of seeing exhausts stains—ultimately there is no exhaustion and no arising: bodhisattvas do not ultimately abide even in suchness, the ultimate nature of things, the dharma expanse; they abide without abiding by strongly adhering to anything whatsoever. For example, just as clouds in the sky do not rest steadily on anything whatsoever, they abide in suchness free from all elaborations without abiding by way of adhering to any phenomenon whatsoever as truly existent.

Second, to teach the first conception of an apprehender, which has the basis of a person substantially existing, the meaning of the two verses stated starting with "In the midst of people..." is: For example, in the midst of a large crowd of people gathered to watch a spectacle, an illusory person—a person emanated by means of illusory mantras and substances—does not think: "I shall please this large crowd of people with my excellent form and diverse activities," but still performs actions that please and delight the spectators, thoroughly displaying diverse miracles such as going and staying. Even though the crowd of people sees that, the illusory emanation is not established as a human body, it does not have a mind, and even its name is not ultimately established.

Likewise, bodhisattvas who practice the perfection of wisdom that does not conceptualize the nature of the path of seeing as truly existent never think, "Having ultimately realized great awakening, I will completely liberate beings from cyclic existence." Although they do not think that, for the sake of taming disciples, they demonstrate diverse births as gods, humans, and so forth, and possess many activities that accomplish the benefit and happiness of beings. Although they do not ultimately exist, they conventionally demonstrate them like illusions, and they practice by way of not conceptualizing those things as truly existent. Thus it is said.

Second, to teach the second conception of an apprehender, which has the basis of a person existing imputedly, the meaning of the two verses stated starting with "For example, a Buddha..." is: Even though emanations, such as supreme emanation bodies, perform all the activities of a Buddha such as teaching the Dharma, with regard to those emanations performing the activities of a Buddha, pride and arrogance thinking "I am the performer of the Buddha's activities" do not arise even slightly, because they do not have any conceptualization whatsoever. Likewise, a bodhisattva who is skilled in practicing the wisdom that does not conceptualize apprehended and apprehender as truly existing, although realizing all phenomena to be of one taste in being empty of true existence, conventionally performs all activities, such as the three of perfecting, ripening, and purifying, and demonstrates diverse activities, like emanations and illusions.

[3-284] translation already produced for this document:
Explanation in order to teach another example. When a carpenter who is skilled in the action of constructing mechanical devices constructs mechanical devices from wood in forms resembling men and women, the men and women constructed in that way also perform all activities such as going and staying, but they do not conceptualize thinking, "I have done this," because they have no minds. Similar to that example, that bodhisattva who is skilled and has attained stability in practicing the wisdom that realizes that although all phenomena are not ultimately existent, conventionally appearances are like illusions, performs all activities that accomplish the purpose of beings while abiding in non-conceptual pristine wisdom free from manifest conceptions that strongly adhere to apprehended and apprehender, like a wish-fulfilling jewel and a wish-granting tree. Thus it is said. heading: **འཕྲོས་དོན།**
translation: Just as when a mantra-holder roaming in the sky without any support to abide on, such as a house or dwelling, desires to abide, by the power of the mantra, in a single instant when it is time to arise in the sky, they bless and make appear whatever place they desire, such as beautiful and delightful parks endowed with captivating flowers, trees, and so forth, without it having arisen from the ground and so forth. Like that example, by the blessings of the unsurpassable mantra of the non-conceptual perfection of wisdom, that bodhisattva who practices the conduct of the Victor's children, such as establishing sentient beings in ripening and liberation, who is skilled in the method of accomplishing the purpose of others, and whose intelligence is clear in realizing the meaning of the natural state, does not apprehend the phenomena of the path that cause realization as truly existent objects of engagement, nor do they apprehend the qualities of a Buddha to be attained or what are not the means for attaining them as truly existent objects to be turned away from; and by abandoning the cognitive obscurations and conceptions—such as apprehending persons like the one explaining the dharma as substantially existent, and apprehending the person desiring the dharma, who is viewed as the very object of the dharma explanation, as a truly existent imputed person—they do not apprehend them as such, and this realization of all phenomena as empty of true existence is the abiding of the bodhisattvas who conventionally desire to pacify the suffering of sentient beings and delight in the path of the Great Vehicle and the qualities of the result such as the ten powers. Therefore, the great difference in the way of abiding from that of hearers, solitary realizers, and so forth is: except for the very abiding of the Tathagatas, who are arhats having abandoned the two obscurations and abiding in the preeminent samadhis such as the eight liberations, the totalities, and the outshinings, this abiding of the bodhisattvas has become the supreme of all the abidings of others, the hearers and solitary realizers, however many there are, which are endowed with the undefiled joy and bliss of the samadhi that pacifies afflictions without exception and thoroughly pacifies all suffering; and because there is nothing higher than that, it is an unsurpassable abiding.

Having thus taught passing beyond the mara of the devaputra, to teach passing beyond the four maras without exception, it is stated: Due to four kinds of causes, that bodhisattva who is skilled in means and possesses the strength of having directly realized emptiness is difficult to be defeated by the four maras, such as the mara of the devaputra, and cannot be moved from the path of the Great Vehicle. What are those four causes? Abiding in the wisdom that realizes phenomena to be empty by nature; great compassion that does not completely abandon accomplishing the purpose of sentient beings; the firm commitment that irreversibly accomplishes unsurpassable awakening for the sake of sentient beings, just as stated in the words of the promise and commitment that were made; and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas, having pleased the Victorious Ones by accumulating great collections of merit and pristine wisdom through making offerings to the Buddhas and so forth. Thus, if they possess those four kinds of causes, they cannot be harmed by the four maras and are able to defeat all maras. Thus it is said.

To explain the remedies for those four conceptions, the three causes of the peak training of the path of seeing—teaching the path of awakening to others, imparting the words and meaning of the perfection of wisdom, and the cause for having no obstacles, which is exerting oneself in practice—and so forth, the meaning of the six verses stated starting with "The Mother of the Tathagatas..." is: When a bodhisattva perfectly teaches the path of seeing and so forth to others in order for them to attain great awakening, and when they explain, write in letters, and so forth this perfection of wisdom, the Mother that generates the Tathagatas, whatever bodhisattva feels heartfelt devotion with supreme joy and also gives it to others, and exerts themselves with sincere resolve in practicing or accomplishing this path themselves, that certain bodhisattva, whose continuum is gentle with love and compassion, should be known as having entered the very path of omniscience. As for the way of abiding without abiding because—although the great awakening subsumed by the peak training of the path of seeing exhausts stains—ultimately there is no exhaustion and no arising: bodhisattvas do not ultimately abide even in suchness, the ultimate nature of things, the dharma expanse; they abide without abiding by strongly adhering to anything whatsoever. For example, just as clouds in the sky do not rest steadily on anything whatsoever, they abide in suchness free from all elaborations without abiding by way of adhering to any phenomenon whatsoever as truly existent.

heading: **འཕྲོས་དོན།**
translation: Although they abide in the samadhi that pacifies all elaborations, they do not fall into the extreme of peace where working for the purpose of others is interrupted. For example, just as winged birds abide in the supportless sky but do not fall to the ground, and fish abide in water but do not die from their ears and noses being blocked, in that way, although bodhisattvas who have attained skill in means have gone beyond the level of ordinary beings through the powers of meditative concentration, and having given rise in their continuum to the direct realization of the truth on the path of seeing, abide one-pointedly in emptiness free from elaborations, they will not have their minds captivated by the bliss of peace and pass into a nirvana where the purpose of others is interrupted, because they possess the preeminent powers of compassion and previous prayers of aspiration.

To explain the remedies for those four conceptions, the three causes of the peak training of the path of seeing—teaching the path of awakening to others, imparting the words and meaning of the perfection of wisdom, and the cause for having no obstacles, which is exerting oneself in practice—and so forth, the meaning of the six verses stated starting with "The Mother of the Tathagatas..." is: When a bodhisattva perfectly teaches the path of seeing and so forth to others in order for them to attain great awakening, and when they explain, write in letters, and so forth this perfection of wisdom, the Mother that generates the Tathagatas, whatever bodhisattva feels heartfelt devotion with supreme joy and also gives it to others, and exerts themselves with sincere resolve in practicing or accomplishing this path themselves, that certain bodhisattva, whose continuum is gentle with love and compassion, should be known as having entered the very path of omniscience. As for the way of abiding without abiding because—although the great awakening subsumed by the peak training of the path of seeing exhausts stains—ultimately there is no exhaustion and no arising: bodhisattvas do not ultimately abide even in suchness, the ultimate nature of things, the dharma expanse; they abide without abiding by strongly adhering to anything whatsoever. For example, just as clouds in the sky do not rest steadily on anything whatsoever, they abide in suchness free from all elaborations without abiding by way of adhering to any phenomenon whatsoever as truly existent.

heading: **འཕྲོས་དོན།**
translation: Therefore, the way one must train in the perfection of wisdom if one desires to attain the state of the three bodies is: Therefore, whoever desires to go to the supreme of all those qualities of all sentient beings, however many there are—that is, desires to attain the truth body; and desires to touch the pristine wisdom of the Buddha that is supremely wondrous and marvelous, which has become the supreme of all qualities; and, having awakened themselves, desires to give the best, supreme, and holy gift of dharma to sentient beings through inconceivable emanated displays, should rely on this supreme abiding of the Victorious Ones and their Children, which accomplishes the benefit and bliss of sentient beings without exception. Thus it is said. From the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, the Lamp of Jewels That Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, this is the commentary on the twenty-seventh chapter, the essence chapter.

Having thus taught passing beyond the mara of the devaputra, to teach passing beyond the four maras without exception, it is stated: Due to four kinds of causes, that bodhisattva who is skilled in means and possesses the strength of having directly realized emptiness is difficult to be defeated by the four maras, such as the mara of the devaputra, and cannot be moved from the path of the Great Vehicle. What are those four causes? Abiding in the wisdom that realizes phenomena to be empty by nature; great compassion that does not completely abandon accomplishing the purpose of sentient beings; the firm commitment that irreversibly accomplishes unsurpassable awakening for the sake of sentient beings, just as stated in the words of the promise and commitment that were made; and possessing the blessings of the Sugatas, having pleased the Victorious Ones by accumulating great collections of merit and pristine wisdom through making offerings to the Buddhas and so forth. Thus, if they possess those four kinds of causes, they cannot be harmed by the four maras and are able to defeat all maras. Thus it is said.

To explain the remedies for those four conceptions, the three causes of the peak training of the path of seeing—teaching the path of awakening to others, imparting the words and meaning of the perfection of wisdom, and the cause for having no obstacles, which is exerting oneself in practice—and so forth, the meaning of the six verses stated starting with "The Mother of the Tathagatas..." is: When a bodhisattva perfectly teaches the path of seeing and so forth to others in order for them to attain great awakening, and when they explain, write in letters, and so forth this perfection of wisdom, the Mother that generates the Tathagatas, whatever bodhisattva feels heartfelt devotion with supreme joy and also gives it to others, and exerts themselves with sincere resolve in practicing or accomplishing this path themselves, that certain bodhisattva, whose continuum is gentle with love and compassion, should be known as having entered the very path of omniscience. As for the way of abiding without abiding because—although the great awakening subsumed by the peak training of the path of seeing exhausts stains—ultimately there is no exhaustion and no arising: bodhisattvas do not ultimately abide even in suchness, the ultimate nature of things, the dharma expanse; they abide without abiding by strongly adhering to anything whatsoever. For example, just as clouds in the sky do not rest steadily on anything whatsoever, they abide in suchness free from all elaborations without abiding by way of adhering to any phenomenon whatsoever as truly existent.

heading: **མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ།**
translation: The nature of the path of seeing: Having thus explained the secondary topics, second, the nature of the path of seeing. The meaning of what is stated in the four verses starting with "This training" is: This training of the perfection of wisdom, which has become the very nature of the great awakening of the path of seeing, has become the supreme of all the measureless trainings of the bodhisattvas that the Guides, the perfect Buddhas, have completely expressed, however many trainings they have taught; and because there is no other higher than this, it is unsurpassed; therefore, whichever wise one desires to go to the level of a Buddha, the other shore or culmination of all trainings, should train in this perfection of wisdom, the path of the Great Vehicle, the training of a Buddha. Explaining how this very path of seeing is the treasury of the twelve hundred qualities and so forth; the storehouse of the thirty-six aspects, grouping the six perfections within each of giving and so forth; and how one is born into the family of the Buddhas and how all the qualities of the ultimate ten grounds arise from this, along with a pair of examples, is: This path of seeing, such as the patience of knowing dharma regarding suffering, is the source of the twelve hundred qualities and so forth, such as seeing the faces of Buddhas, so it is the supreme great treasury of dharma; and it is the holy, wondrous storehouse of dharma with vast wealth of qualities, such as the thirty-six perfections of giving and so forth, dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and factors of awakening; and one is born into the family from which the Buddha himself arises, because one is certain to attain the state of a Buddha. Progressing sequentially through the ten grounds, such as the first ground, the Very Joyful, and reaching the culmination of all qualities is the storehouse from which all the temporary and ultimate bliss and happiness of transmigrators arises and abides; and although all the Protectors of the World of the ten directions, the Buddhas, the transcendent and accomplished conquerors, however many there are—those of the past who have already come, those who have not yet come, and those currently residing—are born from practicing this path of the perfection of wisdom, the natural perfection of wisdom, the dharmadhātu, never becomes exhausted, but abides free from decrease and increase. Therefore, explaining in order to show through examples that this is the cause of all qualities: For example, just as all trees, fruits, flowers, forests, and so forth, however many there are, genuinely arise from the earth and come forth upon the earth; yet, although it produces all the trees and so forth again and again, the earth is not exhausted by way of being interrupted, nor does it increase higher and higher, nor does it completely diminish by changing into another state of a thing, nor does it conceptualize, thinking, "I have produced the plants, forests, and so forth," and even though it produces fruits again and again, it is without weariness or frustration, because they arise from the collection of causes, conditions, and dependent arising, but there is no personal self who is a creator.

[3-289] translation already produced for this document:
Just as when a mantra-holder roaming in the sky without any support to abide on, such as a house or dwelling, desires to abide, by the power of the mantra, in a single instant when it is time to arise in the sky, they bless and make appear whatever place they desire, such as beautiful and delightful parks endowed with captivating flowers, trees, and so forth, without it having arisen from the ground and so forth. Like that example, by the blessings of the unsurpassable mantra of the non-conceptual perfection of wisdom, that bodhisattva who practices the conduct of the Victor's children, such as establishing sentient beings in ripening and liberation, who is skilled in the method of accomplishing the purpose of others, and whose intelligence is clear in realizing the meaning of the natural state, does not apprehend the phenomena of the path that cause realization as truly existent objects of engagement, nor do they apprehend the qualities of a Buddha to be attained or what are not the means for attaining them as truly existent objects to be turned away from; and by abandoning the cognitive obscurations and conceptions—such as apprehending persons like the one explaining the dharma as substantially existent, and apprehending the person desiring the dharma, who is viewed as the very object of the dharma explanation, as a truly existent imputed person—they do not apprehend them as such, and this realization of all phenomena as empty of true existence is the abiding of the bodhisattvas who conventionally desire to pacify the suffering of sentient beings and delight in the path of the Great Vehicle and the qualities of the result such as the ten powers. Therefore, the great difference in the way of abiding from that of hearers, solitary realizers, and so forth is: except for the very abiding of the Tathagatas, who are arhats having abandoned the two obscurations and abiding in the preeminent samadhis such as the eight liberations, the totalities, and the outshinings, this abiding of the bodhisattvas has become the supreme of all the abidings of others, the hearers and solitary realizers, however many there are, which are endowed with the undefiled joy and bliss of the samadhi that pacifies afflictions without exception and thoroughly pacifies all suffering; and because there is nothing higher than that, it is an unsurpassable abiding.

Although they abide in the samadhi that pacifies all elaborations, they do not fall into the extreme of peace where working for the purpose of others is interrupted. For example, just as winged birds abide in the supportless sky but do not fall to the ground, and fish abide in water but do not die from their ears and noses being blocked, in that way, although bodhisattvas who have attained skill in means have gone beyond the level of ordinary beings through the powers of meditative concentration, and having given rise in their continuum to the direct realization of the truth on the path of seeing, abide one-pointedly in emptiness free from elaborations, they will not have their minds captivated by the bliss of peace and pass into a nirvana where the purpose of others is interrupted, because they possess the preeminent powers of compassion and previous prayers of aspiration.

[3-291] translation already produced for this document:
Therefore, the way one must train in the perfection of wisdom if one desires to attain the state of the three bodies is: Therefore, whoever desires to go to the supreme of all those qualities of all sentient beings, however many there are—that is, desires to attain the truth body; and desires to touch the pristine wisdom of the Buddha that is supremely wondrous and marvelous, which has become the supreme of all qualities; and, having awakened themselves, desires to give the best, supreme, and holy gift of dharma to sentient beings through inconceivable emanated displays, should rely on this supreme abiding of the Victorious Ones and their Children, which accomplishes the benefit and bliss of sentient beings without exception. Thus it is said. From the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, the Lamp of Jewels That Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, this is the commentary on the twenty-seventh chapter, the essence chapter.

heading: **མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ།**
translation: Likewise, all the qualities of bliss, happiness, and excellence of all transmigrating sentient beings, however many there are—the Buddhas' children, the bodhisattvas; hearers and solitary realizers; gods such as Brahmā and Indra; and humans and so forth—all arise from meditating on the supreme perfection of wisdom, the path of seeing, because by practicing the path of the Great Vehicle, they awaken perfectly and completely, and from their teaching the dharma, all higher elevations and definite goodness arise. Thus, although all the bliss and goodness of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa arises in dependence upon the perfection of wisdom, that wisdom never becomes exhausted, nor does it increase, in the ultimate sense. Thus it is said.

Where the commentary quotes or glosses words of the root verses, keep those quoted words recognisable in the translation. Keep proper names in their standard Sanskrit forms (Subhūti, Śāriputra, Maitreya, Haribhadra) and technical terms recognisable (prajñāpāramitā = perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva). Do not add commentary, notes, or explanation of your own.

Just as when a mantra-holder roaming in the sky without any support to abide on, such as a house or dwelling, desires to abide, by the power of the mantra, in a single instant when it is time to arise in the sky, they bless and make appear whatever place they desire, such as beautiful and delightful parks endowed with captivating flowers, trees, and so forth, without it having arisen from the ground and so forth. Like that example, by the blessings of the unsurpassable mantra of the non-conceptual perfection of wisdom, that bodhisattva who practices the conduct of the Victor's children, such as establishing sentient beings in ripening and liberation, who is skilled in the method of accomplishing the purpose of others, and whose intelligence is clear in realizing the meaning of the natural state, does not apprehend the phenomena of the path that cause realization as truly existent objects of engagement, nor do they apprehend the qualities of a Buddha to be attained or what are not the means for attaining them as truly existent objects to be turned away from; and by abandoning the cognitive obscurations and conceptions—such as apprehending persons like the one explaining the dharma as substantially existent, and apprehending the person desiring the dharma, who is viewed as the very object of the dharma explanation, as a truly existent imputed person—they do not apprehend them as such, and this realization of all phenomena as empty of true existence is the abiding of the bodhisattvas who conventionally desire to pacify the suffering of sentient beings and delight in the path of the Great Vehicle and the qualities of the result such as the ten powers. Therefore, the great difference in the way of abiding from that of hearers, solitary realizers, and so forth is: except for the very abiding of the Tathagatas, who are arhats having abandoned the two obscurations and abiding in the preeminent samadhis such as the eight liberations, the totalities, and the outshinings, this abiding of the bodhisattvas has become the supreme of all the abidings of others, the hearers and solitary realizers, however many there are, which are endowed with the undefiled joy and bliss of the samadhi that pacifies afflictions without exception and thoroughly pacifies all suffering; and because there is nothing higher than that, it is an unsurpassable abiding.

Although they abide in the samadhi that pacifies all elaborations, they do not fall into the extreme of peace where working for the purpose of others is interrupted. For example, just as winged birds abide in the supportless sky but do not fall to the ground, and fish abide in water but do not die from their ears and noses being blocked, in that way, although bodhisattvas who have attained skill in means have gone beyond the level of ordinary beings through the powers of meditative concentration, and having given rise in their continuum to the direct realization of the truth on the path of seeing, abide one-pointedly in emptiness free from elaborations, they will not have their minds captivated by the bliss of peace and pass into a nirvana where the purpose of others is interrupted, because they possess the preeminent powers of compassion and previous prayers of aspiration.

Therefore, the way one must train in the perfection of wisdom if one desires to attain the state of the three bodies is: Therefore, whoever desires to go to the supreme of all those qualities of all sentient beings, however many there are—that is, desires to attain the truth body; and desires to touch the pristine wisdom of the Buddha that is supremely wondrous and marvelous, which has become the supreme of all qualities; and, having awakened themselves, desires to give the best, supreme, and holy gift of dharma to sentient beings through inconceivable emanated displays, should rely on this supreme abiding of the Victorious Ones and their Children, which accomplishes the benefit and bliss of sentient beings without exception. Thus it is said. From the Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection, the Lamp of Jewels That Illuminates the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, Fulfilling the Hopes of the Fortunate, this is the commentary on the twenty-seventh chapter, the essence chapter.

heading: **མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ།**
translation: Because merely meditating on emptiness in meditative equipoise is not sufficient, but one must also become familiar with the forward and reverse progressions of the twelve links of dependent arising during the subsequent attainment, explaining this very method: The meaning of what is stated in the three verses starting with "Lower sentient beings" is: The Sugatas have taught that in the world, in relation to body and resources, all the classes of sentient beings, however many there are—the lower sentient beings, those of the lower realms; the middling, humans and so forth; and the supreme, gods—do not arise from a Principal, a Lord, permanent Time, and so forth, but arise from the ignorance of self-grasping; by the power of the ignorance of grasping at a personal self, which is the contradictory and discordant class to awareness and pristine wisdom, karma is accumulated, and when conditions assemble, such as being nourished by craving, grasping, and so forth, which are the cooperative conditions of karma, the projected results of birth, aging, sickness, death, and so forth are established, and this great mechanism of the suffering of saṃsāra, such as the completely afflicted twelve links of dependent arising, genuinely arises again and again; yet, even so, that mechanism of ignorance in the continuums of sentient beings is not exhausted by the arising of results, nor does it increase, but remains just as it is.

མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ།དེ་ལྟར་འཕྲོས་དོན་བཤད་ཟིན་ནས། གཉིས་མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ་ནི། བསླབ་པ་འདི་ནི་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་བཞི་གསུངས་པའི་དོན་ནི། མཐོང་ལམ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཆེན་པོ་རང་གི་ངོ་བོར་གྱུར་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་བསླབ་པ་འདི་ནི། འདྲེན་པ་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་བསླབ་ཚད་མེད་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྗོད་པ་བསླབ་གང་ཇི་སྙེད་གཅིག་གསུངས་པ་དེ་དག་ཀུན་གྱི་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་བ་དང་། འདི་ལས་ལྷག་པ་གཞན་མེད་པས་གོང་ནས་མེད་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། མཁས་པ་གང་ཞིག་བསླབ་པ་ཀུན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏེ་མཐར་ཕྱིན་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སར་འགྲོ་བར་འདོད་པས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པའི་ལམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདིར་སློབ་པར་བྱའོ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་རིགས་སུ་སྐྱེས་ཤིང་དོན་དམ་པའི་ས་བཅུའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཐམས་ཅད་འདི་ལས་སྐྱེ་ཚུལ་དཔེ་ཚན་གཉིས་དང་བཅས་པས་འཆད་བ་ནི། སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་ཆོས་ཤེས་པའི་བཟོད་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་མཐོང་བའི་ལམ་འདི་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞལ་མཐོང་བ་སོགས་ཡོན་ཏན་བརྒྱ་ཕྲག་བཅུ་གཉིས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་འབྱུང་གནས་ཡིན་པས་ཆོས་ཀྱི་གཏེར་ཆེན་པོ་མཆོག་དང་། སྦྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཕར་ཕྱིན་སོ་དྲུག་དང་གཟུངས་དང་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དང་། བྱང་ཕྱོགས་སོགས་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ནོར་རྒྱ་ཆེ་བའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་མཛོད་དམ་པ་རྨད་དུ་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ལ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཉིད་འབྱུང་བའི་རིགས་སུ་སྐྱེས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། མ་བྱོན་པ་དང་། ད་ལྟར་ཞལ་བཞུགས་པའི་ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་མགོན་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ལམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་འདི་ཉམས་སུ་བླངས་པ་ལས་འཁྲུངས་ཀྱང་། The nature of the path of seeing: Having thus explained the secondary topics, second, the nature of the path of seeing. The meaning of what is stated in the four verses starting with "This training" is: This training of the perfection of wisdom, which has become the very nature of the great awakening of the path of seeing, has become the supreme of all the measureless trainings of the bodhisattvas that the Guides, the perfect Buddhas, have completely expressed, however many trainings they have taught; and because there is no other higher than this, it is unsurpassed; therefore, whichever wise one desires to go to the level of a Buddha, the other shore or culmination of all trainings, should train in this perfection of wisdom, the path of the Great Vehicle, the training of a Buddha. Explaining how this very path of seeing is the treasury of the twelve hundred qualities and so forth; the storehouse of the thirty-six aspects, grouping the six perfections within each of giving and so forth; and how one is born into the family of the Buddhas and how all the qualities of the ultimate ten grounds arise from this, along with a pair of examples, is: This path of seeing, such as the patience of knowing dharma regarding suffering, is the source of the twelve hundred qualities and so forth, such as seeing the faces of Buddhas, so it is the supreme great treasury of dharma; and it is the holy, wondrous storehouse of dharma with vast wealth of qualities, such as the thirty-six perfections of giving and so forth, dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and factors of awakening; and one is born into the family from which the Buddha himself arises, because one is certain to attain the state of a Buddha. Progressing sequentially through the ten grounds, such as the first ground, the Very Joyful, and reaching the culmination of all qualities is the storehouse from which all the temporary and ultimate bliss and happiness of transmigrators arises and abides; and although all the Protectors of the World of the ten directions, the Buddhas, the transcendent and accomplished conquerors, however many there are—those of the past who have already come, those who have not yet come, and those currently residing—are born from practicing this path of the perfection of wisdom, the natural perfection of wisdom, the dharmadhātu, never becomes exhausted, but abides free from decrease and increase. Therefore, explaining in order to show through examples that this is the cause of all qualities: For example, just as all trees, fruits, flowers, forests, and so forth, however many there are, genuinely arise from the earth and come forth upon the earth; yet, although it produces all the trees and so forth again and again, the earth is not exhausted by way of being interrupted, nor does it increase higher and higher, nor does it completely diminish by changing into another state of a thing, nor does it conceptualize, thinking, "I have produced the plants, forests, and so forth," and even though it produces fruits again and again, it is without weariness or frustration, because they arise from the collection of causes, conditions, and dependent arising, but there is no personal self who is a creator.

Likewise, all the qualities of bliss, happiness, and excellence of all transmigrating sentient beings, however many there are—the Buddhas' children, the bodhisattvas; hearers and solitary realizers; gods such as Brahmā and Indra; and humans and so forth—all arise from meditating on the supreme perfection of wisdom, the path of seeing, because by practicing the path of the Great Vehicle, they awaken perfectly and completely, and from their teaching the dharma, all higher elevations and definite goodness arise. Thus, although all the bliss and goodness of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa arises in dependence upon the perfection of wisdom, that wisdom never becomes exhausted, nor does it increase, in the ultimate sense. Thus it is said.

heading: **མཐོང་ལམ་གྱི་ངོ་བོ།**
translation: The pristine wisdom of the Buddha, the path of meditation that accords with its mode, its point of entry, the path of seeing, the method for generating it, the path of preparation, and its root, the path of accumulation—however many there are, all of these arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom that realizes selflessness. Because one repeatedly familiarizes oneself with that very pristine wisdom that realizes selflessness and accumulates a vast collection of merit, ignorance ceases, and because one does not accumulate karma that projects saṃsāra, the mechanism of suffering does not arise. By being taught by a spiritual friend, conditions of method such as meditating on love and compassion assemble, and the mechanism of pristine wisdom, such as the ten grounds and five paths of the Great Vehicle, genuinely arises, and its root, the perfection of wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, is never exhausted, nor does it increase in the ultimate sense, but abides conventionally as dependent arising, like a magical illusion. Thus, it is said in the Gaganagañjaparipṛcchā Sūtra: "If one genuinely knows all dharmas / That arise in dependence upon causes, / That treasury is inexhaustible; / The treasury of dharma is inconceivable. / The protector of the world has genuinely taught / That these four dharmas are inexhaustible: / Sentient beings, space, bodhicitta, / And likewise, the qualities of a Buddha. / If they were substantial, / They would become completely exhausted. / Because they are non-existent, they are called 'inexhaustible'; / Therefore they are taught as inexhaustible." Therefore, it is said that whichever bodhisattva knows this profound meaning of the perfection of wisdom—that all dharmas of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa conventionally arise in dependence, and if one investigates and searches for them with reasoning, not even the slightest bit is found, so one completely knows that they are without arising by their own intrinsic nature, and without exhaustion, that is, without cessation—penetrates the profound precious treasury of the Buddha's speech and sees the dharmakāya. As it is said in the Suhṛllekha: "This dependent arising is the profound, / Precious treasury of the Victor's speech. / Whoever genuinely sees this / Sees the Buddha, the supreme knower of suchness." Thus, by knowing the meaning of the profound abiding nature, emptiness, familiarizing oneself with it, and abiding on the path of meditation, such as the meditative absorption of leap-over, just as, for example, the sun, being without conceptuality and radiating light, dispels darkness without exception, so too, having destroyed the thick darkness of the obscurations of ignorance along with its latent tendencies without exception, one will attain the supreme pristine wisdom of a spontaneously arisen Buddha, just as it was prophesied that the six hundred monks will become Tathāgatas named Avakīrṇakusuma. This is the commentary on the twenty-eighth chapter, the Chapter of Avakīrṇakusuma, from The Fulfiller of the Hopes of the Fortunate: A Jeweled Lamp Illuminating the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, a Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection.

མཉམ་བཞག་ཏུ་སྟོང་ཉིད་བསྒོམས་པ་ཙམ་གྱིས་མི་མཆོག་པར་རྗེས་ཐོབ་ཏུའང་རྟེན་འབྲེལ་ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་ལུགས་འབྱུང་ལྡོག་སོགས་ལ་འདྲིས་པར་བྱེད་དགོས་པས་ཚུལ་དེ་ཉིད་འཆད་པར། སེམས་ཅན་ཐ་མ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གསུམ་གསུངས་པའི་དོན། འཇིག་རྟེན་ན་ལུས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ལ་ལྟོས་ནས་སེམས་ཅན་ཐ་མ་ངན་སོང་བ་རྣམས་དང་འབྲིང་མི་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་བ་ལྷ་སྟེ་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་རིས་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ་དེ་ཀུན་གཙོ་བོ་དང་།དབང་ཕྱུག་དང་དུས་རྟག་པ་སོགས་ལས་བྱུང་བ་མ་ཡིན་པར་བདག་འཛིན་མ་རིག་པ་ལས་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན་པར་བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་ཏེ་རིག་པ་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་འགལ་ཟླ་མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་སུ་གྱུར་བའི་གང་ཟག་གི་བདག་ཏུ་འཛིན་པའི་མ་རིག་པའི་དབང་གིས་ལས་བསགས་ལས་ཀྱི་ལྷན་ཅིག་བྱེད་རྐྱེན་སྲེད་ལེན་སོགས་ཀྱིས་གསོས་བཏབ་སོགསརྐྱེན་རྣམས་ཚོགས་ནས་སྐྱེ་རྒ་ན་འཆི་སོགས་འཕང་འབྲས་རྣམས་གྲུབ་སྟེ་ཀུན་ནས་ཉོན་མོངས་པའི་རྟེན་འབྲེལ་ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་སོགས་འཁོར་བའི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་གྱི་འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་ཆེན་པོ་འདི་ཡང་ནས་ཡང་དུ་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་ལ། དེ་ལྟ་ནའང་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་མ་་རིག་པའི་འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་དེ་ནི་འབྲས་བུ་བྱུང་པས་ཟད་པ་མེད་ཅིང་འཕེལ་བའང་མེད་དེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་གནས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །
[3-294] translation already produced for this document:
Because merely meditating on emptiness in meditative equipoise is not sufficient, but one must also become familiar with the forward and reverse progressions of the twelve links of dependent arising during the subsequent attainment, explaining this very method: The meaning of what is stated in the three verses starting with "Lower sentient beings" is: The Sugatas have taught that in the world, in relation to body and resources, all the classes of sentient beings, however many there are—the lower sentient beings, those of the lower realms; the middling, humans and so forth; and the supreme, gods—do not arise from a Principal, a Lord, permanent Time, and so forth, but arise from the ignorance of self-grasping; by the power of the ignorance of grasping at a personal self, which is the contradictory and discordant class to awareness and pristine wisdom, karma is accumulated, and when conditions assemble, such as being nourished by craving, grasping, and so forth, which are the cooperative conditions of karma, the projected results of birth, aging, sickness, death, and so forth are established, and this great mechanism of the suffering of saṃsāra, such as the completely afflicted twelve links of dependent arising, genuinely arises again and again; yet, even so, that mechanism of ignorance in the continuums of sentient beings is not exhausted by the arising of results, nor does it increase, but remains just as it is.

heading: **སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར།**
source: སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར། དྲུག་པ་སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་སྟོན་པར།རྒྱན་ལས། འགོག་དང་བཅས་པའི་སྙོམས་འཇུག་དགུ། ནས། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་གཞན་རྣམ་པ་དགུ། །ཞེས་གསུངས། འདི་ལ་གསུམ་ལས། དང་པོ་ནི། སྒོམ་སྤངས་རྟོགས་བའི་ས་བོན་གྱི་དངོས་གཉེན་གྱི་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཉིས་པ་དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། སྒོམ་སྤངས་རྣམ་རྟོག་བསྐོར་དགུའི་དངོས་གཉེན་བར་ཆད་མེད་ལམ་དགུ་དང་། སྒོམ་ལམ་རྣམ་འགྲོལ་ལམ་བསྐོར་དགུ་ཡོད། གསུམ་པ་ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་ས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་འཆད་པར། མཐུ་ཆེན་ལྡན་པ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གསུམ་གསུངས། དེ་ཡང་སྤངས་བྱ་བཟུང་འཛིན་གྱི་རྟོག་པ་བཞི་ལས་བཟུང་རྟོག་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར། ཤེས་སྒྲིབ་བཟུང་བར་རྟོག་པ་གཉིས་སྤངས་པ་སོགས་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་མཐུ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཡི་བྱང་སེམས་སྒོམ་ལམ་པ་དེ་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་དངོས་གཞིའི་སྙོམས་འཇུག་བཞིས་ཀྱང་གནས་ཤིང་ཐོང་རྒལ་གྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་གོམས་པར་ཡང་བྱེད་ལ། དེའི་ཚེ་དེ་ལ་བཟུང་བར་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་རྟེན་པར་བྱེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཞིང་སྙོམས་འཇུག་གི་བདེ་བ་ལ་རོ་མྱོང་བའི་སྒོ་ནས་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པའང་མེད་དེ་གཟུང་བ་བདེན་མེད་དུ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འོན་ཀྱང་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་དངོས་གཞི་སྙོམས་འཇུག་དང་པོའི་ཡན་ལག་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དང་དགའ་བདེ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་བཅས་པ་བཞི་པོ་འདི་བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པ་མཆོག་གི་སྤངས་རྟོགས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་ཐོབ་པ་ཡི་རྟེན་དུ་འགྱུར་ཏེ་མཐོང་སྒོམ་གྱི་ལམ་ཐམས་ཅད་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་དངོས་གཞི་ལ་རྟེན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །བུདྡྷ་ཤྲཱིས་འདི་མན་ཆད་བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་ལ་སྦྱར་ཡང༌། སློབ་དཔོན་ལྟར་ཤེས་སྒྲིབ་འཛིན་རྟོག་གཉིས་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་ལ་གོམས་ཤིང་སྐྱེ་བ་སྣ་ཚོགས་བཟུང་སྟེ་གཞན་དོན་སྒྲུབ་པའི་ཚུལ་ནི། གནས་ལུགས་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་མཆོག་ཐོབ་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྒོམ་ལམ་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དག་ལ་གནས་པ་ནི་གཟུགས་མེད་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དམ་པ་བཞི་དང་འགོག་པའི་སྙོམས་འཇུག་སོགས་ལ་ཡང་སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་ཅིང་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བར་བྱེད་ཀྱང་དེ་དག་ལ་བདེན་པར་མི་ཞེན་ལ།གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་བསམ་གཏན་འདི་དག་མངོན་ཤེས་དང་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་སོགས་ཀྱི་མཐུན་རྐྱེན་དུ་གྱུར་པ་ཡིན་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་དམ་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་མཆོག་ཐོབ་པ་ལ་ཕན་པའི་རྐྱེན་གྱུར་པས་ན་དེ་ལ་སློབ་པ་ཡིན་གྱི། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཉན་རང་ལྟར་ཉོན་མོངས་པའམ་ཟག་པ་ཟད་ནས་ཞི་བའི་བདེ་བ་ལ་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་སློབ་པ་མིན་ཏེ་ལ་དེ་ལ་རང་དོན་དུ་ཞི་བ་དོན་གཉེར་གྱི་བློ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར། ཚུལ་འདི་ནི་ཤེས་སྒྲིབ་བཟུང་འཛིན་གྱི་རྟོགས་པ་བརྒྱ་རྩ་བརྒྱད་སྤངས་པ་སོགས་ཡོན་ཏན་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་སོགས་པའམ་སྡུད་པར་བྱེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་ངོ་མཚར་རྨད་དུ་བྱུང་སྟེ། དེ་ཡང་གང་ཞེ་ན། བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་གནས་ནས་དེ་དག་ལ་བདེན་པར་གྲུབ་པའི་མཚན་མ་ཅུང་ཟད་ཀྱང་མེད་པར་རྟོགས་ཤིང་། བསམས་གཟུགས་བརྒྱད་ཐོབ་པའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་དེ་ལ་གནས་པ་རྣམས་གལ་ཏེ་ལུས་ནི་ཞིག་པར་གྱུར་ཏེ་རྗེས་ནའང་། translation: The peak training of the path of meditation. To indicate the sixth, the peak training of the path of meditation, the Ornament states: "The nine meditative absorptions, along with the cessation... / ...the nine other aspects of discordant classes." Regarding this, there are three points. The first: the definition of the peak training of the path of meditation is that subsequent realization of the Great Vehicle which abides in the class of the actual antidote to the seeds of conceptualizations to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Second, if it is divided, there are the nine uninterrupted paths that are the actual antidotes to the nine cycles of conceptualizations to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and the nine cycles of paths of complete liberation of the path of meditation. Third, its limits are from the first ground up to the tenth ground. To explain such a peak training of the path of meditation, three verses beginning with "Possessing great power" are stated. Moreover, to indicate the two conceptualizations of grasping at an object out of the four conceptualizations of grasped and grasper that are to be abandoned: The bodhisattva on the path of meditation who is "possessing great power" of qualities, such as having abandoned the two conceptualizations of grasping at an object of the cognitive obscuration, abides by way of the four meditative absorptions of the actual dhyānas, and also familiarizes themselves with the leap-over samādhi; and at that time, they do not rely on them by way of clinging to the grasped object as true, nor do they abide by way of relishing the bliss of meditative absorption, because they directly realize the grasped object as being without truth. However, these four actual dhyānas and meditative absorptions along with their branches, such as the samādhi, joy, and bliss of the first, become the support for attaining the qualities of abandonment and realization of supreme, unsurpassed holy awakening, because all paths of seeing and meditation rely on the actual dhyānas. Although Buddhaśrī applies what is from here onwards to the uninterrupted peak training, according to the Master Haribhadra, the method of accomplishing the welfare of others by having abandoned the two conceptualizations of grasping at a grasper of the cognitive obscuration, familiarizing oneself with limitless samādhis, and taking various births is as follows: The bodhisattva who has attained the supreme perfection of wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, and who abides in the four dhyānas of the path of meditation, enters into and experiences the meditative absorptions of the four holy formless samādhis and the meditative absorption of cessation and so forth, yet does not cling to them as true. Because these formless dhyānas are favorable conditions for higher knowledges and miraculous powers and so forth, they become conditions that benefit the attainment of the supreme state of a holy awakened Buddha; therefore they train in them, but that bodhisattva does not train in order to abide in the bliss of peace after afflictions or defilements are exhausted, like the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, because they do not have the mind that seeks peace for their own welfare. This method is the wonderful and marvelous quality of the bodhisattvas who gather or possess limitless qualities, such as having abandoned the one hundred and eight conceptualizations of grasped and grasper of the cognitive obscuration. And what is that? Having abided in samādhis such as the four dhyānas, they realize them to be without even the slightest mark of being truly established; and for those abiding on that path of meditation who have attained the eight dhyānas and formless absorptions, even after their bodies have perished, because the dhyāna branches of the meditative absorptions that are the causes are completely exhausted, by that power they do not take birth in the upper realms, but take birth even in the desire realm for the welfare of others, such as ripening sentient beings, just according to their own desire or intention.

Because merely meditating on emptiness in meditative equipoise is not sufficient, but one must also become familiar with the forward and reverse progressions of the twelve links of dependent arising during the subsequent attainment, explaining this very method: The meaning of what is stated in the three verses starting with "Lower sentient beings" is: The Sugatas have taught that in the world, in relation to body and resources, all the classes of sentient beings, however many there are—the lower sentient beings, those of the lower realms; the middling, humans and so forth; and the supreme, gods—do not arise from a Principal, a Lord, permanent Time, and so forth, but arise from the ignorance of self-grasping; by the power of the ignorance of grasping at a personal self, which is the contradictory and discordant class to awareness and pristine wisdom, karma is accumulated, and when conditions assemble, such as being nourished by craving, grasping, and so forth, which are the cooperative conditions of karma, the projected results of birth, aging, sickness, death, and so forth are established, and this great mechanism of the suffering of saṃsāra, such as the completely afflicted twelve links of dependent arising, genuinely arises again and again; yet, even so, that mechanism of ignorance in the continuums of sentient beings is not exhausted by the arising of results, nor does it increase, but remains just as it is.

།དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་གང་ཞིག་འཁོར་འདས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཐ་སྙད་དུ་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བ་འདི་ལ་རིགས་པས་དཔྱད་ཅིང་བཙལ་ན་ཅུང་ཟད་ཀྱང་རྙེད་པ་མེད་པས་རང་གི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དང་ཟད་པ་སྟེ་འགག་པ་མེད་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ཟབ་མོ་འདི་ལྟ་བུ་ཤེས་པ་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གསུང་གི་མཛོད་ཀྱི་གཅེས་པ་ཟབ་མོར་ཁེང་དུ་ཆུད་ཅིང་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་མཐོང་བར་གསུངས་ཏེ། བཤེས་སྤྲིང་ལས། རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་འདི་རྒྱལ་བ་ཡི། །གསུང་གི་མཛོད་ཀྱི་གཅེས་པ་ཟབ་མོ་སྟེ། །གང་གིས་འདི་ནི་ཡང་དག་མཐོང་བ་དེས། །སངསརྒྱས་དེ་ཉིད་རིག་པ་རྣམ་མཆོག་མཐོང་། །ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་ལྟར་གནས་ལུགས་ཟབ་མོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་དོན་ཤེས་ཤིང་གོམས་པར་བྱས་ཏེ་ཐོང་རྒལ་གྱི་སྙོམ་འཇུག་ལ་སོགས་པ་སྒོམ་པའི་ལམ་ལ་གནས་པར་བྱས་པས་དཔེར་ན་ཉི་མ་མེད་ཅིང་འོད་ཟེར་རབ་ཏུ་འཕྲོ་བས་མུན་པ་མ་ལུས་པ་བསལ་བ་ལྟར་དུ་མ་རིག་པ་བག་ཆགས་དང་བཅས་པའི་སྒྲིབ་པའི་མུན་པ་ཐིབས་པོ་མ་ལུས་པ་བཅོམ་ནས་རང་བྱུང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་མཆོག་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ་དགེ་སློང་བརྒྱ་ཕྲག་དྲུག་ཅུ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་མེ་ཏོག་བཀྲམ་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་འགྱུར་པར་ལུང་བསྟན་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །ཡོན་ཏན་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་སྡུད་པ་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པའི་འགྲེལ་བ་ཟབ་མ་ོརྟེན་འབྱུང་གི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་གསལ་བར་བྱེད་པའི་ནོར་བུའི་སྒྲོན་མེ་སྐལ་བཟང་རེ་སྐོང་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལས་མེ་ཏོག་བཀྲམ་པའི་ལེའུ་སྟེ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད་པའི་འགྲེལ་བའོ།།    །།
[3-295] translation already produced for this document:
The pristine wisdom of the Buddha, the path of meditation that accords with its mode, its point of entry, the path of seeing, the method for generating it, the path of preparation, and its root, the path of accumulation—however many there are, all of these arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom that realizes selflessness. Because one repeatedly familiarizes oneself with that very pristine wisdom that realizes selflessness and accumulates a vast collection of merit, ignorance ceases, and because one does not accumulate karma that projects saṃsāra, the mechanism of suffering does not arise. By being taught by a spiritual friend, conditions of method such as meditating on love and compassion assemble, and the mechanism of pristine wisdom, such as the ten grounds and five paths of the Great Vehicle, genuinely arises, and its root, the perfection of wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, is never exhausted, nor does it increase in the ultimate sense, but abides conventionally as dependent arising, like a magical illusion. Thus, it is said in the Gaganagañjaparipṛcchā Sūtra: "If one genuinely knows all dharmas / That arise in dependence upon causes, / That treasury is inexhaustible; / The treasury of dharma is inconceivable. / The protector of the world has genuinely taught / That these four dharmas are inexhaustible: / Sentient beings, space, bodhicitta, / And likewise, the qualities of a Buddha. / If they were substantial, / They would become completely exhausted. / Because they are non-existent, they are called 'inexhaustible'; / Therefore they are taught as inexhaustible." Therefore, it is said that whichever bodhisattva knows this profound meaning of the perfection of wisdom—that all dharmas of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa conventionally arise in dependence, and if one investigates and searches for them with reasoning, not even the slightest bit is found, so one completely knows that they are without arising by their own intrinsic nature, and without exhaustion, that is, without cessation—penetrates the profound precious treasury of the Buddha's speech and sees the dharmakāya. As it is said in the Suhṛllekha: "This dependent arising is the profound, / Precious treasury of the Victor's speech. / Whoever genuinely sees this / Sees the Buddha, the supreme knower of suchness." Thus, by knowing the meaning of the profound abiding nature, emptiness, familiarizing oneself with it, and abiding on the path of meditation, such as the meditative absorption of leap-over, just as, for example, the sun, being without conceptuality and radiating light, dispels darkness without exception, so too, having destroyed the thick darkness of the obscurations of ignorance along with its latent tendencies without exception, one will attain the supreme pristine wisdom of a spontaneously arisen Buddha, just as it was prophesied that the six hundred monks will become Tathāgatas named Avakīrṇakusuma. This is the commentary on the twenty-eighth chapter, the Chapter of Avakīrṇakusuma, from The Fulfiller of the Hopes of the Fortunate: A Jeweled Lamp Illuminating the Suchness of Profound Dependent Arising, a Commentary on the Verses of the Precious Qualities Collection.

heading: **བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར།**
source: བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར། བདུན་པ་བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱར་ནི།རྒྱན་ལས། སྟོང་གསུམ་སྐྱོ་བོ་ཉན་ཐོས་དང༌། །ནས། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན། །ཞེས་གསུངས། འདི་ལ་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་བ། ས་མཚམས་གསུམ། དང་པོ་ནི། མཁྱེན་གསུམ་བསྡུས་བསྒོམ་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ལས་རབ་ཏུ་གྱུར་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མཐར་ཐུག་གང་ཞིག །རང་གི་འབྲས་བུར་གྱུར་པའི་རྣམ་མཁྱེན་དངོས་སུ་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་དེ། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་རྒྱུན་མཐའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །གཉིས་པ་དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། སྐད་ཅིག་སྦྱོར་བཞི་ཡོད། གསུམ་པ་ས་མཚམས་རྒྱུན་མཐའ་ཁོ་ནར་ཡོད། ཆུ་ཡི་པདྨ་བཞིན་སྲིད་པར་གནས་ཀྱང་སྲིད་པའི་སྐྱོན་གྱིས་མ་གོས་པའི་བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་འཆད་པར། དཔེར་ན། འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་གི་མི་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་ལྷ་ཡི་ཡུལ་གྱི་གནས་དང་ལྷ་ཡི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་ལྟ་ན་སྡུག་པ་སོགས་ཕན་སུམ་ཚོགས་ཤིང་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་དེར་མ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་ཕྱིས་ཞིག་ན་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ལ་སོགས་པས་སོང་སྟེ་དེ་ན་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་བའི་ཁང་བཟང་སྐྱེད་མོའི་ཚལ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཡུལ་ཡིད་དུ་འོང་བ་དེ་རྣམས་མཐོང་ནས་དེ་དག་ལ་མ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིས་འཛམ་གླིང་འདིར་འོང་བར་གྱུར་ན་དེ་རང་གི་ཡུལ་དང་ཁང་ཁྱིམ་སོགས་ལ་སྐྱུག་ལོག་ཅིང་ཡིད་མི་འོངས་པར་མཐོང་ནས་ཆགས་པ་མི་བྱེད་པར་ལྟར། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྒོས་པའི་ལམ་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་གཞི་དང་རྟེན་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་བདེན་མེད་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དང་བྱམས་སྙིང་རྗེ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འཆད་པ། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ལ་བརྩོན་ཏེ་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་རྣམ་མཐར་བརྒྱད་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་གནས་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་རབ་ཕུལ་དུ་བྱུང་བ་མཐོང་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དང་དགའ་བདེ་ལ་མི་ཞེན་ཅིང་དེས་དབང་གིས་སྐྱེ་བ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་ཞེས་པ་ཁམས་འོག་མ་གཅིག་པུ་མ་ཡིན་པར་རང་གར་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་གནས་ཏེ། ཁམས་གསུམ་གྱི་ཆོས་གང་ལའང་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དེ་འཁོར་བར་གནས་ཀྱང་འཁོར་བའི་སྐྱོན་གྱིས་མ་གོས་པར་དཔེར་ན་ཆུ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པ་ཡི་པདྨ་ཆུས་མ་གོས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱིས་པའི་ཆོས་ལ་མི་གནས་སོ། །ཞེས་པའོ། །
translation: The uninterrupted peak training. To indicate the seventh, the uninterrupted peak training, the Ornament states: "The Śrāvakas in the trichiliocosm... / ...the uninterrupted samādhi." Regarding this, there are three points: the definition, the divisions, and the limits. The first: the definition of the uninterrupted peak training is that ultimate yoga of a bodhisattva—held by wisdom that is superior to the path of accumulation of the Great Vehicle which meditates upon the three knowledges in a condensed manner—that actually produces the omniscient knowledge that becomes its own result. It is synonymous with the knowledge at the end of the continuum. Second, if it is divided, there are the four momentary trainings. Third, its limit is exclusively at the end of the continuum. To explain the uninterrupted peak training wherein they abide in existence but are not tainted by the flaws of existence, like a lotus in water: For example, if a person from Jambudvīpa who had never before gone to a place in the realm of the gods or the divine city of Sudarśana and so forth which are perfect and supreme, later went there by miraculous powers and so forth, and having seen the pleasing objects such as the palaces and pleasure groves completely held by the gods there, was not attached to them and later came back to this Jambudvīpa, they would become nauseated by their own objects and houses and so forth, see them as unpleasing, and not develop attachment. In the same way as that example, to explain the wisdom that realizes truthlessness and the love, compassion, and so forth of a bodhisattva which become the supreme basis and support for the qualities of the path of meditation: Making effort in the yoga of the uninterrupted samādhi, having abided in samādhis such as the four dhyānas and the eight liberations, they see the supreme, excellent qualities of a Buddha, and therefore do not cling to the samādhis and the joy and bliss of the dhyānas and formless realms, and having abandoned birth by the power of that, they "again" abide "in the desire realm"—meaning not just the single lower realm, but rather they abide wherever they wish in the desire realm, and they have no attachment to any phenomena of the three realms; therefore, although they abide in saṃsāra, they are not tainted by the flaws of saṃsāra—just as a lotus born from water is not tainted by water, they do not abide in childish phenomena.

སྒོམ་སྤངས་རྟོགས་བའི་ས་བོན་གྱི་དངོས་གཉེན་གྱི་རིགས་སུ་གནས་པའི་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་རྗེས་ལ་མངོན་རྟོགས་དེ། སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཉིས་པ་དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། སྒོམ་སྤངས་རྣམ་རྟོག་བསྐོར་དགུའི་དངོས་གཉེན་བར་ཆད་མེད་ལམ་དགུ་དང་། སྒོམ་ལམ་རྣམ་འགྲོལ་ལམ་བསྐོར་དགུ་ཡོད། གསུམ་པ་ས་མཚམས་དང་པོ་ནས་ས་བཅུ་པའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་སྒོམ་ལམ་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་འཆད་པར། མཐུ་ཆེན་ལྡན་པ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་གསུམ་གསུངས། དེ་ཡང་སྤངས་བྱ་བཟུང་འཛིན་གྱི་རྟོག་པ་བཞི་ལས་བཟུང་རྟོག་གཉིས་སྟོན་པར། The peak training of the path of meditation. To indicate the sixth, the peak training of the path of meditation, the Ornament states: "The nine meditative absorptions, along with the cessation... / ...the nine other aspects of discordant classes." Regarding this, there are three points. The first: the definition of the peak training of the path of meditation is that subsequent realization of the Great Vehicle which abides in the class of the actual antidote to the seeds of conceptualizations to be abandoned by the path of meditation. Second, if it is divided, there are the nine uninterrupted paths that are the actual antidotes to the nine cycles of conceptualizations to be abandoned by the path of meditation, and the nine cycles of paths of complete liberation of the path of meditation. Third, its limits are from the first ground up to the tenth ground. To explain such a peak training of the path of meditation, three verses beginning with "Possessing great power" are stated. Moreover, to indicate the two conceptualizations of grasping at an object out of the four conceptualizations of grasped and grasper that are to be abandoned: The bodhisattva on the path of meditation who is "possessing great power" of qualities, such as having abandoned the two conceptualizations of grasping at an object of the cognitive obscuration, abides by way of the four meditative absorptions of the actual dhyānas, and also familiarizes themselves with the leap-over samādhi; and at that time, they do not rely on them by way of clinging to the grasped object as true, nor do they abide by way of relishing the bliss of meditative absorption, because they directly realize the grasped object as being without truth. However, these four actual dhyānas and meditative absorptions along with their branches, such as the samādhi, joy, and bliss of the first, become the support for attaining the qualities of abandonment and realization of supreme, unsurpassed holy awakening, because all paths of seeing and meditation rely on the actual dhyānas. Although Buddhaśrī applies what is from here onwards to the uninterrupted peak training, according to the Master Haribhadra, the method of accomplishing the welfare of others by having abandoned the two conceptualizations of grasping at a grasper of the cognitive obscuration, familiarizing oneself with limitless samādhis, and taking various births is as follows: The bodhisattva who has attained the supreme perfection of wisdom that realizes the abiding nature, and who abides in the four dhyānas of the path of meditation, enters into and experiences the meditative absorptions of the four holy formless samādhis and the meditative absorption of cessation and so forth, yet does not cling to them as true. Because these formless dhyānas are favorable conditions for higher knowledges and miraculous powers and so forth, they become conditions that benefit the attainment of the supreme state of a holy awakened Buddha; therefore they train in them, but that bodhisattva does not train in order to abide in the bliss of peace after afflictions or defilements are exhausted, like the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, because they do not have the mind that seeks peace for their own welfare. This method is the wonderful and marvelous quality of the bodhisattvas who gather or possess limitless qualities, such as having abandoned the one hundred and eight conceptualizations of grasped and grasper of the cognitive obscuration. And what is that? Having abided in samādhis such as the four dhyānas, they realize them to be without even the slightest mark of being truly established; and for those abiding on that path of meditation who have attained the eight dhyānas and formless absorptions, even after their bodies have perished, because the dhyāna branches of the meditative absorptions that are the causes are completely exhausted, by that power they do not take birth in the upper realms, but take birth even in the desire realm for the welfare of others, such as ripening sentient beings, just according to their own desire or intention.

heading: **བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར།**
source: བརྒྱད་པ་བསལ་བྱ་ལོག་སྒྲུབ་སྟོན་པར་རྒྱན་ལས། དམིགས་པ་འཐད་དང་དེ་ཡི་ནི། །ནས། །རྣམ་པ་བཅུ་དྲུག་དག་ཏུ་བཞེད། །ཅེས་གསུངས། འདི་ལ་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱི་བ། ས་མཚམས་གསུམ། དང་པོ་ནི། འདིར་བསྟན་བདེན་གཉིས་ངོ་བོ་གཅིག་ལ་འདུར་མི་རུང་བར་འཛིན་པའི་ས་བོན་དང་མངོན་འགྱུར་པ་ཅི་རིགས་པས་བསྡུས་པ་དེ། འདིར་བསྟན་བསལ་བྱ་ལོག་སྒྲུབ་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། གཉིས་པ་དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། དམིགས་པ་འཐད་པ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པར། དམིགས་པའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ངེས་པར་བཟུང་བ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པར། རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། བདེན་པ་གཉིས་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། སྦྱོར་བ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། ཐབས་མཁས་པ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། ཐུབ་པའི་མངོན་རྟོགས་པ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། ལམ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། མི་མཐུན་ཕྱོགས་དང་གཉེན་པོ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། ཆོས་ཀྱི་མཚན་ཉིད་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ། སྒོམ་པ་ལ་ལོག་པར་རྟོག་པ་དང་བཅུ་དྲུག་ཡོད།གསུམ་པ་ས་མཚམས་ལམ་མ་ཞུགས་ནས་ས་བདུན་པའི་བར་དུ་ཡོད། གསལ་བྱ་ལོག་སྒྲུབ་དེ་ཉིད་བུདྡྷ་ཤྲཱི་ལྟར་ན་གོང་གི་འདི་ནི་ཡོན་ཏན་སོགས་པའི་ངོ་མཚར་རྨད་དུ་བྱུང་སྟེ། ཞེས་པ་ནས་བསྟན་པར་བཞེད་ཀྱང་། རང་ལུགས་སློབ་དཔོན་གྱི་བཞེད་པ་ལྟར། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པ་ཞེས་སོགས་ཚིགས་བཅད་ལྔ་གསུངས། དེའང་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེན་པར་མེད་ན་དམིགས་པ་དང་། དོན་གཉེར་བླངས་དོར་སོགས་ཇི་ལྟར་འཐད་སྙམ་དུ་ལོག་པར་ཞུགས་པས་དེས་གཉེན་པོ་འཁོར་གསུམ་གང་དུའང་ཆགས་པའམ་ཞེན་པ་མེད་པར་དོན་གཉིས་རྫོགས་པར་བྱེད་ཚུལ་ནི། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་བསམ་གཟུགས་བརྒྱད་ཐོབ་ཀྱང་དེ་དག་ལ་མངོན་ཞེན་མེད་ཅིང་གཟུགས་མེད་སོགས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་མི་ལེན་བར་འདོད་ཁམས་སོགས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་བཟུང་བའི་དགོས་པ་ཡང༌། བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་དེས་ཆོས་བསྟན་པ་སོགས་སྒོ་ནས་སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པར་བྱ་བ་དང༌། རང་ཉིད་གང་དུ་འཚང་རྒྱ་འགྱུར་གྱི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་སྦྱང་བ་དང་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྣམས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པ་སོགས་གཞན་དོན་བྱེད་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཟད་དེ་དགོས་པ་གཞན་མེད་དོ། །དེའི་ཕྱིར་གཟུགས་མེད་ཁམས་ན་ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་དང༌། སྦྱིན་ཡུལ་སོགས་མེད་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་བསྐྱེད་པའི་སྦྱིན་སོགས་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་ཉམས་ལེན་དང་གཞན་དོན་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་འགྲུབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་ངོ་ཞེས་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཁམས་སུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེས་སྐྱེ་བ་དོན་དུ་གཉེར་ནས་བླང་བར་མི་བྱེད་དོ། །
translation: The eighth, the mistaken practices that are the objects to be eliminated. To indicate this, the Ornament states: "The tenability of the object of focus, and its... / ...are asserted as the sixteen aspects." Regarding this, there are three points: the definition, the divisions, and the limits. The first: the definition of the mistaken practice that is the object to be eliminated taught here is that which is subsumed by either the seeds or the manifest forms, whichever is appropriate, of apprehending that the two truths cannot be combined into a single essence. Second, if it is divided: mistaken conceptualization regarding the tenability of the object of focus, mistaken conceptualization regarding definitely apprehending the nature of the object of focus, mistaken conceptualization regarding the knowledge of omniscience, mistaken conceptualization regarding the two truths, mistaken conceptualization regarding the training, mistaken conceptualization regarding the Three Jewels, mistaken conceptualization regarding skill in means, mistaken conceptualization regarding the realization of the Muni, mistaken conceptualization regarding the perverted, mistaken conceptualization regarding the path, mistaken conceptualization regarding the discordant class and the antidote, mistaken conceptualization regarding the definition of phenomena, and mistaken conceptualization regarding meditation—there are sixteen. Third, its limit is from before entering the path up to the seventh ground. According to Buddhaśrī, the mistaken practices that are the objects to be eliminated themselves are asserted to be taught from the earlier line, "These are the marvellous qualities, etc." However, according to our own system, following the assertion of the Master, the five verses starting with "The great beings..." are spoken. Moreover, the way in which they perfectly accomplish the two aims without being attached or clinging to any of the three spheres, as an antidote to those who mistakenly engage by thinking, "If all phenomena lack true existence, how could objects of focus, and adopting and discarding what is sought after, and so forth, be tenable?", is this: Although that bodhisattva attains the eight dhyānas and formless realms, they have no manifest clinging to them, and without taking birth in the formless realms and so forth, the purpose for taking birth in the desire realm and so forth is solely to accomplish the aims of others—for those "great beings" to completely mature sentient beings through teaching the Dharma and so forth, to purify the buddhafield where they themselves will become a buddha, and to completely perfect the perfections and so forth—there is no other purpose. Therefore, because there is no teaching of the Dharma, objects of giving, and so forth in the formless realm, thinking, "The practice of the perfections such as giving which generate the qualities of awakening and the vast accomplishment of the aims of others would degenerate," that bodhisattva does not seek out and take "birth in the formless realm."

བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར། བདུན་པ་བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱར་ནི།རྒྱན་ལས། སྟོང་གསུམ་སྐྱོ་བོ་ཉན་ཐོས་དང༌། །ནས། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན། །ཞེས་གསུངས། འདི་ལ་མཚན་ཉིད། དབྱེ་བ། ས་མཚམས་གསུམ། དང་པོ་ནི། མཁྱེན་གསུམ་བསྡུས་བསྒོམ་ཐེག་ཆེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་ལམ་ལས་རབ་ཏུ་གྱུར་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པའི་སེམས་དཔའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་མཐར་ཐུག་གང་ཞིག །རང་གི་འབྲས་བུར་གྱུར་པའི་རྣམ་མཁྱེན་དངོས་སུ་སྐྱེད་བྱེད་དེ། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་གྱི་མཚན་ཉིད། དེ་དང་རྒྱུན་མཐའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དོན་གཅིག །གཉིས་པ་དེ་ལ་དབྱེ་ན། སྐད་ཅིག་སྦྱོར་བཞི་ཡོད། གསུམ་པ་ས་མཚམས་རྒྱུན་མཐའ་ཁོ་ནར་ཡོད། ཆུ་ཡི་པདྨ་བཞིན་སྲིད་པར་གནས་ཀྱང་སྲིད་པའི་སྐྱོན་གྱིས་མ་གོས་པའི་བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར་འཆད་པར། དཔེར་ན། འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང་གི་མི་ཞིག་སྔོན་ཆད་ལྷ་ཡི་ཡུལ་གྱི་གནས་དང་ལྷ་ཡི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་ལྟ་ན་སྡུག་པ་སོགས་ཕན་སུམ་ཚོགས་ཤིང་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་དེར་མ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་ཕྱིས་ཞིག་ན་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་ལ་སོགས་པས་སོང་སྟེ་དེ་ན་ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་བའི་ཁང་བཟང་སྐྱེད་མོའི་ཚལ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཡུལ་ཡིད་དུ་འོང་བ་དེ་རྣམས་མཐོང་ནས་དེ་དག་ལ་མ་ཆགས་པའི་ཕྱིས་འཛམ་གླིང་འདིར་འོང་བར་གྱུར་ན་དེ་རང་གི་ཡུལ་དང་ཁང་ཁྱིམ་སོགས་ལ་སྐྱུག་ལོག་ཅིང་ཡིད་མི་འོངས་པར་མཐོང་ནས་ཆགས་པ་མི་བྱེད་པར་ལྟར། དཔེ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སྒོས་པའི་ལམ་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་གཞི་དང་རྟེན་མཆོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་བདེན་མེད་རྟོགས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་དང་བྱམས་སྙིང་རྗེ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འཆད་པ། བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་ལ་བརྩོན་ཏེ་བསམ་གཏན་བཞི་དང་རྣམ་མཐར་བརྒྱད་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ལ་གནས་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་རབ་ཕུལ་དུ་བྱུང་བ་མཐོང་པས་བསམ་གཏན་གཟུགས་མེད་ཀྱི་ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་དང་དགའ་བདེ་ལ་མི་ཞེན་ཅིང་དེས་དབང་གིས་སྐྱེ་བ་སྤངས་ཏེ་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་ཞེས་པ་ཁམས་འོག་མ་གཅིག་པུ་མ་ཡིན་པར་རང་གར་འདོད་པའི་ཁམས་སུ་གནས་ཏེ། ཁམས་གསུམ་གྱི་ཆོས་གང་ལའང་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དེ་འཁོར་བར་གནས་ཀྱང་འཁོར་བའི་སྐྱོན་གྱིས་མ་གོས་པར་དཔེར་ན་ཆུ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པ་ཡི་པདྨ་ཆུས་མ་གོས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱིས་པའི་ཆོས་ལ་མི་གནས་སོ། །ཞེས་པའོ། །

The uninterrupted peak training. To indicate the seventh, the uninterrupted peak training, the Ornament states: "The Śrāvakas in the trichiliocosm... / ...the uninterrupted samādhi." Regarding this, there are three points: the definition, the divisions, and the limits. The first: the definition of the uninterrupted peak training is that ultimate yoga of a bodhisattva—held by wisdom that is superior to the path of accumulation of the Great Vehicle which meditates upon the three knowledges in a condensed manner—that actually produces the omniscient knowledge that becomes its own result. It is synonymous with the knowledge at the end of the continuum. Second, if it is divided, there are the four momentary trainings. Third, its limit is exclusively at the end of the continuum. To explain the uninterrupted peak training wherein they abide in existence but are not tainted by the flaws of existence, like a lotus in water: For example, if a person from Jambudvīpa who had never before gone to a place in the realm of the gods or the divine city of Sudarśana and so forth which are perfect and supreme, later went there by miraculous powers and so forth, and having seen the pleasing objects such as the palaces and pleasure groves completely held by the gods there, was not attached to them and later came back to this Jambudvīpa, they would become nauseated by their own objects and houses and so forth, see them as unpleasing, and not develop attachment. In the same way as that example, to explain the wisdom that realizes truthlessness and the love, compassion, and so forth of a bodhisattva which become the supreme basis and support for the qualities of the path of meditation: Making effort in the yoga of the uninterrupted samādhi, having abided in samādhis such as the four dhyānas and the eight liberations, they see the supreme, excellent qualities of a Buddha, and therefore do not cling to the samādhis and the joy and bliss of the dhyānas and formless realms, and having abandoned birth by the power of that, they "again" abide "in the desire realm"—meaning not just the single lower realm, but rather they abide wherever they wish in the desire realm, and they have no attachment to any phenomena of the three realms; therefore, although they abide in saṃsāra, they are not tainted by the flaws of saṃsāra—just as a lotus born from water is not tainted by water, they do not abide in childish phenomena.

heading: **བར་ཆད་མེད་པའི་རྩེ་སྦྱོར།**
translation: The manner of this is, for example, if a person were to find treasures made of jewels, but at that time there were enemies or they would be wasted, they would not develop the mind of being attached to them or desiring to take them, and they would not take them; but later, when there are no enemies, by the power of necessity at another time that person would fully take those great treasures for the sake of others, and having taken them, would go to their own home and, without being attached to them, would give them away to relatives and friends, and so forth. In the same way, bodhisattvas who are skilled in the nature of the two truths, who bestow temporary joy and ultimate bliss upon sentient beings, having attained the four samādhis subsumed by the main practices of the dhyānas which are pacified of the flaws of dullness and agitation, have no attachment or manifest clinging to possessing the bliss of the dhyānas, and letting go of the attained samādhis of the dhyānas that produce results, those who possess affection for all wandering sentient beings as if they were their only child proceed to take birth "again" in the desire realm for the sake of others, because the immeasurable aims of others will be accomplished.
